279	### 2026-05-21 — Perf-log producer-side module landed
280	
281	Built the perf-log subsystem end-to-end on the producer side, including the real USB-device CDC ACM sink. Producers are not yet wired (module is dark beyond a SESSION + 1 Hz DROP heartbeat), but the wire path is live: a `PERF_REC_SESSION` is re-emitted on every host DTR-rising edge, so reconnecting a terminal mid-session always sees the schema record.
282	
283	**What landed under [`firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/`](../default/src/perf_log/):**
284	- `perf_log_records.h` — wire format, schema version 1. 16 B common header (`magic` 0x4D56 'MV', `type`, `flags`, `frame_epoch`, `ts_counter`). Record types: SESSION, STAMP, DETECTOR, TIMING, PATCH, DROP, TASK_HIGHWATER. Stage IDs cover ISC_IRQ, VIDEO_PUBLISH, CV_START, CV_END, TP_TICK, FBL_SEND, CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE.
285	- `perf_log.{h,c}` — façade with separate task / `*FromISR` entry points (mirrors `xQueueSend` / `xQueueSendFromISR`). Two queues sized for the 30× small/large record-size ratio: state queue (slot = 40 B largest small record, depth 128) and patch queue (slot = `sizeof(perf_rec_patch_t)` = 814 B, depth 8). Drop-on-full, never block. Per-queue + sink drop counters RMW under `taskENTER_CRITICAL` / `taskENTER_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR` (the XC32 ARM926 port doesn't link libatomic; GCC's `__atomic_add_fetch` falls through to a libcall and won't link). Drain task at `tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 2` (above idle, below detector/timing) with 2 KB stack; emits one `PERF_REC_DROP` per second.
286	- `perf_log_sink.h` + `perf_log_sink_cdc.c` — sink interface and USB-device CDC ACM implementation. CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over `LEN || PAYLOAD`; framing is `0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56 || u16 LEN || PAYLOAD || u16 CRC`. MCC now ships USB-device + USB-device-CDC class config (UDPHS); the sink owns the application side: opens `USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0`, registers the device-layer event handler (Attach on POWER_DETECTED, register CDC handler on CONFIGURED), and exposes a blocking `WriteFramed`. CDC class events handle GET/SET line coding, control-line state (DTR latched into `s_cls`), and signal `WRITE_COMPLETE` via `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` on a binary semaphore. Single producer (the drain task); writes are serialized one at a time on a single cache-aligned 832 B staging buffer (header + max patch payload + CRC). DTR-gated: if the host hasn't asserted DTR, frames are dropped into `s_drop_sink`. Write timeout (100 ms) drops + accumulates and the next state-machine pass observes DECONFIGURED if the host went away.
287	+ Cold-boot-with-cable required an explicit `Detach → 100 ms → Attach` edge after handler registration; relying on the driver's natural VBUS-edge `POWER_DETECTED` event to fire after-the-fact didn't enumerate (suspected: host gave up retrying after observing transient pull-up state during early boot, or the UDPHS driver's `vbusLevel` tracking races with handler-registration timing). The forced edge gives the host an unambiguous device-arrival regardless.
288	- μs timestamps via `SYS_TIME_CounterGet()` (TC0 CH0 raw counter) — host divides by `timer_freq_hz` from the SESSION record. Explicitly *not* the `xTaskGetTickCount() * (1000000 / configTICK_RATE_HZ)` pattern at [cv_marvin_v1.c:156](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L156); that's ms-resolution masquerading as μs and is useless for sub-frame attribution.
289	
290	**Wired into [`app.c`](../default/src/app.c):** `PerfLog_Initialize()` after `Video_Initialize()` (queues exist before any producer can post); `PerfLog_Start()` at the end of `APP_Initialize` (creates the drain task; Harmony brings the scheduler up after `APP_Initialize` returns, so this is the standard "create static tasks before `vTaskStartScheduler`" pattern). `cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` updated.
291	
292	**Producers not yet wired** — module is dark today. Next steps land them in this order: (1) ISR producers (`video.c` ISC_IRQ + VIDEO_PUBLISH; `fretboard_link.c` CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE — *no* `LOG_INFO` from this ISR per the 2026-05-20/21 freeze pattern); (2) task producers in `cv_marvin_v1`, `timing_pipeline`, `fretboard_link.FretboardLink_Send`. Replaces the commented-out 2 Hz dump at [`cv_marvin_v1.c:336-351`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L336-L351). `PERF_REC_PATCH` emission slots in last (Tier 2 — reuses already-sampled 5×5 patches, no new I/O).
293	
294	### 2026-05-21 — Perf-logging bandwidth/capacity scoping
295	
296	Crunched numbers ahead of designing a frame-by-frame perf log (video + detector + actuator state) so we know which resolutions and which transports are actually in scope. Detail below; takeaway is that the spec's already-chosen "sparse keyframes + dense state" point (~1 MB/s) is the only real sweet spot, and the "full-rate raw video" wish is dead on arrival across every transport SAM9X75 has.
297	
298	**Baseline — 720×480 RGB888 (BGR888-packed in our pipeline) @ 60 Hz**
299	
300	- Per frame: 720 × 480 × 3 = **1.04 MB**.
301	- Per second: **62.2 MB/s ≈ 498 Mb/s**.
302	- All state payload (detector_state_t × 2 detectors + actuator + timing snapshot + per-frame metadata header) is ~150 B/frame ≈ **9 KB/s** — rounding error against pixels. This is a video-bandwidth problem, not a state-volume problem.
303	
304	**Scaled-down variants (per-second bandwidth)**
305	
306	| Variant | B/s |
307	|---|---|
308	| Full 720×480 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 62.2 MB/s |
309	| Same @ 30 Hz | 31.1 MB/s |
310	| 720×480 RGB565 @ 60 Hz | 41.5 MB/s |
311	| 720×480 grayscale @ 60 Hz | 20.7 MB/s |
312	| 360×240 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 15.6 MB/s |
313	| 360×240 RGB888 @ 30 Hz | 7.78 MB/s |
314	| 180×120 RGB888 @ 30 Hz | 1.94 MB/s |
315	| Strike-line strip 720×80 @ 60 Hz | 10.4 MB/s |
316	| 5 ROI patches 32×32 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 922 KB/s |
317	| State-only (no pixels) @ 60 Hz | 9.1 KB/s |
318	
319	**Capacity over a session length**
320	
321	| Stream | 1 min | 5 min (song) | 10 min |
322	|---|---|---|---|
323	| Full @ 60 Hz | 3.73 GB | 18.7 GB | 37.3 GB |
324	| 360×240 @ 30 Hz | 467 MB | 2.33 GB | 4.67 GB |
325	| 1 keyframe/s + state (≈ spec §4.6) | 62 MB | 311 MB | 622 MB |
326	| ROI patches 60 Hz | 55 MB | 277 MB | 553 MB |
327	| State only | 547 KB | 2.7 MB | 5.5 MB |
328	
329	**Transport ceilings on this hardware** (sustained, realistic)
330	
331	| Channel | Sustained | Peripheral status |
332	|---|---|---|
333	| UART 115.2 kBd (console) | ~11 KB/s | in use (FLEXCOM4) |
334	| UART 921.6 kBd | ~92 KB/s | EDBG bridge cap |
335	| UART 3 Mbd (FLEXCOM max) | ~300 KB/s | unlikely through bridges |
336	| USB CDC ACM (HS device, class-stack overhead) | ~5–15 MB/s | device peripheral unused |
337	| USB Bulk (HS device, custom class) | ~30–40 MB/s | needs custom host-side reader |
338	| SDMMC Class-10 via FAT32 | ~5–10 MB/s | already planned for §4.6 keyframes |
339	| SDMMC UHS-I | ~25–50 MB/s | bus capable, FS overhead bites |
340	| GMAC Ethernet UDP | ~30–60 MB/s | GMAC unused |
341	| GMAC Ethernet TCP | ~10–20 MB/s | GMAC unused |
342	
343	**What fits where**
344	
345	- **State-only (9 KB/s)** fits everywhere including the console UART — no new transport needed if the goal is just "trace detector + timing + actuator decisions per frame."
346	- **ROI patches 60 Hz (~1 MB/s)** preserves everything cv_marvin_v1 actually samples; streams comfortably over USB CDC, fits an entire song on SD with room to spare.
347	- **1 keyframe/s + dense state (~1 MB/s)** is what spec §4.6 already commits to, fits any modern SD card, and survives over USB CDC or Ethernet.
348	- **Full 60 Hz (62 MB/s)** doesn't fit any transport sustained, *and* a 5-minute song at that rate is 18.7 GB — DOA.
349	
350	**Implication for what to build next.** The scoping confirms the spec's existing reference-data architecture is the right place to start; perf-logging is a *consumer* of the same infrastructure, not a separate path. Next step is to figure out which questions the perf log actually has to answer (latency attribution? frame-rate stability? detector confidence over time? actuator jitter?) and pick the minimum stream that answers them. State-only might already be enough for the latency/jitter questions; ROI patches are the cheapest way to get "did the detector see what I think it saw" replayability.
351	
352	### 2026-05-21 — cv_marvin_v1 threshold tuning + timing-pipeline tweaks
353	
354	First end-to-end gameplay test on hardware. Detector was firing roughly random presses at first; resolved by reading actual signal values rather than guessing.
355	
356	**Visibility added:**
357	- State-reactive overlay in `cv_marvin_v1.c` — position rings always; filled center dot when `s_pressed[i]` (white in the hold ring) or `s_edge_active[i]` (fret-color in the edge ring). Lets the user watch chatter live: stable note → steady dot for hold duration; strum window → flash on the edge dot.
358	- Periodic ~2 Hz log dump (`frame_count % 30 == 0`) showing per-fret `hold_dist / edge_dist / P E` flags.
359	
360	**Diagnosis (Easy mode, no real B/O presses):**
361	- Idle hold floor sits at 22–48 across all five frets, **not** the limited-range 16 floor `display_path.md` would suggest. Playfield-glow at the sample sites is well above the limited-range black point.
362	- Real-press hold spikes to 67–186, leaving a clean gap above the noise ceiling.
363	- Hold threshold 50 with release-frac 0.6 (release=30) was *below* the idle floor for Y and B → those frets latched permanently pressed and never released.
364	- Edge threshold 50 was at the peak of real-edge signal (40–53), almost never tripping. timing_pipeline only uses `pressed` today, so dead edges aren't the chatter source — but lowering edge threshold lets `s_edge_active` overlay flicker meaningfully again.
365	
366	**Settings landed (in `cv_marvin_v1.c`):**
367	- `CV_HOLD_THRESH`: 50 → **100** (after iterating 65 → 80 → 100; 100 cleanly above noise across all frets, real presses still spike to 150–186).
368	- `CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC`: 0.60 → **0.78** (release ≈ 78 — above the noise ceiling, comfortably below real-press floor).
369	- `CV_EDGE_THRESH`: 50 → **25** (gives the overlay an honest edge indicator without affecting pipeline behavior).
370	- Sample coords nudged 1 px on G/R/Y/B/O edges + B hold for slightly cleaner alignment.
371	
372	**Performance:** Expert-mode play is now quite good — clean note recognition, fret hold-through across consecutive same-fret notes confirmed by trace through `process_releases` (release suppressed when the next chord-commit's `note_q` entry already needs the bit, within `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS − TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS = 190 ms` of detector-release-to-detector-press).
373	
374	**Timing-pipeline tweaks** (Greg's hand-edits): `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS` 50→25, `TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS` 20→30, `TP_FIFO_CAP` 16→32.
375	
376	Open question added above: `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220 ms` is Expert-tuned; Easy/Medium/Hard may need different values because note travel time differs.
377	
378	### 2026-05-21 — Manual fretboard-control producer + timing-pipeline gate
379	
380	Stood up the actuator-side half of a basic on-device manual-control surface — primarily for game-menu navigation (start a song, advance menus, hit pause) where single-finger input is the natural shape. UI half waits on a Microchip Graphics Composer regen.
381	
382	What landed:
383	
384	- `actuator/manual_control.{h,c}` — second producer of `FretboardLink_Send`, alongside `timing_pipeline`. Internal state: `s_fret_mask` (bits 0..4) and `s_strum_mask` (bits 5..6). Public API: `Initialize / SetEnabled / IsEnabled / SetFret / SetStrum`. Both fret and strum are momentary — held while the UI button is down, cleared on release. `recompute_and_send` only calls `FretboardLink_Send` while enabled.
385	- `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool)` — output gate on `publish_mask`. Pipeline still advances internal state when gated, so the next `advance()` (≤ `TP_TICK_MS` = 5 ms) after re-enable republishes the right mask without a stale frame.
386	- `ManualControl_SetEnabled` ordering: enter manual mode = gate timing pipeline first, zero local state, send `0`, set enabled flag (so a stale pipeline frame can't race a manual zero on the wire); exit = clear enabled flag, zero state, send `0`, ungate pipeline.
387	- App init wires `ManualControl_Initialize()` after `TimingPipeline_Initialize()`. No Legato dependency at this stage.
388	- `cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` adds `manual_control.c` and `ui/manual_input.c`.
389	
390	UI half landed same session after Greg ran the Composer regen. Composer added 8 buttons to `Screen0` — `Screen0_Button_Manual_{Green,Red,Yellow,Blue,Orange,StrumDown,StrumUp,Enable}` — plus 15 extern `event_Screen0_Button_Manual_*` handler declarations the application must define. The binding shape came out simpler than the plan called for: `screenShow_Screen0` itself calls `setPressedEventCallback` / `setReleasedEventCallback` with those extern symbols, so the linker resolves them and **no `ManualInput_Bind()` walk is needed**. `ui/manual_input.c` is just the 15 function bodies forwarding to `ManualControl_SetFret / Strum / SetEnabled`. The originally planned `APP_Tasks` poll-loop for null widget pointers is moot — `APP_Tasks` keeps the existing `vTaskDelete(NULL)`.
391	
392	Strum buttons are momentary, not one-shot: holding the strum button keeps the fretboard's strum line asserted, which Guitar Hero / Rock Band menus interpret as auto-repeat scrolling — the primary use case for this surface. Gameplay-path strums still pulse correctly because they go through `timing_pipeline`, which has its own `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS` one-shot. The Enable button is `setToggleable(LE_TRUE)` with only `OnReleased`; both the widget and `ManualControl` default to off, so a simple `SetEnabled(!IsEnabled())` flip stays in sync without querying the widget's toggle state.
393	
394	Plan agent flagged two real blockers worth recording: (1) Legato's input pipeline routes each touch to one focus widget — multi-finger momentary chords aren't possible without a custom dispatcher, so the model is single-finger only; (2) the lazy widget-pointer init means any code that walks the `Screen0_*` pointers has to run post-`screenShow_Screen0` — moot here because Composer does the wiring itself, but still true for any future shim that needs to read or modify widget state.
395	
396	Decision-log entries above cover the producer-as-peer pattern, the Composer-driven UI choice, and the single-finger input model.
397	
398	**Bring-up over the wire.** Marvin enumerates the EDBG CDC and `FretboardLink_Send` round-trips cleanly through the queue, but the fretboard MCU's SERCOM1 wasn't receiving anything. Two real fixes:
399	
400	1. **EDBG bridge needs DTR raised.** The bridge holds its UART TX idle until the host asserts DTR. Added `USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_ControlLineStateSet` with `dtr=1, carrier=1` to `open_cdc()` after the existing `LineCodingSet(115200)`. Baud matters here — fretboard runs a real UART at 115200, not USB-CDC-ignored.
401	2. **Control-pipe completion handlers run from ISR context.** First instrumented attempt logged `LOG_INFO` directly from the new `SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE` / `SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE` event cases; system froze mid-print. Microchip's CDC stack dispatches *all* class events from ISR (the existing `WRITE_COMPLETE` case already uses `*FromISR` primitives — that was the precedent). `log_vprintf` takes a mutex with `portMAX_DELAY`, illegal from ISR. Stripped both the diagnostic logging and the latch infrastructure once the link was confirmed functional. Captured for the journal because it's a recurring shape: any new event-handler case in this stack must stay strictly ISR-safe.
402	
403	### 2026-05-20 — USB CDC host attach: EDBG composite enumerates, CDC class driver now binds
404	
405	Picked up where the prior session left off — VBUS not asserting, no device detected. Closed both halves.
406	
407	**VBUS.** MCC's `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` callback is wired in the host driver but the host stack never invokes it on this build. Asserted the two VBUS GPIOs (`VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_Set` / `VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_Set`) directly from `APP_Initialize` ahead of consumer init and `USB_HOST_BusEnable`. EDBG immediately enumerates.
408	
409	**Class-driver binding.** Enumeration succeeded but the CDC attach handler never fired. Added per-interface descriptor logging inside `F_USB_HOST_UpdateDeviceTask` to see what was actually being matched. Output revealed VID `0x03EB` PID `0x2175` — an EDBG composite with five interfaces: HID/CMSIS-DAP, CDC ACM IAD pair (comm + data), vendor, MSC. The IAD passed TPL match and got assigned to the CDC driver, but the CDC instance still flipped to `STATE_ERROR` without our app-level handler ever seeing the attach.
410	
411	Root cause was inside Microchip's CDC class driver: `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` (both single-interface and IAD paths) requires the comm interface to declare `bInterfaceProtocol == USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_AT_V250` (`0x01`). EDBG declares `0x00` (none) — functionally identical CDC ACM in practice; Linux/macOS accept either. The TPL/IAD pre-check passes (TPL wildcards subclass/protocol), the CDC driver gets the interface group, then immediately rejects it on the AT-V.250 check. The interrupt pipe never opens, the instance errors out, and the app-level listener stays silent.
412	
413	Fix: relaxed both checks to `(AT_V250 || NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. After the patch the FBL log shows `CDC device attached, handle opened` and `c=Y` heartbeat as expected. Logged as patch #7 in the MCC re-apply list.
414	
415	Also tested a hypothesis from the prior session that `USB_HOST_Initialize` had to run *after* the EHCI/OHCI driver inits. With the diagnostic logging in place, MCC's emitted order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well — the host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time. Backed out the hand-edit; one fewer re-apply patch to maintain. Decision-log entry above.
416	
417	Diagnostic instrumentation stripped at the end of the session: the per-interface descriptor dump and enumeration state-change logger in `usb_host.c`, and the periodic OHCI/EHCI register heartbeat in `fretboard_link.c`. What remains on disk: the two `usb_host_cdc.c` protocol-relaxation lines (patch #7), the app-level VBUS asserts, and a minimal `USB_HOST_EVENT` printf so future host-stack drama still surfaces in the log.
418	
419	Next session: revisit timing-pipeline behavior end-to-end now that the actuator wire is live.

421	### 2026-05-20 — Hardware bring-up after USB CDC host regen: TC358743 wedge resolved
422	
423	First on-target test after the M2 actuator path landed. Symptoms: video stream not starting, USB ports unpowered, FBL heartbeat firing with `connected=N`. Boot stopped after `TC358743: probe starting`.
424	
425	Root cause: the USB MCC regen reordered SYS_Initialize so `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize` ran *after* `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize`. With AIC initialized late, the FLEXCOM6 interrupt vector wasn't owned by the AIC when the first I²C transfer ran; `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` blocked forever waiting for an ISR that never fired. FBL stayed alive because it's pure FreeRTOS — no peripheral interrupt dependency.
426	
427	Fix: reverted SYS_Initialize order so MMU/AIC/WDT-disable run before TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC. Display + capture came back on first boot. Logged as patch #6 in the MCC re-apply list above.
428	
429	USB enumeration is still not working (VBUS not asserting, no device detected). That's a separate investigation — next session.

431	### 2026-05-20 — Static-allocation conversion, cv_marvin_v1 port, USB CDC host bring-up
432	
433	Long session covering three independent threads:
434	
435	1. **Static-allocation conversion.** Adopted project rule: marvin code never uses dynamic FreeRTOS APIs. MCC regenerated with `configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION=1` and `vApplicationGetIdleTaskMemory`. Converted `log.c`, `video.c`, `detector.c`, `cv_marvin_v1.c` to `xTaskCreateStatic` / `xQueueCreateStatic` / `xSemaphoreCreateMutexStatic` with per-module `Static{Task,Queue,Semaphore}_t` plus storage arrays at file scope. FreeRTOS heap stays at heap_1 only because MCC tasks still need it. Also fixed two latent video.c issues surfaced by the build: forward-declared `s_capture_armed/s_display_bound` above the ISR that reads them, added missing `#include <stdbool.h>` to `video.h`.
436	
437	2. **cv_marvin_v1 reference port.** Ported `tools/fret-tuner/detect_video.py` to C — 5×5 patch BGR sampling, brightness-based hold detect with hysteresis (`HOLD_THRESH=50`, release at 60%), color-filtered edge detect with rising-edge `press_count`, per-fret BGR target/reject filter table. Coords scaled from Python's 1920×1080 anchor to 720×480 (Wii 480p60) at port time — same Elgato direct-pixel topology, just different resolution. Bus record stays canonical (option A): only `pressed / confidence / raw_value` cross the bus; `press_count` and raw color distances stay private to the module. Recording-format choice (custom packed binary vs nanopb vs CBOR) deferred to M5. ISC framebuffer pool moved from `.region_cache_aligned` to `.region_nocache` so CPU readers see DMA writes coherently; cap dropped 1080p→720p to fit the 16 MB nocache region.
438	
439	3. **USB CDC host MCC regen.** Decided on USB CDC (marvin host, fretboard device) for the actuator/detector link instead of FLEXCOM UART — single cable, auto-enumeration, host-PC-debuggable. MCC regenerated with EHCI+OHCI host drivers and CDC host class. VBUS power-enable pins on PC27+PC31 (one per port). Hand-edit needed in `initialization.c` `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` because MCC assumes a single VBUS pin named `VBUS_AH` and emits one Set/Clear call; with two pins we need both per-pin macros explicitly. Logged as patch #5 in the MCC re-apply list.

441	Spec update: added §4.8 game-state awareness & control as a marvin subsystem (peer of detection but separate bus, video-frame consumer not a detector). Defers recognizer algorithm + arbitration boundary as Q10/Q11.

192	/* Drop counters are RMW from both task (send_state, EmitPatch,
193	 * NoteSinkDrop) and ISR (EmitStampFromISR) contexts. ARM926 single-
194	 * issue makes a single 32-bit aligned store atomic, but the increment
195	 * is LDR/ADD/STR — an ISR firing between LDR and STR loses an increment.
196	 * Critical sections (which globally disable IRQs on this port) keep
197	 * the RMW indivisible. The counters are diagnostic, so the very brief
198	 * IRQ-off window is fine. */
199	static inline void counter_add_task(volatile uint32_t *p, uint32_t v)
200	{
201	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
202	    *p += v;
203	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
204	}
205	
206	static inline void counter_add_isr(volatile uint32_t *p, uint32_t v)
207	{
208	    UBaseType_t s = taskENTER_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR();
209	    *p += v;
210	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR(s);
211	}

217	    {

8	/* Perf-log wire format. Mirror this header byte-for-byte in the host
9	 * decoder (tools/marvin-perf). Bump PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION on
10	 * every layout change; the host refuses streams that don't match.
11	 *
12	 * All fields little-endian, naturally aligned, fixed width. Records
13	 * are framed on the wire by the drain task (SOF magic + length + CRC);
14	 * the structs below are the framed payload only. */
15	
16	#define PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION   1u
17	
18	#define PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC        0x4D56u   /* 'M','V' little-endian */
19	
20	/* SOF bytes: 0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56 ("UMRV"). Distinct from the 16-bit
21	 * header magic so a mid-stream reader can resync on a 4-byte pattern. */
22	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_0            0x55u
23	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_1            0x4Du
24	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_2            0x52u
25	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_3            0x56u
26	
27	typedef enum
28	{
29	    PERF_REC_SESSION        = 0x01,
30	    PERF_REC_STAMP          = 0x02,
31	    PERF_REC_DETECTOR       = 0x03,
32	    PERF_REC_TIMING         = 0x04,
33	    PERF_REC_PATCH          = 0x05,
34	    PERF_REC_DROP           = 0x06,
35	    PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER = 0x07,
36	} perf_rec_type_t;
37	
38	/* stage_id values for PERF_REC_STAMP. Producer call sites map 1:1. */
39	typedef enum
40	{
41	    PERF_STAGE_ISC_IRQ            = 0x10,
42	    PERF_STAGE_VIDEO_PUBLISH      = 0x11,
43	    PERF_STAGE_CV_START           = 0x20,
44	    PERF_STAGE_CV_END             = 0x21,
45	    PERF_STAGE_TP_TICK            = 0x30,
46	    PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND           = 0x40,
47	    PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE = 0x41,
48	} perf_stage_t;
49	
50	#define PERF_FLAG_FROM_ISR        0x01u
51	
52	/* Common header on every record. 16 B. */
53	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
54	{
55	    uint16_t magic;           /* PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC */
56	    uint8_t  type;            /* perf_rec_type_t */
57	    uint8_t  flags;           /* PERF_FLAG_* */
58	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* Video_FrameInfo.frame_count at producer site */
59	    uint64_t ts_counter;      /* SYS_TIME raw counter; host divides by timer_freq_hz */
60	} perf_hdr_t;
61	
62	/* PERF_REC_SESSION — emitted once when the drain task starts. The host
63	 * decoder uses timer_freq_hz to convert ts_counter to seconds and
64	 * schema_version to refuse mismatched streams. */
65	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
66	{
67	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
68	    uint32_t   timer_freq_hz;
69	    uint16_t   schema_version;
70	    uint16_t   reserved;
71	    uint32_t   fw_git_short;  /* zero until we wire a build-time symbol */
72	    uint32_t   reserved2;
73	} perf_rec_session_t;
74	
75	/* PERF_REC_STAMP — single-point timestamp marker. aux is stage-specific:
76	 *   ISC_IRQ           : reserved (0)
77	 *   VIDEO_PUBLISH     : subscriber bitmask
78	 *   CV_START / CV_END : reserved (0)
79	 *   TP_TICK           : publish_mask (low 7 bits)
80	 *   FBL_SEND          : queued mask
81	 *   CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE: USB CDC result code */
82	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
83	{
84	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
85	    uint8_t    stage_id;      /* perf_stage_t */
86	    uint8_t    reserved[3];

88	    uint32_t   reserved2;

92	/* PERF_REC_DETECTOR — per-frame snapshot of cv_marvin_v1 internals.
93	 * hold/edge values use the same 0..65535 scaling as
94	 * detector_state_t.{raw_value, confidence} so the host can share one
95	 * conversion path. */
96	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
97	{
98	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
99	    uint16_t   hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];   /* 5 × 2 = 10 B */
100	    uint16_t   edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];   /* 5 × 2 = 10 B */
101	    uint8_t    pressed_mask;
102	    uint8_t    edge_active_mask;
103	    uint16_t   reserved;
104	} perf_rec_detector_t;
105	
106	/* PERF_REC_TIMING — timing_pipeline state at the per-frame tick. */
107	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
108	{
109	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
110	    uint8_t    publish_mask;       /* low 7 bits = chord on the wire */
111	    uint8_t    chord_window_fill;  /* records currently held in chord window */
112	    uint8_t    fifo_depth;         /* delay FIFO depth */
113	    uint8_t    strum_dir;          /* 0 = none, 1 = down, 2 = up */
114	    uint32_t   reserved;
115	    uint32_t   reserved2;
116	    uint32_t   reserved3;
117	} perf_rec_timing_t;
118	
119	/* PERF_REC_DROP — drain task emits at 1 Hz. Counters are cumulative
120	 * since session start; host computes deltas. */
121	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
122	{
123	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
124	    uint32_t   dropped_state;
125	    uint32_t   dropped_patch;
126	    uint32_t   dropped_sink;
127	    uint32_t   reserved;
128	} perf_rec_drop_t;
129	
130	/* PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER — periodic stack high-water dump. task_id is
131	 * a stable enum mirrored in the host decoder; words is the
132	 * uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark return (StackType_t units). */
133	typedef enum
134	{
135	    PERF_TASK_VIDEO          = 0,
136	    PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1   = 1,
137	    PERF_TASK_DETECTOR_DRAIN = 2,
138	    PERF_TASK_TIMING         = 3,
139	    PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK = 4,
140	    PERF_TASK_PERF_DRAIN     = 5,
141	} perf_task_id_t;
142	
143	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
144	{
145	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
146	    uint8_t    task_id;
147	    uint8_t    reserved[3];
148	    uint32_t   words;
149	} perf_rec_task_highwater_t;
150	
151	/* PERF_REC_PATCH — Tier 2 ROI dump. Two 5×5 BGR patches per fret
152	 * (hold sensor + edge sensor). Coords are the (hx,hy) / (ex,ey) the
153	 * detector actually sampled — host can replay the detector math
154	 * pixel-for-pixel. */
155	#define PERF_PATCH_DIM        5u    /* matches CV_PATCH_RADIUS = 2 */
156	#define PERF_PATCH_PIXELS     (PERF_PATCH_DIM * PERF_PATCH_DIM)
157	#define PERF_PATCH_BYTES      (PERF_PATCH_PIXELS * 3u)   /* 75 B per patch */
158	
159	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
160	{
161	    uint16_t hx, hy;
162	    uint16_t ex, ey;
163	    uint8_t  hold_bgr[PERF_PATCH_BYTES];
164	    uint8_t  edge_bgr[PERF_PATCH_BYTES];
165	} perf_patch_fret_t;        /* 8 + 75 + 75 = 158 B */
166	
167	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
168	{
169	    perf_hdr_t        hdr;
170	    uint16_t          frame_w;
171	    uint16_t          frame_h;
172	    uint32_t          reserved;
173	    perf_patch_fret_t fret[FRET_COUNT];   /* 5 × 158 = 790 B */
174	} perf_rec_patch_t;          /* 16 + 8 + 790 = 814 B */
175	
176	#endif /* PERF_LOG_RECORDS_H */

39	static void emit_static_header(void)
40	{
41	    LOG_INFO("\r\n=== diag: build ===\r\n"
42	             "  CPU=%u Hz  tick=%u Hz  max_pri=%u\r\n"
43	             "  rt_counter=SYS_TIME (%u Hz)  total_heap=%u  free_now=%u\r\n",
44	             (unsigned)configCPU_CLOCK_HZ,
45	             (unsigned)configTICK_RATE_HZ,
46	             (unsigned)configMAX_PRIORITIES,
47	             (unsigned)SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet(),
48	             (unsigned)configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE,
49	             (unsigned)xPortGetFreeHeapSize());
50	}
51	
52	static void emit_task_dump(void)
53	{
54	    configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE total = 0;
55	    UBaseType_t n = uxTaskGetSystemState(s_status, DIAG_MAX_TASKS, &total);
56	
57	    /* SYS_TIME drives the run-time counter at full chip-timer rate; show
58	     * accumulated CPU time in ms for readability. ticks_per_ms is computed
59	     * once at startup, but freq is constant so a local recompute is fine. */
60	    uint64_t ticks_per_ms = (uint64_t)SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet() / 1000u;
61	    if (ticks_per_ms == 0u) { ticks_per_ms = 1u; }
62	
63	    LOG_INFO("\r\n=== diag: tasks (n=%u total_cpu_ms=%lu) ===\r\n"
64	             "  %-16s St Pri  HWM   CPU(ms)  Pct\r\n",
65	             (unsigned)n,
66	             (unsigned long)(total / ticks_per_ms),
67	             "Name");
68	
69	    configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE slice = total / 1000u;
70	    if (slice == 0u) { slice = 1u; }
71	
72	    for (UBaseType_t i = 0u; i < n; i++)
73	    {
74	        unsigned pct10 = (unsigned)(s_status[i].ulRunTimeCounter / slice);
75	        unsigned long cpu_ms =
76	            (unsigned long)(s_status[i].ulRunTimeCounter / ticks_per_ms);
77	        LOG_INFO("  %-16s %c  %2u %5u %9lu  %3u.%01u%%\r\n",
78	                 s_status[i].pcTaskName,
79	                 state_char(s_status[i].eCurrentState),
80	                 (unsigned)s_status[i].uxCurrentPriority,
81	                 (unsigned)s_status[i].usStackHighWaterMark,
82	                 cpu_ms,
83	                 pct10 / 10u, pct10 % 10u);
84	    }
85	}
86	
87	static void diag_task(void *param)
88	{
89	    (void)param;
90	
91	    emit_static_header();
92	
93	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(DIAG_FIRST_DELAY_MS));
94	
95	    for (;;)
96	    {
97	        emit_task_dump();
98	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(DIAG_PERIOD_MS));
99	    }
100	}
101	
102	void Diag_Initialize(void)
103	{
104	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(diag_task,
105	                            "Diag",
106	                            DIAG_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
107	                            NULL,
108	                            DIAG_TASK_PRIORITY,
109	                            s_task_stack,
110	                            &s_task_tcb);
111	}
112
```

           hdr_fill(&slot.hwm.hdr, PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER, 0u, 0u);
           slot.hwm.task_id = (uint8_t)id;
           slot.hwm.words   = words;

(c) 1-byte bitmask matches `tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py` and `firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h` exactly (G/R/Y/B/O at bits 0..4, strum-down bit 5, strum-up bit 6) — no reason to invent a new framing while the protocol is this small. Latest-wins semantics on the marvin→fretboard queue (depth 1 + overwrite) so a stalled USB write can't accumulate stale chords. (d) **Actuator-latency compensation deferred until mechanical actuators arrive.** Today's actuator is direct GPIO assertion on the fretboard PCB — latency ≈ 0, so today's design is sound. Future paths considered: (1) marvin compensates by subtracting a fretboard-published latency from `assert_at`/`strum_at`; (2) fretboard compensates by accepting timestamped events and scheduling locally. Path 2 needs a richer wire format (event + abs-timestamp); path 1 keeps the byte protocol but pushes the timing math up. Pick when we know which actuator (voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid) we're driving. |
73	| 2026-05-20 | Game-state awareness & high-level game control is a marvin subsystem (spec §4.8). Distinct from the gameplay note-detection path: a video-frame consumer (not a detector) emits typed game-state events on `xGameStateQueue`, and a controller layer translates verbs ("start single-player song X") into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link | Want marvin to drive whole-session play, not just notes once gameplay starts. Game-state observation belongs on marvin because it's CV on the same captured frames. Separating its bus from `xDetectorStateQueue` keeps `detector_state_t` narrow per the 2026-05-20 multi-detector decision. Per-game catalog (menu graph + song list) is metadata kept on marvin. Default arbitration with timing pipeline: mutually exclusive — controller runs only outside `gameplay` state. Phasing: M9 observer-only, M10 control. Open: recognizer algorithm (Q10), arbitration boundary (Q11). |

114	     #define configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE             uint64_t
115	     #define portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS()

118	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). _**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 17:17:09Z)**_

Found the bug — it's a 32-bit timer wrap. `ts_counter` jumps backwards by ~15.1 s every ~16 s, which is exactly UINT32_MAX/266 MHz = 16.1 s.

[perf_log.c:78](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c#L78) calls `SYS_TIME_CounterGet()` which returns **uint32_t** — the cast to `uint64_t` happens after truncation. The journal already documents this exact problem for FreeRTOS run-time stats (patch #8), and the 64-bit variant `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()` is already declared and used by `FreeRTOSConfig.h`. Quick fix:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 17:17:24Z)**_

Declared in `sys_time.h` which is pulled via `definitions.h`. No additional include needed. Rebuild + recapture should give monotonic 64-bit timestamps and the timeline will span the full capture duration.

The "groups" you saw on the drop line are also explained: each DROP record is followed by 5 HWM records emitted within ~0.2 ms. The timeline likely renders all of them on the same track (or close enough to overlap visually). After Phase 2 lands STAMP records the strict-by-type filtering will sort that out.

perf-log: use 64-bit SYS_TIME counter for ts_counter

SYS_TIME_CounterGet() returns uint32_t, so the cast to uint64_t in
hdr_fill happened after truncation — the high 32 bits were always zero
and ts_counter wrapped every ~16 s at 266 MHz. Switch to
SYS_TIME_Counter64Get() (already declared in sys_time.h and used by
FreeRTOSConfig for run-time stats) so timestamps are genuinely 64-bit
monotonic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

#include <stdint.h>

#include "task.h"

#include "log.h"

#define DIAG_TASK_STACK_WORDS    1024u
#define DIAG_TASK_PRIORITY       1u

#define DIAG_PERIOD_MS           10000u
#define DIAG_FIRST_DELAY_MS      2000u

/* Sized above the current 16-task footprint (9 MCC + 7 marvin) with
 * headroom for future tasks. uxTaskGetSystemState writes only as many
 * entries as it has tasks to fill. */
#define DIAG_MAX_TASKS           24u

static StackType_t  s_task_stack[DIAG_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;

{

    {
        case eRunning:   return 'X';
        case eReady:     return 'R';
        case eBlocked:   return 'B';
        case eSuspended: return 'S';
        case eDeleted:   return 'D';
        default:         return '?';
    }
}

             "  rt_counter=SYS_TIME (%u Hz)  total_heap=%u  free_now=%u\r\n",
             (unsigned)configCPU_CLOCK_HZ,
             (unsigned)configTICK_RATE_HZ,
             (unsigned)configMAX_PRIORITIES,
             (unsigned)SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet(),
             (unsigned)configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE,
             (unsigned)xPortGetFreeHeapSize());
}

static void emit_task_dump(void)
{
    configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE total = 0;
    UBaseType_t n = uxTaskGetSystemState(s_status, DIAG_MAX_TASKS, &total);

    /* SYS_TIME drives the run-time counter at full chip-timer rate; show
     * accumulated CPU time in ms for readability. ticks_per_ms is computed
     * once at startup, but freq is constant so a local recompute is fine. */
    uint64_t ticks_per_ms = (uint64_t)SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet() / 1000u;
    if (ticks_per_ms == 0u) { ticks_per_ms = 1u; }

    LOG_INFO("\r\n=== diag: tasks (n=%u total_cpu_ms=%lu) ===\r\n"
             "  %-16s St Pri  HWM   CPU(ms)  Pct\r\n",
             (unsigned)n,
             (unsigned long)(total / ticks_per_ms),
             "Name");

    configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE slice = total / 1000u;
    if (slice == 0u) { slice = 1u; }

    for (UBaseType_t i = 0u; i < n; i++)
    {
        unsigned pct10 = (unsigned)(s_status[i].ulRunTimeCounter / slice);
        unsigned long cpu_ms =
            (unsigned long)(s_status[i].ulRunTimeCounter / ticks_per_ms);
        LOG_INFO("  %-16s %c  %2u %5u %9lu  %3u.%01u%%\r\n",
                 s_status[i].pcTaskName,
                 state_char(s_status[i].eCurrentState),
                 (unsigned)s_status[i].uxCurrentPriority,
                 (unsigned)s_status[i].usStackHighWaterMark,
                 cpu_ms,
                 pct10 / 10u, pct10 % 10u);
    }
}

static void diag_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    emit_static_header();

    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(DIAG_FIRST_DELAY_MS));

    for (;;)
    {
        emit_task_dump();
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(DIAG_PERIOD_MS));
    }
}

void Diag_Initialize(void)
{
    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(diag_task,
                            "Diag",
                            DIAG_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                            NULL,
                            DIAG_TASK_PRIORITY,
                            s_task_stack,
                            &s_task_tcb);
}
```

I'd wire **STAMP producers** next — they're already declared in `perf_log.h` but no firmware site calls them yet, and they're the original point of the perf log (6-stage pipeline latency per frame). It's cheap (6 `PerfLog_EmitStamp(stage, frame_epoch, aux)` calls at the right pipeline points, no schema change), and once they flow the timeline actually shows the latency story instead of just heartbeats.

Phase 2 (STRIP + TASK_RUNTIME + live WS, schema bump to v2) is the alternative — bigger but unlocks pixels-in-browser. STAMPs first feels like the higher-leverage move; redirect if you'd rather jump to Phase 2.

164	static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)
165	{
166	    if (!s_connected) { return false; }
167	
168	    static uint8_t tx_byte;
169	    tx_byte = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
170	
171	    /* Drain any prior signal so we wait for *this* write's completion. */
172	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, 0);
173	
174	    USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th;
175	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT r = USB_HOST_CDC_Write(s_cdc_handle, &th, &tx_byte, 1u);
176	    if (r != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
177	    {
178	        LOG_WARN("FBL: CDC_Write rejected, r=%d\r\n", (int)r);
179	        return false;
180	    }
181	
182	    if (xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS)) != pdTRUE)
183	    {
184	        LOG_WARN("FBL: write timeout, marking detached\r\n");
185	        close_cdc();
186	        return false;
187	    }
188	    if (s_last_write_result != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
189	    {
190	        LOG_WARN("FBL: write completion err=%d\r\n", (int)s_last_write_result);
191	        return false;
192	    }
193	    return true;
194	}
195	
196	static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
197	{
198	    (void)param;
199	
200	    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started\r\n");
201	
202	    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;
203	
204	    for (;;)
205	    {
206	        if (s_cdc_obj_valid && s_cdc_handle == USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID)
207	        {
208	            s_cdc_obj_valid = false;
209	            (void)open_cdc(s_cdc_obj_pending);
210	        }
211	
212	        uint8_t mask;
213	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
214	        {
215	            last_mask = mask;
216	        }
217	        else
218	        {
219	            mask = last_mask;
220	        }
221	
222	        if (s_connected)
223	        {
224	            (void)send_one_byte(mask);
225	        }
226	    }

120	static void sample_and_emit_hwms(void)
121	{
122	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
123	    {
124	        TaskHandle_t h = s_task_handles[i];
125	        if (h == NULL) { continue; }
126	        uint32_t words = (uint32_t)uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark(h);
127	        PerfLog_EmitTaskHighwater((perf_task_id_t)i, words);
128	    }
129	}
130	
131	static void perf_log_drain_task(void *param)
132	{
133	    (void)param;
134	
135	    PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize();
136	    s_running = true;
137	
138	    TickType_t last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
139	    bool prev_connected = false;
140	
141	    for (;;)
142	    {
143	        bool now_connected = PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected();
144	        if (now_connected && !prev_connected)
145	        {
146	            emit_session_record();
147	        }
148	        prev_connected = now_connected;
149	
150	        perf_rec_state_slot_t srec;
151	        if (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec,
152	                          pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DRAIN_RX_TIMEOUT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
153	        {
154	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
155	        }
156	
157	        perf_rec_patch_t prec;
158	        while (xQueueReceive(s_patch_q, &prec, 0) == pdTRUE)
159	        {
160	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&prec, (uint16_t)sizeof(prec));
161	        }
162	
163	        if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - last_drop) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DROP_REPORT_PERIOD_MS))
164	        {
165	            last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
166	            emit_drop_record();
167	            sample_and_emit_hwms();
168	        }
169	    }
170	}

77	def iter_frames(
78	    chunks: Iterable[bytes],
79	    stats: FrameStats | None = None,
80	) -> Iterator[FrameBytes]:
81	    """Consume an iterable of byte chunks, yield validated frame payloads.
82	
83	    The iterator handles arbitrary chunk boundaries (a frame may straddle as
84	    many chunks as it likes), resyncs on the 4-byte SOF after byte loss, and
85	    drops frames whose CRC does not match. Counters are accumulated into
86	    `stats` if supplied.
87	    """
88	    if stats is None:
89	        stats = FrameStats()
90	
91	    buf = bytearray()
92	    skipped_since_last_ok = 0
93	
94	    for chunk in chunks:
95	        if not chunk:
96	            continue
97	        buf.extend(chunk)
98	
99	        while True:
100	            sof_idx = buf.find(SOF_BYTES)
101	            if sof_idx < 0:
102	                # No SOF in buffer. Drop everything but the last 3 bytes (a
103	                # SOF could still be straddling the boundary).
104	                if len(buf) > 3:
105	                    skipped_since_last_ok += len(buf) - 3
106	                    stats.bytes_resync_dropped += len(buf) - 3
107	                    del buf[: len(buf) - 3]
108	                break
109	
110	            if sof_idx > 0:
111	                skipped_since_last_ok += sof_idx
112	                stats.bytes_resync_dropped += sof_idx
113	                del buf[:sof_idx]
114	
115	            # buf now starts with SOF. Need 4 (SOF) + 2 (LEN) before we can
116	            # bound the frame.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 17:48:34Z)**_

Data is healthy. To your question — **no, not every record has a frame_epoch**, and that's by design:

**Carry frame_epoch (one shared epoch per ISC frame):**
- `ISC_IRQ`, `VIDEO_PUBLISH`, `CV_START`, `CV_END`, `TP_TICK` — exactly 3199 of each over the capture, one set per frame.

**frame_epoch = 0 (not tied to a frame):**
- `Session`, `Drop`, `TaskHighwater` — housekeeping, no frame association.
- `FBL_SEND`, `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` — actuator side. The cmd queue between TimingPipeline and FretboardLink carries only `uint8_t mask`, no epoch. Host pairs FBL_SEND→CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE by ts_counter adjacency, which is what the plan calls for.

**Sanity numbers:**
- Span: **53.4 s**, frame_epoch **4186..7384** = 3199 frames → **59.9 Hz** ✓
- Stages 5/frame perfectly balanced (3199 each).
- **53 Drop records** at 1 Hz, **265 HWM** (53 × 5 active tasks) — matches drain cadence.
- `dropped_state = 0`, `dropped_patch = 0` over the whole capture — perf-log queues never overflowed.
- `dropped_sink = 993136` bytes is **constant first→last drop** — that's pre-attach sink discard accumulated before USB enumerated. No bytes lost during the capture itself.
- `FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` ≈ 240/s — consistent with the 5 ms TimingPipeline tick pushing into a latest-wins queue and FretboardLink draining as fast as USB CDC round-trips allow (~4 ms each).

So the data looks right — what specifically looked off in the viewer?

28	| 2026-05-21 | `configMAX_PRIORITIES` bumped 5 → 8; tasks re-tiered into 4 active bands (UI=2, diagnostic+perf-wire=3, vision=4, strum-critical+host-wire=5) plus 3 reserve bands (1, 6, 7) and idle (0). MCC tasks re-prioritised via the per-component yml files so future regens preserve the layout. | Pre-change layout had 11 tasks bunched at priority 1 (9 MCC pollers + VideoTask + DetectorDrain) and 4 at priority 2, with no headroom. Two concrete problems: (a) VideoTask was *below* its consumer CvMarvinV1, a classic priority inversion that would bite during any priority-2 busy spell; (b) Legato (UI rendering) at the same priority as USB host driver tasks meant a heavy frame redraw could stall fretboard wire transit. The new layout puts strum-critical output above vision-real-time above diagnostic-I/O above UI, which matches the failure-cost ordering: a late strum is a missed note, a late detector tick recovers next frame, a late UI paint is jitter only. Reserve bands cost ~60 B BSS each, leave room for future watchdog or fault-recovery work to land without re-shuffling. Setting priorities in MCC yml (rather than patching `tasks.c` post-regen) avoids a re-apply patch — the source of truth and the emitted code now agree. |
29	| 2026-05-21 | `manual_control` lands as the second producer of `fretboard_link`, alongside `timing_pipeline`. Mode-level arbitration is two-mode (`timing_pipeline` vs `manual_control`) and embedded in `ManualControl_SetEnabled`: entering manual mode calls `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false)` then takes the wire; exiting reverses. | First concrete validation of the 2026-05-20 multi-producer `fretboard_link` design — `FretboardLink_Send` stays the only entry point; arbitration lives one layer up. Embedded toggle is enough for two producers; refactor to a dedicated `actuator_mode` arbiter when a third producer (game-state controller §4.8) arrives. `timing_pipeline.publish_mask` keeps updating internal state when gated so the next ≤5 ms tick after re-enable republishes a correct mask without a stale frame. |
30	| 2026-05-21 | Legato chosen for the manual-control surface; widgets authored in Microchip Graphics Composer (regenerated into `le_gen_screen_Screen0.{h,c}`); marvin-side code is a thin event-binding shim (`ui/manual_input.c`) | Composer makes the layout iterable in a tool rather than C source, and keeps our code out of MCC-clobbered files: only the binding shim references the Composer-generated widget pointers. **Does not commit spec Q5 for the full operator UI** — that's still M5's call. 31	| 2026-05-21 | Manual-control input model is single-finger momentary; multi-finger chord input is out of scope for this surface | Legato's input pipeline (`legato_input.c:340/429`) routes each touch to a single focus widget, so a second simultaneous touch cancels the first button's release and strands its `pressed` state. Workarounds (custom maxtouch dispatcher; toggle-style frets) are real but not worth the complexity here — primary use case is game-menu navigation, which is single-finger by nature. 33	| 2026-05-20 | Relax Microchip's host CDC-ACM Communications-interface protocol check to accept `bInterfaceProtocol == 0x00 (None)` in addition to `0x01 (AT_V250)` | The fretboard hardware exposes its UART to marvin via the on-board EDBG debugger's CDC ACM (composite VID=0x03EB PID=0x2175: HID + CDC ACM IAD + vendor + MSC). EDBG declares the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol=0x00` rather than the AT-command protocol Microchip hardcodes. The TPL/IAD match accepts the device (host stack does call `interfaceAssign`), but the per-interface check inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` then rejects the comm interface, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to STATE_ERROR, and our attach handler never fires. 8	/* Perf-log wire format. Mirror this header byte-for-byte in the host
9	 * decoder (tools/marvin-perf). Bump PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION on
10	 * every layout change; the host refuses streams that don't match.
11	 *
12	 * All fields little-endian, naturally aligned, fixed width. Records
13	 * are framed on the wire by the drain task (SOF magic + length + CRC);
14	 * the structs below are the framed payload only. */
15	
16	#define PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION   1u
17	
18	#define PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC        0x4D56u   /* 'M','V' little-endian */
19	
20	/* SOF bytes: 0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56 ("UMRV"). Distinct from the 16-bit
21	 * header magic so a mid-stream reader can resync on a 4-byte pattern. */
22	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_0            0x55u
23	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_1            0x4Du
24	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_2            0x52u
25	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_3            0x56u
26	
27	typedef enum
28	{
29	    PERF_REC_SESSION        = 0x01,
30	    PERF_REC_STAMP          = 0x02,
31	    PERF_REC_DETECTOR       = 0x03,
32	    PERF_REC_TIMING         = 0x04,
33	    PERF_REC_PATCH          = 0x05,
34	    PERF_REC_DROP           = 0x06,
35	    PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER = 0x07,
36	} perf_rec_type_t;
37	
38	/* stage_id values for PERF_REC_STAMP. Producer call sites map 1:1. */
39	typedef enum

43	    PERF_STAGE_CV_START           = 0x20,
44	    PERF_STAGE_CV_END             = 0x21,

57	    uint8_t  flags;           /* PERF_FLAG_* */

133	typedef enum

135	    PERF_TASK_VIDEO          = 0,
136	    PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1   = 1,
137	    PERF_TASK_DETECTOR_DRAIN = 2,

139	    PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK = 4,
140	    PERF_TASK_PERF_DRAIN     = 5,

149	} perf_rec_task_highwater_t;

155	#define PERF_PATCH_DIM        5u    /* matches CV_PATCH_RADIUS = 2 */
156	#define PERF_PATCH_PIXELS     (PERF_PATCH_DIM * PERF_PATCH_DIM)
157	#define PERF_PATCH_BYTES      (PERF_PATCH_PIXELS * 3u)   /* 75 B per patch */
158

165	} perf_patch_fret_t;        /* 8 + 75 + 75 = 158 B */

174	} perf_rec_patch_t;          /* 16 + 8 + 790 = 814 B */

12	/* Per-frame performance log. Producers post records onto two static
13	 * queues (small / patch); a low-priority drain task frames them
14	 * (SOF + length + payload + CRC-16/CCITT) and pushes the bytes out the
15	 * USB-device CDC sink. Drop-on-full, never block. The pipeline must
16	 * remain unaffected if perf-log vanishes.
17	 *
18	 * All emit calls take ≈O(memcpy) and never lock. The ISR variants use
19	 * xQueueSendFromISR; the task variants use xQueueSend with zero block
20	 * time. Choose by call site — passing the wrong one will not corrupt
21	 * state but may misuse the higher_priority_task_woken pathway. */
22	
23	void PerfLog_Initialize(void);     /* call after Video_Initialize */
24	void PerfLog_Start(void);          /* call after vTaskStartScheduler */
25	
26	bool PerfLog_IsRunning(void);
27	
28	/* ─── Task-context emit ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
29	
30	void PerfLog_EmitStamp(perf_stage_t stage, uint32_t frame_epoch, uint32_t aux);
31	void PerfLog_EmitDetector(uint32_t frame_epoch,
32	                          const uint16_t hold_dist[FRET_COUNT],
33	                          const uint16_t edge_dist[FRET_COUNT],
34	                          uint8_t  pressed_mask,
35	                          uint8_t  edge_active_mask);
36	void PerfLog_EmitTiming(uint32_t frame_epoch,
37	                        uint8_t  publish_mask,
38	                        uint8_t  chord_window_fill,
39	                        uint8_t  fifo_depth,
40	                        uint8_t  strum_dir);
41	void PerfLog_EmitPatch(uint32_t frame_epoch,
42	                       uint16_t frame_w, uint16_t frame_h,
43	                       const perf_patch_fret_t fret[FRET_COUNT]);
44	
45	void PerfLog_EmitTaskHighwater(perf_task_id_t id, uint32_t words);

47	/* Each marvin task module hands its TaskHandle_t to perf_log after
48	 * xTaskCreateStatic. The 1 Hz drain task samples uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark
49	 * for every registered handle and emits a PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER record.
50	 * Unregistered slots are skipped. */
51	void PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(perf_task_id_t id, TaskHandle_t handle);

1	"""Validated frame payload → typed record dataclass."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from typing import Union
6	
7	from .records import (
8	    Detector,
9	    Drop,
10	    FRET_COUNT,
11	    Header,
12	    HDR_SIZE,
13	    PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC,
14	    Patch,
15	    PatchFret,
16	    PATCH_FRET_SIZE,
17	    RecordType,
18	    Session,
19	    Stamp,
20	    TaskHighwater,
21	    Timing,
22	    UnknownRecord,
23	    _PATCH_FRET_FMT,
24	)
25	
26	
27	Record = Union[
28	    Session, Stamp, Detector, Timing, Drop, TaskHighwater, Patch, UnknownRecord
29	]
30	
31	
32	class DecodeError(Exception):
33	    pass
34	
35	
36	def _check(payload: bytes, expected_size: int, name: str) -> None:
37	    if len(payload) != expected_size:
38	        raise DecodeError(
39	            f"{name}: payload length {len(payload)} != expected {expected_size}"
40	        )
41	
42	
43	def _decode_session(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Session:
44	    _check(payload, Session.SIZE, "Session")
45	    timer_freq_hz, schema_version, _reserved, fw_git_short, _reserved2 = (
46	        Session._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
47	    )
48	    return Session(
49	        hdr=hdr,
50	        timer_freq_hz=timer_freq_hz,
51	        schema_version=schema_version,
52	        fw_git_short=fw_git_short,
53	    )
54	
55	
56	def _decode_stamp(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Stamp:
57	    _check(payload, Stamp.SIZE, "Stamp")
58	    stage_id, _reserved, aux, _reserved2, _reserved3 = Stamp._BODY.unpack_from(
59	        payload, HDR_SIZE
60	    )
61	    return Stamp(hdr=hdr, stage_id=stage_id, aux=aux)
62	
63	
64	def _decode_detector(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Detector:
65	    _check(payload, Detector.SIZE, "Detector")
66	    fields = Detector._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
67	    # 5 hold, 5 edge, pressed_mask, edge_active_mask, reserved
68	    hold = tuple(fields[0:5])
69	    edge = tuple(fields[5:10])
70	    pressed_mask = fields[10]
71	    edge_active_mask = fields[11]
72	    return Detector(
73	        hdr=hdr,
74	        hold_dist=hold,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
75	        edge_dist=edge,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
76	        pressed_mask=pressed_mask,
77	        edge_active_mask=edge_active_mask,
78	    )
79	
80	
81	def _decode_timing(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Timing:
82	    _check(payload, Timing.SIZE, "Timing")
83	    publish_mask, chord_window_fill, fifo_depth, strum_dir, *_ = (
84	        Timing._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
85	    )
86	    return Timing(
87	        hdr=hdr,
88	        publish_mask=publish_mask,
89	        chord_window_fill=chord_window_fill,
90	        fifo_depth=fifo_depth,
91	        strum_dir=strum_dir,
92	    )
93	
94	
95	def _decode_drop(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Drop:
96	    _check(payload, Drop.SIZE, "Drop")
97	    dropped_state, dropped_patch, dropped_sink, _reserved = Drop._BODY.unpack_from(
98	        payload, HDR_SIZE
99	    )
100	    return Drop(
101	        hdr=hdr,
102	        dropped_state=dropped_state,
103	        dropped_patch=dropped_patch,
104	        dropped_sink=dropped_sink,
105	    )
106	
107	
108	def _decode_task_highwater(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> TaskHighwater:
109	    _check(payload, TaskHighwater.SIZE, "TaskHighwater")
110	    task_id, _reserved, words = TaskHighwater._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
111	    return TaskHighwater(hdr=hdr, task_id=task_id, words=words)
112	
113	
114	def _decode_patch(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Patch:
115	    _check(payload, Patch.SIZE, "Patch")
116	    frame_w, frame_h, _reserved = Patch._PRELUDE.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
117	    fret_offset = HDR_SIZE + Patch._PRELUDE.size
118	    fret = []
119	    for i in range(FRET_COUNT):
120	        off = fret_offset + i * PATCH_FRET_SIZE
121	        hx, hy, ex, ey, hold_bgr, edge_bgr = _PATCH_FRET_FMT.unpack_from(payload, off)
122	        fret.append(
123	            PatchFret(
124	                hx=hx, hy=hy, ex=ex, ey=ey,
125	                hold_bgr=hold_bgr, edge_bgr=edge_bgr,
126	            )
127	        )
128	    return Patch(
129	        hdr=hdr,
130	        frame_w=frame_w,
131	        frame_h=frame_h,
132	        fret=tuple(fret),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
133	    )
134	
135	
136	_DISPATCH = {
137	    RecordType.SESSION: _decode_session,
138	    RecordType.STAMP: _decode_stamp,
139	    RecordType.DETECTOR: _decode_detector,
140	    RecordType.TIMING: _decode_timing,
141	    RecordType.DROP: _decode_drop,
142	    RecordType.TASK_HIGHWATER: _decode_task_highwater,
143	    RecordType.PATCH: _decode_patch,
144	}
145	
146	
147	def decode_record(payload: bytes) -> Record:
148	    """Decode a CRC-validated frame payload into a typed Record dataclass.
149	
150	    Caller (framing.iter_frames) has already verified CRC and length sanity.
151	    Unknown record types are surfaced as UnknownRecord so a forward-schema
152	    firmware does not crash an older host.
153	    """
154	    if len(payload) < HDR_SIZE:
155	        raise DecodeError(f"payload {len(payload)} < HDR_SIZE {HDR_SIZE}")
156	    hdr = Header.unpack(payload)
157	    if hdr.magic != PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC:
158	        raise DecodeError(f"bad magic 0x{hdr.magic:04x}")
159	
160	    decoder = _DISPATCH.get(hdr.type)
161	    if decoder is None:
162	        return UnknownRecord(hdr=hdr, raw=payload)
163	    return decoder(hdr, payload)
164
```
</details></tool-use>

132	{
133	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
134	    {
135	        TaskHandle_t h = s_task_handles[i];

142	static void perf_log_drain_task(void *param)
143	{
144	    (void)param;
145	
146	    PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize();
147	    s_running = true;
148	
149	    TickType_t last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
150	    bool prev_connected = false;
151	
152	    for (;;)
153	    {
154	        bool now_connected = PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected();
155	        if (now_connected && !prev_connected)
156	        {
157	            emit_session_record();
158	        }
159	        prev_connected = now_connected;
160	
161	        perf_rec_state_slot_t srec;
162	        if (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec,
163	                          pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DRAIN_RX_TIMEOUT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
164	        {
165	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
166	        }
167	
168	        perf_rec_patch_t prec;
169	        while (xQueueReceive(s_patch_q, &prec, 0) == pdTRUE)
170	        {
171	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&prec, (uint16_t)sizeof(prec));
172	        }
173	
174	        if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - last_drop) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DROP_REPORT_PERIOD_MS))
175	        {
176	            last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
177	            emit_drop_record();
178	            sample_and_emit_hwms();
179	        }
180	    }
181	}

225	/* Drop counters are RMW from both task (send_state, EmitPatch,
226	 * NoteSinkDrop) and ISR (EmitStampFromISR) contexts. ARM926 single-
227	 * issue makes a single 32-bit aligned store atomic, but the increment
228	 * is LDR/ADD/STR — an ISR firing between LDR and STR loses an increment.
229	 * Critical sections (which globally disable IRQs on this port) keep
230	 * the RMW indivisible. The counters are diagnostic, so the very brief
231	 * IRQ-off window is fine. */
232	static inline void counter_add_task(volatile uint32_t *p, uint32_t v)
233	{
234	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
235	    *p += v;
236	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
237	}
238	
239	static inline void counter_add_isr(volatile uint32_t *p, uint32_t v)

     void PerfLog_EmitTaskRuntime(perf_task_id_t id,
                                  perf_task_state_t state,
                                  uint8_t priority,
                                  uint32_t run_time_counter)
     {
         perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
         memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
         hdr_fill(&slot.runtime.hdr, PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME, 0u, 0u);
         slot.runtime.task_id          = (uint8_t)id;
         slot.runtime.state            = (uint8_t)state;
         slot.runtime.priority         = priority;
         slot.runtime.run_time_counter = run_time_counter;
         send_state(&slot);
     }

     void PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(uint32_t frame_epoch,
                                     perf_strip_kind_t kind,
                                     const uint8_t *frame, uint32_t frame_stride,
                                     uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
                                     uint16_t w, uint16_t h)
     {
         if (s_strip_q == NULL || frame == NULL) { return; }
         if (w == 0u || h == 0u) { return; }
         if (w > PERF_STRIP_MAX_W || h > PERF_STRIP_MAX_H) { return; }

         static perf_rec_strip_t r;
         memset(&r, 0, PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES);
         hdr_fill(&r.hdr, PERF_REC_STRIP, 0u, frame_epoch);
         r.x = x; r.y = y; r.w = w; r.h = h;
         r.kind = (uint8_t)kind;

         const uint32_t row_bytes = (uint32_t)w * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
         const uint8_t *src = frame + (uint32_t)y * frame_stride + (uint32_t)x * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
         uint8_t *dst = r.bgr;
         for (uint16_t row = 0u; row < h; row++)
         {
             memcpy(dst, src, row_bytes);
             src += frame_stride;
             dst += row_bytes;
         }

         if (xQueueSend(s_strip_q, &r, 0) != pdTRUE)
         {
             counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
         }
     }
     ```

86	 * still produces a reading instead of a silent zero. */
87	static void sample_patch_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh,
88	                             uint16_t px, uint16_t py, float out[3])
89	{
90	    int cx = (int)px;
91	    if (cx < 0)        { cx = 0; }
92	    else if (cx >= fw) { cx = fw - 1; }
93	    int cy = (int)py;
94	    if (cy < 0)        { cy = 0; }
95	    else if (cy >= fh) { cy = fh - 1; }

97	    int r = (int)CV_PATCH_RADIUS;
98	    int x0 = cx - r;       if (x0 < 0)  { x0 = 0; }
99	    int y0 = cy - r;       if (y0 < 0)  { y0 = 0; }
100	    int x1 = cx + r + 1;   if (x1 > fw) { x1 = fw; }
101	    int y1 = cy + r + 1;   if (y1 > fh) { y1 = fh; }
102	
103	    uint32_t sum_b = 0u, sum_g = 0u, sum_r = 0u;
104	    uint32_t row_stride = (uint32_t)fw * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
105	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
106	    {
107	        const uint8_t *row = frame
108	                           + (uint32_t)y * row_stride
109	                           + (uint32_t)x0 * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
110	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
111	        {
112	            sum_b += row[0];
113	            sum_g += row[1];
114	            sum_r += row[2];
115	            row   += CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
116	        }
117	    }
118	    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(x1 - x0) * (uint32_t)(y1 - y0);
119	    out[0] = (float)sum_b / (float)n;
120	    out[1] = (float)sum_g / (float)n;
121	    out[2] = (float)sum_r / (float)n;
122	}

124	/* Max channel — triggers on any color or white. */
125	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
126	{
127	    float m = bgr[0];
128	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
129	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
130	    return m;
131	}

133	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
134	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
135	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
136	{
137	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
138	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
139	    float cmin = bgr[0];
140	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
141	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
142	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
143	
144	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
145	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
146	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
147	    return (target - reject) * sat;
148	}

158	    state.detector_id  = (uint8_t)DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1;
159	
160	    const float    hold_release = CV_HOLD_THRESH * CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
161	    const uint8_t *fbuf = (const uint8_t *)frame->buffer;
162	    uint16_t       fw   = frame->width;
163	    uint16_t       fh   = frame->height;

172	        float hd = brightness(hold_bgr);

280	    int w = (int)fw, h = (int)fh;
281	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
282	    {
283	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
284	        const uint8_t *e = s_overlay_edge_bgr[i];
285	
286	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
287	                  s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
288	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
289	                  e[0], e[1], e[2]);
290	
291	        if (s_pressed[i])
292	        {
293	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
294	                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
295	        }
296	        if (s_edge_active[i])
297	        {
298	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
299	                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);
300	        }
301	    }
302	}
303	
304	/* ─── Task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
305	
306	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
307	{
308	    (void)param;
309	
310	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
311	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
312	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
313	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
314	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
315	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
316	    configASSERT(subscribed);
317	
318	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
319	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
320	
321	    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");
322	
323	    for (;;)
324	    {
325	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
326	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
327	
328	        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
329	        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
330	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
331	        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }
332	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL){ continue; }
333	
334	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_START, frame.frame_count, 0u);
335	        detect_frame(&frame, bus);
336	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_END, frame.frame_count, 0u);
337	        draw_overlay((uint8_t *)frame.buffer, frame.width, frame.height);
338	
339	        // /* ~2 Hz signal dump for threshold tuning. hold/edge values shown
340	        //  * vs the 50 threshold, with P/E flags reflecting current state. */
341	        // if ((frame.frame_count % 30u) == 0u)
342	        // {

344	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_GREEN],  (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_GREEN],
345	        //              s_pressed[FRET_GREEN]      ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_GREEN]  ? 'E' : '.',

348	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_YELLOW], (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_YELLOW],

353	        //              s_pressed[FRET_ORANGE]     ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_ORANGE] ? 'E' : '.');
354	        // }

3	Hand-mirror — bump EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION here whenever
4	PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION is bumped on the firmware side, and keep every

6	layouts. All multi-byte fields are little-endian.

9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import struct
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	from enum import IntEnum
14	from typing import ClassVar

16	
17	EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1

19	PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC = 0x4D56  # 'M','V' little-endian

23	FRET_COUNT = 5
24

27	PATCH_BYTES = PATCH_PIXELS * 3  # 75 B per BGR patch

31	    SESSION = 0x01
32	    STAMP = 0x02
33	    DETECTOR = 0x03
34	    TIMING = 0x04
35	    PATCH = 0x05
36	    DROP = 0x06

38

42	    VIDEO_PUBLISH = 0x11

44	    CV_END = 0x21
45	    TP_TICK = 0x30
46	    FBL_SEND = 0x40
47	    CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE = 0x41

52	    CV_MARVIN_V1 = 1

56	    PERF_DRAIN = 5

58

61

63	# ─── Common header ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
64	
65	_HDR_FMT = struct.Struct("<HBBIQ")
66	HDR_SIZE = _HDR_FMT.size  # 16
67	
68	
69	@dataclass(frozen=True)
70	class Header:
71	    magic: int
72	    type: int
73	    flags: int
74	    frame_epoch: int
75	    ts_counter: int
76	
77	    @classmethod
78	    def unpack(cls, buf: bytes | memoryview) -> "Header":
79	        return cls(*_HDR_FMT.unpack_from(buf, 0))

89	    schema_version: int

175	    fret: tuple[PatchFret, PatchFret, PatchFret, PatchFret, PatchFret]
176	
177	    SIZE: ClassVar[int] = HDR_SIZE + 8 + FRET_COUNT * PATCH_FRET_SIZE  # 814
178	    _PRELUDE: ClassVar[struct.Struct] = struct.Struct("<HHI")

183	    hdr: Header
184	    raw: bytes

186

188	MAX_RECORD_BYTES = Patch.SIZE  # 814

126	            )

131	        frame_h=frame_h,
132	        fret=tuple(fret),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
133	    )
134	
135	
136	_DISPATCH = {
137	    RecordType.SESSION: _decode_session,
138	    RecordType.STAMP: _decode_stamp,
139	    RecordType.DETECTOR: _decode_detector,
140	    RecordType.TIMING: _decode_timing,
141	    RecordType.DROP: _decode_drop,
142	    RecordType.TASK_HIGHWATER: _decode_task_highwater,
143	    RecordType.PATCH: _decode_patch,
144	}
145	
146	
147	def decode_record(payload: bytes) -> Record:
148	    """Decode a CRC-validated frame payload into a typed Record dataclass.
149	
150	    Caller (framing.iter_frames) has already verified CRC and length sanity.
151	    Unknown record types are surfaced as UnknownRecord so a forward-schema
152	    firmware does not crash an older host.
153	    """
154	    if len(payload) < HDR_SIZE:
155	        raise DecodeError(f"payload {len(payload)} < HDR_SIZE {HDR_SIZE}")
156	    hdr = Header.unpack(payload)
157	    if hdr.magic != PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC:
158	        raise DecodeError(f"bad magic 0x{hdr.magic:04x}")
159	
160	    decoder = _DISPATCH.get(hdr.type)
161	    if decoder is None:
162	        return UnknownRecord(hdr=hdr, raw=payload)
163	    return decoder(hdr, payload)

```python
"""Validated frame payload → typed record dataclass."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Union

from .records import (
    Detector,
    Drop,
    Header,
    HDR_SIZE,
    PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC,
    RecordType,
    Session,
    Stamp,
    STRIP_BPP,
    STRIP_HDR_BYTES,
    STRIP_MAX_BYTES,
    Strip,
    TaskHighwater,
    TaskRuntime,
    Timing,
    UnknownRecord,
    _STRIP_BODY,
)


Record = Union[
    Session, Stamp, Detector, Timing, Drop, TaskHighwater, TaskRuntime,
    Strip, UnknownRecord,
]


class DecodeError(Exception):
    pass


def _check(payload: bytes, expected_size: int, name: str) -> None:
    if len(payload) != expected_size:
        raise DecodeError(
            f"{name}: payload length {len(payload)} != expected {expected_size}"
        )


def _decode_session(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Session:
    _check(payload, Session.SIZE, "Session")
    timer_freq_hz, schema_version, _reserved, fw_git_short, _reserved2 = (
        Session._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
    )
    return Session(
        hdr=hdr,
        timer_freq_hz=timer_freq_hz,
        schema_version=schema_version,
        fw_git_short=fw_git_short,
    )


def _decode_stamp(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Stamp:
    _check(payload, Stamp.SIZE, "Stamp")
    stage_id, _reserved, aux, _reserved2, _reserved3 = Stamp._BODY.unpack_from(
        payload, HDR_SIZE
    )
    return Stamp(hdr=hdr, stage_id=stage_id, aux=aux)


def _decode_detector(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Detector:
    _check(payload, Detector.SIZE, "Detector")
    fields = Detector._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
    hold = tuple(fields[0:5])
    edge = tuple(fields[5:10])
    pressed_mask = fields[10]
    edge_active_mask = fields[11]
    return Detector(
        hdr=hdr,
        hold_dist=hold,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        edge_dist=edge,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        pressed_mask=pressed_mask,
        edge_active_mask=edge_active_mask,
    )


def _decode_timing(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Timing:
    _check(payload, Timing.SIZE, "Timing")
    publish_mask, chord_window_fill, fifo_depth, strum_dir, *_ = (
        Timing._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
    )
    return Timing(
        hdr=hdr,
        publish_mask=publish_mask,
        chord_window_fill=chord_window_fill,
        fifo_depth=fifo_depth,
        strum_dir=strum_dir,
    )


def _decode_drop(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Drop:
    _check(payload, Drop.SIZE, "Drop")
    dropped_state, dropped_strip, dropped_sink, _reserved = Drop._BODY.unpack_from(
        payload, HDR_SIZE
    )
    return Drop(
        hdr=hdr,
        dropped_state=dropped_state,
        dropped_strip=dropped_strip,
        dropped_sink=dropped_sink,
    )


def _decode_task_highwater(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> TaskHighwater:
    _check(payload, TaskHighwater.SIZE, "TaskHighwater")
    task_id, _reserved, words = TaskHighwater._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
    return TaskHighwater(hdr=hdr, task_id=task_id, words=words)


def _decode_task_runtime(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> TaskRuntime:
    _check(payload, TaskRuntime.SIZE, "TaskRuntime")
    task_id, state, priority, _reserved, run_time_counter, _reserved2 = (
        TaskRuntime._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
    )
    return TaskRuntime(
        hdr=hdr,
        task_id=task_id,
        state=state,
        priority=priority,
        run_time_counter=run_time_counter,
    )


def _decode_strip(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Strip:
    if len(payload) < STRIP_HDR_BYTES:
        raise DecodeError(
            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} < header {STRIP_HDR_BYTES}"
        )
    x, y, w, h, kind, _reserved = _STRIP_BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
    expected_pixels = w * h * STRIP_BPP
    if expected_pixels > STRIP_MAX_BYTES:
        raise DecodeError(
            f"Strip: w*h*bpp {expected_pixels} > max {STRIP_MAX_BYTES}"
        )
    expected_total = STRIP_HDR_BYTES + expected_pixels
    if len(payload) != expected_total:
        raise DecodeError(
            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} != expected {expected_total} "
            f"({w}×{h}×{STRIP_BPP})"
        )
    bgr = bytes(payload[STRIP_HDR_BYTES:expected_total])
    return Strip(hdr=hdr, x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h, kind=kind, bgr=bgr)


_DISPATCH = {
    RecordType.SESSION: _decode_session,
    RecordType.STAMP: _decode_stamp,
    RecordType.DETECTOR: _decode_detector,
    RecordType.TIMING: _decode_timing,
    RecordType.DROP: _decode_drop,
    RecordType.TASK_HIGHWATER: _decode_task_highwater,
    RecordType.TASK_RUNTIME: _decode_task_runtime,
    RecordType.STRIP: _decode_strip,
}


def decode_record(payload: bytes) -> Record:
    """Decode a CRC-validated frame payload into a typed Record dataclass.

    Caller (framing.iter_frames) has already verified CRC and length sanity.
    Unknown record types are surfaced as UnknownRecord so a forward-schema
    firmware does not crash an older host.
    """
    if len(payload) < HDR_SIZE:
        raise DecodeError(f"payload {len(payload)} < HDR_SIZE {HDR_SIZE}")
    hdr = Header.unpack(payload)
    if hdr.magic != PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC:
        raise DecodeError(f"bad magic 0x{hdr.magic:04x}")

    decoder = _DISPATCH.get(hdr.type)
    if decoder is None:
        return UnknownRecord(hdr=hdr, raw=payload)
    return decoder(hdr, payload)

```

402	    """Compact, JSON-friendly view of a record. Avoid sending raw pixel bytes
403	    over JSON — strips travel out as PNG via the dedicated endpoint."""
404	    hdr = rec.hdr  # type: ignore[union-attr]
405	    base: dict[str, Any] = {
406	        "type": type(rec).__name__,
407	        "frame_epoch": hdr.frame_epoch,
408	        "ts_counter": hdr.ts_counter,
409	        "flags": hdr.flags,
410	    }
411	    if isinstance(rec, Session):
412	        base.update(
413	            timer_freq_hz=rec.timer_freq_hz,
414	            schema_version=rec.schema_version,
415	            fw_git_short=rec.fw_git_short,
416	        )

420	        except ValueError:
421	            base["stage"] = f"stage_{rec.stage_id:#04x}"
422	        base["stage_id"] = rec.stage_id
423	        base["aux"] = rec.aux
424	    elif isinstance(rec, Drop):
425	        base.update(
426	            dropped_state=rec.dropped_state,
427	            dropped_patch=rec.dropped_patch,
428	            dropped_sink=rec.dropped_sink,
429	        )
430	    elif isinstance(rec, TaskHighwater):
431	        try:
432	            base["task_name"] = TaskId(rec.task_id).name
433	        except ValueError:
434	            base["task_name"] = f"task_{rec.task_id}"
435	        base["task_id"] = rec.task_id
436	        base["words"] = rec.words
437	    elif isinstance(rec, Patch):
438	        base["frame_w"] = rec.frame_w
439	        base["frame_h"] = rec.frame_h
440	        # Pixels travel via the strip PNG endpoint — don't inline them.
441	    else:
442	        # Detector, Timing, UnknownRecord — keep generic field projection.
443	        for fname in getattr(rec, "__dataclass_fields__", {}):
444	            if fname == "hdr":
445	                continue
446	            v = getattr(rec, fname)
447	            if isinstance(v, (bytes, bytearray)):

449	            elif isinstance(v, tuple):
450	                base[fname] = list(v)
451	            else:
452	                base[fname] = v
