10	- **Video source**: two BGR888 strips per frame (sensing line + strike line, 240×32 each); design with full HDMI in mind for later (separate transport, deferred).
11	- **Tech stack**: browser app + local server, with the option to migrate to native if needed.
12	- **Capture format**: capture-as-directory (`manifest.json` + `perf.bin`); see Architectural commitment #2.
13	
14	## Approach
15	
16	### Architectural commitments
17	
18	1. **Library / web split.** `marvin_perf` stays pure — no FastAPI imports in `decode`/`framing`/`analyze`/`records`/`transport`. New code lives under `marvin_perf/web/` and is gated by an optional `[dependency-groups] viewer` in `pyproject.toml`. `uv sync` keeps the default install light; `uv sync --group viewer` pulls fastapi, uvicorn[standard], pillow.
19	2. **Capture-as-directory, not file.** A capture is a directory containing `manifest.json` + `perf.bin`. The bin is byte-for-byte identical to today's raw stream — `decode` and `summarize` of just the bin file still work. The directory adds a sidecar manifest carrying metadata that's expensive to recompute on every viewer load and a future-proof slot for `video.mp4` when full HDMI lands. **Distinct CLI flags** (no extension-sniffing magic): `record --out FILE.bin` writes a raw file (legacy); `record --out-dir DIR` writes a capture directory.
20	3. **Live and offline are one code path.** A live session is a capture being written. The server starts a serial-reader thread that streams bytes into a freshly-created capture directory's `perf.bin` via a `TeeSource`-like sink. The browser viewer always loads from a capture directory; "live mode" just means tailing the file as it grows + a "follow live" toggle that keeps the playhead at newest. No separate code path for live decoding.
21	4. **Two-clock model: `ts_counter` is the playhead, `frame_epoch` is a grouping key.** Every record's header carries both: `ts_counter` is the free-running 64-bit ~266 MHz counter (~3.76 ns resolution, no practical wrap) filled by `hdr_fill` in `perf_log.c:75` on **every** record; `frame_epoch` is the 32-bit per-ISC-frame counter (~16.67 ms resolution, ~830-day wrap, equals 0 for records not tied to a frame — SESSION, DROP, TASK_HIGHWATER). The **playhead lives on the `ts_counter` axis**, displayed as ms since the first SESSION's `ts_counter` (sub-ms / μs at zoom). `frame_epoch` is used only to group records that share a frame (six STAMPs + one DETECTOR + two STRIPs per frame all share an epoch) — it drives stage-pair latency math and "which strips are current at the playhead" lookup, not the timeline axis itself. Events are sparse and do not need to align with strip emissions: a STAMP at 12.345 ms renders at 12.345 ms even if no STRIP was emitted that frame. **STRIP lookup at playhead** = nearest sensing/strike strip pair at-or-before `playhead_ts` within ~1 frame period of tolerance; otherwise UI shows "no strip for this frame" rather than stale pixels. **frame_epoch wrap-awareness** still applies when it's used as a group key. **No-SESSION fallback** (mid-stream attach, no `timer_freq_hz` known): display raw tick axis with a banner instead of refusing to load.
22	
23	5. **PATCH layout: variable-size BGR888 strips, kind-tagged.** Replaces the v1 per-fret 5×5 hold/edge thumbnails. The v2 schema lands two kinds — `SENSING` and `STRIKE` — each a 240×32 strip emitted once per ISC frame, aligned to the playfield's middle-third of the 720×480 source frame. Bandwidth budget: 240 × 32 × 3 × 2 strips × 60 Hz = **2.76 MB/s pixel payload**, plus ~25 KB/s of state pipeline → ~2.79 MB/s sink load against the conservative ~5 MB/s USB CDC ACM ceiling = **~44 % headroom**. Per-record overhead is ~40 B (16 hdr + ~16 body coords + 8 framing) so two strips cost ~80 B/frame fixed, dwarfed by the 23 KB pixel payload. **Schema bump to v2** when this lands; `producer_capabilities` in the manifest carries `STRIP` so older viewers fall through to "Unknown" cleanly.
24	
25	   **Future kinds (score region, minimap, HUD slice, etc.) plug into the same record type** — the wire format treats `kind`, `x/y/w/h`, and `bgr[]` as fully variable per record. Adding a new kind is a `perf_strip_kind_t` enum entry plus a producer; no schema bump. They will run at lower cadence than the 60 Hz sensing/strike strips — score doesn't need per-frame refresh, and the remaining ~2.2 MB/s of headroom is plenty for a few-Hz score patch alongside the strips. Each kind is **independently toggleable at the producer** so the operator can disable strips during HDMI-heavy work or bench testing without code changes.

# marvin perf-log — host→device record-type masking

## Context

The perf-log channel currently emits ~1.88 MB/s under the v2 schema, dominated by 60 Hz STRIP records (~2.76 MB/s pixel payload at 240×32) and per-frame DETECTOR/TIMING traffic. The visual viewer landed and works, but the volume is doing two things wrong:

1. **Most of those records aren't analytically useful for the next round of tuning.** The user's pending question is "is the CV→fretboard path always timely?" — that question is answered by STAMP latency math (CV_START → CV_END → TP_TICK → FBL_SEND → CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE), with SESSION + DROP + TASK_HIGHWATER + TASK_RUNTIME as health context. STRIP, DETECTOR, and TIMING add no signal for that question and dominate the wire.
2. **The high-rate stamp + strip traffic is starving the 128-deep state queue** (`dropped_state ≈ 707/s` measured 2026-05-22), which is why HWM and RUNTIME records aren't reaching the host today. Cutting the volume at the source is a cleaner fix than enlarging queues we don't actually want full.

A device-side rebuild every time we want to look at a different facet of the system is the wrong pattern. We want a **runtime knob the host can set per-capture**: tell the device which record types to emit, default-all-on for parity with today, and let `marvin-perf record --types STAMP,SESSION,DROP,HIGHWATER,RUNTIME` produce a focused capture without firmware changes.

The CDC ACM endpoint is already bidirectional — the device just doesn't read today. This plan adds an RX path on the device, a small command framer reusing the existing CRC/SOF wire format, a per-record-type mask filter at the emit funnel, and a host-side CLI flag to drive it. Live-WS UI integration in the viewer is **deferred to a follow-up** — landing the firmware + CLI gives the headless tooling the win immediately.

## Approach

### Architectural commitments

1. **Reuse the TX framer for RX.** SOF (`0x55 4D 52 56`) + LEN(u16 LE) + PAYLOAD + CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE is direction-agnostic. The device gets a small RX state machine that runs the same framer in reverse. Host gets one new pure function `frame_encode(payload) -> bytes`. No new wire-level concepts.

2. **Distinct command magic from record magic.** Records start with `PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC = 0x4D56` ('MV'); commands start with `PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC = 0x4D43` ('MC'). The device's RX parser rejects anything that isn't a command frame, and the host decoder rejects anything that isn't a record frame. Catches confusion if a host accidentally writes record bytes back, or if a wedged device tries to re-emit something into its own RX.

3. **No schema bump for v2.** The change is purely additive at the host→device edge — the device keeps emitting the same v2 records. No new record types on the wire (we considered a `PERF_REC_MASK_STATE` echo, deferred — host owns the mask state; if it's not echoed back the host knows what it sent). `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays at 2.

4. **Default = all-on; mask is RAM-only.** Boot state is `s_enabled_mask = 0xFFFFFFFFu`, identical to today's behavior. Host sends the desired mask on every connect. Reset on reboot — no flash persistence (would need a new subsystem for one knob; not worth it).

5. **Mask is read lock-free at emit time.** `volatile uint32_t s_enabled_mask`; 32-bit aligned single-load on Cortex-A is atomic. Updates are 32-bit aligned single-stores from the RX path. No locks on the hot path. Worst case during a mask change: one in-flight emit is decided against the old mask — fine.

6. **Filter at the queue funnel, not at every call site.** Two early-return checks: one in `send_state` (perf_log.c:285) covering all state records, and one in `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame` (perf_log.c:366). ISR path `PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR` (perf_log.c:403) gets the same check inline. Producer call sites are unchanged — they just get cheap drops when masked.

### Wire format

\```c
/* Host→device. Wrapped in the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer as TX. Magic
 * intentionally distinct from PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC so a misrouted
 * record frame doesn't get parsed as a command. */
#define PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC   0x4D43u   /* 'M','C' little-endian */

typedef enum {
    PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK = 0x01u,    /* sole command for v0 */
} perf_cmd_t;

typedef struct __attribute__((packed)) {
    uint16_t magic;        /* PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC */
    uint8_t  cmd_id;       /* perf_cmd_t */
    uint8_t  reserved;
} perf_cmd_hdr_t;

typedef struct __attribute__((packed)) {
    perf_cmd_hdr_t hdr;
    uint32_t       enabled_mask;   /* bit i = PERF_REC_* code i */
} perf_cmd_set_mask_t;
\```

`enabled_mask` bit layout: bit `n` corresponds to `PERF_REC_*` value `n`. Bit 1 = SESSION, bit 2 = STAMP, bit 3 = DETECTOR, bit 4 = TIMING, bit 5 = STRIP, bit 6 = DROP, bit 7 = TASK_HIGHWATER, bit 8 = TASK_RUNTIME. Bit 0 unused. Bits ≥ 9 reserved.

**SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask.** It's how the host learns `timer_freq_hz` and the schema version on connect; masking it would break the playhead. The filter explicitly bypasses for `PERF_REC_SESSION`.

**DROP follows the mask.** If the user explicitly turns it off they accept losing the drop heartbeat — that's their call.

### Device side

**`perf_log_records.h`** — add the three new types above. No record-side changes, no schema bump.

**`perf_log.h`** — expose two new functions:
\```c
void     PerfLog_SetEnabledMask(uint32_t mask);
uint32_t PerfLog_GetEnabledMask(void);
\```

**`perf_log.c`** — three filter points + the mask state:
- File-scope `static volatile uint32_t s_enabled_mask = 0xFFFFFFFFu;`
- New helper `static inline bool type_enabled(uint8_t type)` → `type == PERF_REC_SESSION || (s_enabled_mask & (1u << type))`
- `send_state` (line 285): `if (!type_enabled(slot->hdr.type)) { return; }` before `xQueueSend`
- `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame` (line 366): `if (!type_enabled(PERF_REC_STRIP)) { return; }` after the existing NULL/dimension guards
- `PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR` (line 403): same check — STAMPs from ISR drop early like task-context ones
- `PerfLog_SetEnabledMask` writes `s_enabled_mask` and emits a one-line `LOG_INFO("PerfLog: mask=0x%08lx\r\n", mask)` so the UART has a record of what was selected

**`perf_log_sink_cdc.c`** — RX path:
- New CDC event branch in the existing event handler (`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:97-156`) for `USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE`
- `static uint8_t s_rx_buf[64] __attribute__((aligned(4)));` — one-packet buffer (matches the bulk-OUT max-packet of 64 B), DMA-aligned
- New `static perf_rx_framer_t s_rx_framer;` — small SOF-resync state machine: `WAIT_SOF_0..3 → READ_LEN → READ_PAYLOAD → READ_CRC`
- On `EVENT_DEVICE_CONFIGURED` (already at line 147) prime the first `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read(s_rx_buf, 64)` after the existing event-handler registration
- On `EVENT_READ_COMPLETE`: feed bytes through the framer; on a valid `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`, call `PerfLog_SetEnabledMask`; re-prime the next read
- Framer rejects on bad magic, bad CRC, bad LEN — count drops in a new `s_rx_drops` counter for diagnostics (printable via LOG, not on the wire)
- The framer is small enough (single command type, ≤16 B framed) that parsing in the event-handler context is safe — no task hand-off needed for v0

**Where the framer state machine lives.** A new `perf_log_rx.{h,c}` pair under `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/` keeps the framer separable and testable independently of the CDC sink. The sink calls `PerfLogRx_Feed(bytes, len)` from the event handler; the rx module dispatches recognized commands by calling back into `PerfLog_SetEnabledMask`. Mirror of the host-side decoder split (framing.py vs transport.py).

**No schema/version negotiation.** Old firmware ignores host commands silently (it never primes a read). New firmware accepts. The host treats command-send as best-effort fire-and-forget — no ACK required for v0.

### Host side

**`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/framing.py`** — add:
\```python
def frame_encode(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    """SOF + LEN(u16LE) + payload + CRC16-CCITT-FALSE(u16LE).
    Mirror of the device-side framer in perf_log_sink_cdc.c."""
\```
Pure function, no I/O. New unit test `test_framing.py::test_encode_round_trip` confirms `frame_encode → iter_frames` round-trips for the existing payload sizes.

**`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py`** — add command-side helpers:
\```python
PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC   = 0x4D43
PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK = 0x01

def encode_set_mask_cmd(mask: int) -> bytes:
    """Returns the framed command bytes ready for SerialSource.send_command."""
\```
And a `RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME: dict[str, int]` mapping `"SESSION" → 0x01`, `"STAMP" → 0x02`, etc., for CLI parsing.

**`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/transport.py`** — extend `SerialSource`:
\```python
def send_command(self, payload: bytes) -> int:
    """Write framed bytes to the device. Caller pre-frames via
    framing.frame_encode. Safe to call after __enter__ has set DTR."""
    return self._ser.write(payload)
\```
No changes to `__iter__` — `send_command` operates on the same `self._ser` already held. Thread-safety: pyserial's `write` is thread-safe under most platforms; we only call it from the CLI's main thread before iteration begins anyway.

**`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/cli.py`** — three changes:
1. Add `--types` flag to `live` and `record`:
   \```

   \```
   Comma-separated names from `RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME`. Special tokens: `ALL` (default, 0xFFFFFFFF), `MIN` (SESSION+DROP only). Resolves to a u32 mask, gets sent immediately after `SerialSource.__enter__` returns, before iteration starts.
2. New `set-mask` subcommand:
   \```
   marvin-perf set-mask --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --types STAMP,SESSION,DROP
   \```
   Opens the port, sends one frame, exits. For poking a running capture from another terminal.
3. Help text on `--types` lists the type names with their bit numbers.

**`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/`** — **deferred.** Live WS hasn't shipped; when it does, add `POST /api/live/set_mask` and a checkbox panel in `app.js` (see findings: tab structure at lines 169-178, route pattern at api.py:154 ready). Out of scope for this plan.

### Phasing

- **Phase 1 — firmware + framing tests (this plan).** Records header additions, perf_log filter, RX framer module, CDC RX prime, host `frame_encode`, host `SerialSource.send_command`, host CLI `--types` flag and `set-mask` subcommand, unit tests. - **Phase 2 — viewer integration (deferred).** Live-WS UI checkbox panel; `POST /api/live/set_mask` route; visual state badge for "mask: STAMP+SESSION+DROP" in the toolbar.

- **Unit tests** (`uv run pytest`):

  - `test_framing.py::test_encode_command_known_vector` — assert the byte sequence for `encode_set_mask_cmd(0x000000FE)` matches a hand-computed expected (SOF + len=8 + magic + cmd + reserved + mask + CRC)

- **Schema**: `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays at 2; existing 74-test suite passes unchanged.

- New CDC event branch in the existing event handler (`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:97-156`) for `USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE`
- `static uint8_t s_rx_buf[64] __attribute__((aligned(4)));` — one-packet buffer (matches the bulk-OUT max-packet of 64 B), DMA-aligned
- New `static perf_rx_framer_t s_rx_framer;` — small SOF-resync state machine: `WAIT_SOF_0..3 → READ_LEN → READ_PAYLOAD → READ_CRC`
- On `EVENT_DEVICE_CONFIGURED` (already at line 147) prime the first `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read(s_rx_buf, 64)` after the existing event-handler registration
- On `EVENT_READ_COMPLETE`: feed bytes through the framer; on a valid `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`, call `PerfLog_SetEnabledMask`; re-prime the next read
- Framer rejects on bad magic, bad CRC, bad LEN — count drops in a new `s_rx_drops` counter for diagnostics (printable via LOG, not on the wire)
- The framer is small enough (single command type, ≤16 B framed) that parsing in the event-handler context is safe — no task hand-off needed for v0

**Where the framer state machine lives.** A new `perf_log_rx.{h,c}` pair under `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/` keeps the framer separable and testable independently of the CDC sink. The sink calls `PerfLogRx_Feed(bytes, len)` from the event handler; the rx module dispatches recognized commands by calling back into `PerfLog_SetEnabledMask`. Mirror of the host-side decoder split (framing.py vs transport.py).

**No schema/version negotiation.** Old firmware ignores host commands silently (it never primes a read). New firmware accepts. The host treats command-send as best-effort fire-and-forget — no ACK required for v0.

### Host side

**`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/framing.py`** — add:
```python
def frame_encode(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    """SOF + LEN(u16LE) + payload + CRC16-CCITT-FALSE(u16LE).
    Mirror of the device-side framer in perf_log_sink_cdc.c."""
```
Pure function, no I/O. New unit test `test_framing.py::test_encode_round_trip` confirms `frame_encode → iter_frames` round-trips for the existing payload sizes.

**`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py`** — add command-side helpers:
```python
PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC   = 0x4D43
PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK = 0x01

def encode_set_mask_cmd(mask: int) -> bytes:
    """Returns the framed command bytes ready for SerialSource.send_command."""
```
And a `RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME: dict[str, int]` mapping `"SESSION" → 0x01`, `"STAMP" → 0x02`, etc., for CLI parsing.

**`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/transport.py`** — extend `SerialSource`:
```python
def send_command(self, payload: bytes) -> int:
    """Write framed bytes to the device. Caller pre-frames via
    framing.frame_encode. Safe to call after __enter__ has set DTR."""
    return self._ser.write(payload)
```
No changes to `__iter__` — `send_command` operates on the same `self._ser` already held. Thread-safety: pyserial's `write` is thread-safe under most platforms; we only call it from the CLI's main thread before iteration begins anyway.

**`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/cli.py`** — three changes:
1. Add `--types` flag to `live` and `record`:
   ```
   --types STAMP,SESSION,DROP,HIGHWATER,RUNTIME
   ```
   Comma-separated names from `RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME`. Special tokens: `ALL` (default, 0xFFFFFFFF), `MIN` (SESSION+DROP only). Resolves to a u32 mask, gets sent immediately after `SerialSource.__enter__` returns, before iteration starts.
2. New `set-mask` subcommand:
   ```
   marvin-perf set-mask --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --types STAMP,SESSION,DROP
   ```
   Opens the port, sends one frame, exits. For poking a running capture from another terminal.
3. Help text on `--types` lists the type names with their bit numbers.

**`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/`** — **deferred.** Live WS hasn't shipped; when it does, add `POST /api/live/set_mask` and a checkbox panel in `app.js` (see findings: tab structure at lines 169-178, route pattern at api.py:154 ready). Out of scope for this plan.

### Phasing

- **Phase 1 — firmware + framing tests (this plan).** Records header additions, perf_log filter, RX framer module, CDC RX prime, host `frame_encode`, host `SerialSource.send_command`, host CLI `--types` flag and `set-mask` subcommand, unit tests. End-to-end: `marvin-perf record --types STAMP,SESSION,DROP,HIGHWATER,RUNTIME --out-dir captures/cv-only-test` → confirm only those types appear in the capture and `dropped_state` stays at zero.
- **Phase 2 — viewer integration (deferred).** Live-WS UI checkbox panel; `POST /api/live/set_mask` route; visual state badge for "mask: STAMP+SESSION+DROP" in the toolbar.

### Verification

- **Unit tests** (`uv run pytest`):
  - `test_framing.py::test_encode_round_trip` — encode → decode pure-fn round-trip on a synthetic command payload
  - `test_framing.py::test_encode_command_known_vector` — assert the byte sequence for `encode_set_mask_cmd(0x000000FE)` matches a hand-computed expected (SOF + len=8 + magic + cmd + reserved + mask + CRC)
  - `test_cli.py::test_types_flag_parses` — `--types STAMP,SESSION` resolves to mask `0x06`
  - `test_cli.py::test_types_all_min_tokens` — `ALL`→`0xFFFFFFFF`, `MIN`→`0x42` (SESSION|DROP)
- **Bench (with hardware)**:
  - `marvin-perf record --types STAMP,SESSION,DROP,HIGHWATER,RUNTIME --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out-dir /tmp/cv-only --duration 30` (or Ctrl-C after ~30 s)
  - `marvin-perf summarize /tmp/cv-only/perf.bin` → confirm zero STRIP/DETECTOR/TIMING records, non-zero everything else, `dropped_state == 0`, `dropped_strip == 0`
  - With STRIP off, expected sink load drops from 1.88 MB/s to ~25 KB/s; the state-queue starvation noted in the journal should disappear (HWM and RUNTIME records appear in the capture instead of being dropped)
  - Sanity check the firmware UART log shows `PerfLog: mask=0x000000c6` (or matching value) when the host attaches
- **Backward compatibility**:
  - `marvin-perf record --port ... --out-dir /tmp/all` without `--types` → default ALL mask, capture identical in shape to today's
  - Old firmware (no RX path) + new host with `--types`: host sends, device ignores, capture is unfiltered. No crash. Document this in `--types --help`.
- **Schema**: `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays at 2; existing 74-test suite passes unchanged.

103	                                           USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
104	            break;
105	        }
106	
107	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SEND_BREAK:
108	            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(s_dev_handle,
109	                                           USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
110	            break;
111	
112	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_RECEIVED:
113	            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(s_dev_handle,
114	                                           USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
115	            break;
116	
117	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE:
118	        {
119	            BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
120	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_write_done, &hpw);
121	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
122	            break;
123	        }
124	
125	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE:
126	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_SENT:
127	        default:
128	            break;
129	    }
130	    return USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE_NONE;
131	}
132	
133	/* ─── Device-layer event handler ─────────────────────────────────────────── */
134	
135	static void device_event_handler(USB_DEVICE_EVENT event, void *eventData,
136	                                 uintptr_t context)
137	{
138	    (void)context;
139	
140	    switch (event)
141	    {
142	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESET:
143	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DECONFIGURED:
144	            s_is_configured = false;
145	            break;
146	
147	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_CONFIGURED:
148	        {
149	            const USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DATA_CONFIGURED *cd = eventData;
150	            if (cd->configurationValue == 1u)
151	            {
152	                (void)USB_DEVICE_CDC_EventHandlerSet(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
153	                                                    cdc_event_handler, 0u);
154	                s_is_configured = true;
155	                LOG_INFO("PERF: USB device CDC configured\r\n");
156	            }
157	            break;
158	        }
159	
160	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_DETECTED:
161	            (void)USB_DEVICE_Attach(s_dev_handle);
162	            break;
163	
164	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_REMOVED:
165	            (void)USB_DEVICE_Detach(s_dev_handle);
166	            s_is_configured = false;
167	            break;
168	
169	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SUSPENDED:
170	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESUMED:
171	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SOF:
172	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_ERROR:
173	        default:
174	            break;
175	    }
176	}
177	
178	/* ─── Public sink interface ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
179	
180	void PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize(void)
181	{
182	    s_write_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_write_done_buf);
183	    configASSERT(s_write_done != NULL);
184	
185	    /* Open may fail until USB_DEVICE_Initialize finishes its own first
186	     * task tick — retry until success. Drain task is alive at this
187	     * point so vTaskDelay is fine. */
188	    while (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
189	    {
190	        s_dev_handle = USB_DEVICE_Open(USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0,
191	                                       DRV_IO_INTENT_READWRITE);
192	        if (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
193	        {
194	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SINK_OPEN_RETRY_MS));
195	        }
196	    }
197	
198	    USB_DEVICE_EventHandlerSet(s_dev_handle, device_event_handler, 0u);
199	
200	    /* Cold-boot-with-cable case: by the time we register the handler the
201	     * UDPHS driver may have already raced past the VBUS edge it needed
202	     * to fire POWER_DETECTED, or the host may have seen a brief pull-up
203	     * assertion during early boot and given up retrying. Force a clean
204	     * detach→short delay→attach edge so the host sees an unambiguous
205	     * device-arrival on the bus. Hot-plug after this point is unaffected
206	     * because POWER_REMOVED/POWER_DETECTED still drive Detach/Attach. */
207	    (void)USB_DEVICE_Detach(s_dev_handle);
208	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100));
209	    (void)USB_DEVICE_Attach(s_dev_handle);
210	
211	    LOG_INFO("PERF: USB device opened, waiting for host enumeration\r\n");
212	}
213	
214	bool PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected(void)
215	{
216	    return s_is_configured && s_cls.dtr;
217	}
218	
219	void PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(const void *payload, uint16_t len)
220	{
221	    if (!s_is_configured || !s_cls.dtr)
222	    {
223	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
224	        return;
225	    }
226	
227	    uint16_t total = (uint16_t)(6u + len + 2u);
228	    if (total > SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX)
229	    {
230	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
231	        return;
232	    }
233	
234	    s_tx_frame[0] = 0x55u;
235	    s_tx_frame[1] = 0x4Du;
236	    s_tx_frame[2] = 0x52u;
237	    s_tx_frame[3] = 0x56u;
238	    s_tx_frame[4] = (uint8_t)(len & 0xFFu);
239	    s_tx_frame[5] = (uint8_t)((len >> 8) & 0xFFu);
240	    memcpy(&s_tx_frame[6], payload, len);
241	
242	    uint16_t crc = 0xFFFFu;
243	    crc = crc16_ccitt(crc, &s_tx_frame[4], (uint16_t)(2u + len));
244	    s_tx_frame[6u + len]      = (uint8_t)(crc & 0xFFu);
245	    s_tx_frame[6u + len + 1u] = (uint8_t)((crc >> 8) & 0xFFu);
246	
247	    /* Drain any prior signal so we wait for *this* write's completion. */
248	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, 0);
249	
250	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
251	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT r = USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
252	                                                  &th,
253	                                                  s_tx_frame, total,
254	                                                  USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_FLAGS_DATA_COMPLETE);
255	    if (r != USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT_OK)
256	    {
257	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
258	        return;
259	    }
```

#ifndef PERF_LOG_RX_H
#define PERF_LOG_RX_H

#include <stdint.h>

/* Host→device command framer. Symmetric with the TX framer in
 * perf_log_sink_cdc.c: SOF (0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56) + LEN(u16 LE) + payload
 * + CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE(u16 LE). On a complete, validated frame the
 * framer dispatches the command (currently only PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK)
 * by calling into perf_log.h. Bad magic / CRC / LEN bumps a drop
 * counter and resyncs on the next SOF byte.
 *
 * Fed from the CDC sink's USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE handler in
 * USB-ISR context. State is small (≤16 B framed payload for the sole
 * command today) and parsing is non-blocking — no task hand-off. */

void     PerfLogRx_Initialize(void);
void     PerfLogRx_Feed(const uint8_t *bytes, uint32_t len);
uint32_t PerfLogRx_GetDropCount(void);

#endif /* PERF_LOG_RX_H */

```

#include "perf_log_rx.h"
#include "perf_log.h"
#include "perf_log_records.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

/* Largest command frame today is perf_cmd_set_mask_t (8 B payload). The
 * buffer is sized to allow a small amount of growth without re-tuning. */
#define PL_RX_PAYLOAD_MAX  64u

typedef enum
{
    RX_WAIT_SOF_0 = 0,
    RX_WAIT_SOF_1,
    RX_WAIT_SOF_2,
    RX_WAIT_SOF_3,
    RX_READ_LEN_0,
    RX_READ_LEN_1,
    RX_READ_PAYLOAD,
    RX_READ_CRC_0,
    RX_READ_CRC_1,
} rx_state_t;

static rx_state_t s_state;
static uint16_t   s_len;
static uint16_t   s_payload_idx;
static uint8_t    s_payload[PL_RX_PAYLOAD_MAX];
static uint16_t   s_crc_calc;
static uint16_t   s_crc_rx;
static uint32_t   s_drops;

static uint16_t crc16_ccitt(uint16_t crc, uint8_t b)
{
    crc ^= (uint16_t)b << 8;
    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < 8u; i++)
    {
        crc = (crc & 0x8000u) ? (uint16_t)((crc << 1) ^ 0x1021u)
                              : (uint16_t)(crc << 1);
    }
    return crc;
}

static void reset(void)
{
    s_state       = RX_WAIT_SOF_0;
    s_len         = 0u;
    s_payload_idx = 0u;
    s_crc_calc    = 0xFFFFu;
    s_crc_rx      = 0u;
}

static void drop_and_reset(void)
{
    s_drops++;
    reset();
}

/* Resync helper: if we're past WAIT_SOF_0 and the byte we just rejected
 * happens to be the first SOF byte of a fresh frame, give it credit
 * rather than waiting another full frame for the sync window. */
static void resync(uint8_t b)
{
    drop_and_reset();
    if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_0)
    {
        s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_1;
    }
}

static void dispatch_payload(void)
{
    if (s_len < sizeof(perf_cmd_hdr_t)) { return; }

    perf_cmd_hdr_t hdr;
    memcpy(&hdr, s_payload, sizeof(hdr));
    if (hdr.magic != PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC) { return; }

    switch (hdr.cmd_id)
    {
        case PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK:
            if (s_len == sizeof(perf_cmd_set_mask_t))
            {
                perf_cmd_set_mask_t cmd;
                memcpy(&cmd, s_payload, sizeof(cmd));
                PerfLog_SetEnabledMask(cmd.enabled_mask);
            }
            break;

        default:
            break;
    }
}

void PerfLogRx_Initialize(void)
{
    reset();
    s_drops = 0u;
}

void PerfLogRx_Feed(const uint8_t *bytes, uint32_t len)
{
    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < len; i++)
    {
        uint8_t b = bytes[i];
        switch (s_state)
        {
            case RX_WAIT_SOF_0:
                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_0) { s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_1; }
                break;

            case RX_WAIT_SOF_1:
                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_1) { s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_2; }
                else                     { resync(b); }
                break;

            case RX_WAIT_SOF_2:
                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_2) { s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_3; }
                else                     { resync(b); }
                break;

            case RX_WAIT_SOF_3:
                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_3) { s_state = RX_READ_LEN_0; }
                else                     { resync(b); }
                break;

            case RX_READ_LEN_0:
                s_len      = b;
                s_crc_calc = crc16_ccitt(s_crc_calc, b);
                s_state    = RX_READ_LEN_1;
                break;

            case RX_READ_LEN_1:
                s_len     |= (uint16_t)b << 8;
                s_crc_calc = crc16_ccitt(s_crc_calc, b);
                if (s_len == 0u || s_len > PL_RX_PAYLOAD_MAX) { drop_and_reset(); }
                else                                          { s_state = RX_READ_PAYLOAD; }
                break;

            case RX_READ_PAYLOAD:
                s_payload[s_payload_idx++] = b;
                s_crc_calc = crc16_ccitt(s_crc_calc, b);
                if (s_payload_idx >= s_len) { s_state = RX_READ_CRC_0; }
                break;

            case RX_READ_CRC_0:
                s_crc_rx = b;
                s_state  = RX_READ_CRC_1;
                break;

            case RX_READ_CRC_1:
                s_crc_rx |= (uint16_t)b << 8;
                if (s_crc_rx == s_crc_calc) { dispatch_payload(); reset(); }
                else                        { drop_and_reset(); }
                break;

            default:
                drop_and_reset();
                break;
        }
    }
}

uint32_t PerfLogRx_GetDropCount(void)
{
    return s_drops;
}

```

1	"""Wire-frame parser for the perf-log USB CDC stream.
2	
3	Wire layout (mirrors firmware perf_log_sink_cdc.c:234-245):
4	
5	    SOF(4)  | LEN(u16 LE) | PAYLOAD(LEN bytes) | CRC(u16 LE)
6	
7	CRC is CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE computed over `LEN || PAYLOAD` (NOT including SOF).
8	
9	This module is purely byte-level. It does not understand record types — that's
10	decode.py's job. It exists to (a) resync after mid-stream join or byte loss,
11	(b) reject corrupt frames, and (c) yield validated payloads upward.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
17	from dataclasses import dataclass
18	
19	from .records import MAX_RECORD_BYTES, SOF_BYTES
20	
21	
22	# ─── CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
23	
24	_CRC_TABLE: list[int] = []
25	
26	
27	def _build_crc_table() -> list[int]:
28	    table: list[int] = []
29	    for byte in range(256):
30	        crc = byte << 8
31	        for _ in range(8):
32	            crc = ((crc << 1) ^ 0x1021) if (crc & 0x8000) else (crc << 1)
33	            crc &= 0xFFFF
34	        table.append(crc)
35	    return table
36	
37	
38	_CRC_TABLE = _build_crc_table()
39	
40	
41	def crc16_ccitt_false(data: bytes | memoryview, init: int = 0xFFFF) -> int:
42	    """CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE: poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflection, no xorout.
43	
44	    Mirrors firmware perf_log_sink_cdc.c:58-70 byte-for-byte.
45	    """
46	    crc = init
47	    for b in data:
48	        crc = ((crc << 8) ^ _CRC_TABLE[(crc >> 8) ^ b]) & 0xFFFF
49	    return crc
50	
51	
52	# ─── Frame iterator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
53	
54	
55	@dataclass(frozen=True)
56	class FrameBytes:
57	    """A successfully-parsed wire frame's payload + provenance."""
58	
59	    payload: bytes
60	    bytes_skipped_before: int  # diagnostic: bytes dropped resyncing to this frame
61	
62	
63	class FrameError(Exception):
64	    """Wire-level frame error (CRC mismatch, length out of range)."""
65	
66	
67	class FrameStats:
68	    """Mutable counters surfaced by `iter_frames` for the CLI."""
69	
70	    def __init__(self) -> None:
71	        self.frames_ok: int = 0
72	        self.bytes_resync_dropped: int = 0
73	        self.crc_mismatches: int = 0
74	        self.bad_lengths: int = 0
75	
76	
77	def iter_frames(
78	    chunks: Iterable[bytes],
79	    stats: FrameStats | None = None,
80	) -> Iterator[FrameBytes]:
81	    """Consume an iterable of byte chunks, yield validated frame payloads.
82	
83	    The iterator handles arbitrary chunk boundaries (a frame may straddle as
84	    many chunks as it likes), resyncs on the 4-byte SOF after byte loss, and
85	    drops frames whose CRC does not match. Counters are accumulated into
86	    `stats` if supplied.
87	    """
88	    if stats is None:
89	        stats = FrameStats()
90	
91	    buf = bytearray()
92	    skipped_since_last_ok = 0
93	
94	    for chunk in chunks:
95	        if not chunk:
96	            continue
97	        buf.extend(chunk)
98	
99	        while True:
100	            sof_idx = buf.find(SOF_BYTES)
101	            if sof_idx < 0:
102	                # No SOF in buffer. Drop everything but the last 3 bytes (a
103	                # SOF could still be straddling the boundary).
104	                if len(buf) > 3:
105	                    skipped_since_last_ok += len(buf) - 3
106	                    stats.bytes_resync_dropped += len(buf) - 3
107	                    del buf[: len(buf) - 3]
108	                break
109	
110	            if sof_idx > 0:
111	                skipped_since_last_ok += sof_idx
112	                stats.bytes_resync_dropped += sof_idx
113	                del buf[:sof_idx]
114	
115	            # buf now starts with SOF. Need 4 (SOF) + 2 (LEN) before we can
116	            # bound the frame.
117	            if len(buf) < 6:
118	                break
119	
120	            length = buf[4] | (buf[5] << 8)
121	
122	            # Sanity-bound the length. A bogus LEN (e.g. mid-payload bytes
123	            # that happened to align with SOF) will trip this; treat the SOF
124	            # as a false positive and step past it.
125	            if length < 16 or length > MAX_RECORD_BYTES:
126	                stats.bad_lengths += 1
127	                skipped_since_last_ok += 1
128	                stats.bytes_resync_dropped += 1
129	                del buf[0]
130	                continue
131	
132	            total = 6 + length + 2
133	            if len(buf) < total:
134	                break
135	
136	            payload = bytes(buf[6 : 6 + length])
137	            crc_observed = buf[6 + length] | (buf[6 + length + 1] << 8)
138	            crc_expected = crc16_ccitt_false(buf[4 : 6 + length])
139	
140	            if crc_observed != crc_expected:
141	                # Bad CRC. Likely a false-positive SOF in the middle of an
142	                # earlier frame; step past one byte and rescan.
143	                stats.crc_mismatches += 1
144	                skipped_since_last_ok += 1
145	                stats.bytes_resync_dropped += 1
146	                del buf[0]
147	                continue
148	
149	            # Good frame — consume it from the buffer and yield.
150	            del buf[:total]
151	            stats.frames_ok += 1
152	            yield FrameBytes(
153	                payload=payload,
154	                bytes_skipped_before=skipped_since_last_ok,
155	            )
156	            skipped_since_last_ok = 0
157

```text
1	"""Byte sources feeding `framing.iter_frames`.
2	
3	Each source is an iterable of `bytes` chunks. Chunk size is not load-bearing —
4	the framer handles arbitrary boundaries.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
10	from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
11	from pathlib import Path
12	from typing import BinaryIO
13	
14	
15	# ─── File source ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
16	
17	
18	class FileSource(AbstractContextManager["FileSource"]):
19	    """Iterate over fixed-size chunks from a captured `.bin` file."""
20	
21	    def __init__(self, path: str | Path, chunk_bytes: int = 64 * 1024) -> None:
22	        self.path = Path(path)
23	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
24	        self._fh: BinaryIO | None = None
25	
26	    def __enter__(self) -> "FileSource":
27	        self._fh = self.path.open("rb")
28	        return self
29	
30	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
31	        if self._fh is not None:
32	            self._fh.close()
33	            self._fh = None
34	
35	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
36	        if self._fh is None:
37	            raise RuntimeError("FileSource must be used as a context manager")
38	        while True:
39	            chunk = self._fh.read(self.chunk_bytes)
40	            if not chunk:
41	                return
42	            yield chunk
43	
44	
45	# ─── Serial source ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
46	
47	
48	class SerialSource(AbstractContextManager["SerialSource"]):
49	    """Read bytes from the marvin USB-device CDC ACM port via pyserial.
50	
51	    The firmware sink is DTR-gated (`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:216`); pyserial raises
52	    DTR by default on open, which triggers the firmware to re-emit a SESSION
53	    record. CDC ACM ignores baud rate; we still pass one because pyserial
54	    requires it.
55	    """
56	
57	    def __init__(
58	        self,
59	        port: str,
60	        *,
61	        baudrate: int = 921600,
62	        chunk_bytes: int = 4096,
63	        read_timeout_s: float = 0.1,
64	    ) -> None:
65	        self.port = port
66	        self.baudrate = baudrate
67	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
68	        self.read_timeout_s = read_timeout_s
69	        self._ser: object | None = None
70	
71	    def __enter__(self) -> "SerialSource":
72	        # Imported lazily so file-only workflows do not require pyserial.
73	        import serial  # noqa: WPS433  (intentional lazy import)
74	
75	        self._ser = serial.Serial(
76	            port=self.port,
77	            baudrate=self.baudrate,
78	            timeout=self.read_timeout_s,
79	            dsrdtr=False,
80	        )
81	        # Make DTR explicit — some platforms default it off.
82	        try:
83	            self._ser.dtr = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
84	        except (OSError, AttributeError):
85	            pass
86	        return self
87	
88	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
89	        if self._ser is not None:
90	            try:
91	                self._ser.close()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
92	            finally:
93	                self._ser = None
94	
95	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
96	        if self._ser is None:
97	            raise RuntimeError("SerialSource must be used as a context manager")
98	        ser = self._ser
99	        while True:
100	            # `read` with timeout returns whatever has arrived (possibly empty
101	            # on timeout). `in_waiting` lets us drain the OS buffer in one go
102	            # when bytes are already queued.
103	            n = max(1, getattr(ser, "in_waiting", 0))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
104	            chunk: bytes = ser.read(min(n, self.chunk_bytes))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
105	            if chunk:
106	                yield chunk
107	
108	
109	# ─── Tee — passthrough source that also records to disk ──────────────────────
110	
111	
112	class TeeSource(AbstractContextManager["TeeSource"]):
113	    """Wrap any byte source so every chunk is also appended to a file.
114	
115	    Used by `marvin-perf live --also-record FILE` so a single live session
116	    yields both inline decode output and a `.bin` capture for later
117	    summarize/replay.
118	    """
119	
120	    def __init__(
121	        self,
122	        upstream: Iterable[bytes] | AbstractContextManager[Iterable[bytes]],
123	        out_path: str | Path,
124	    ) -> None:
125	        self.upstream = upstream
126	        self.out_path = Path(out_path)
127	        self._fh: BinaryIO | None = None
128	
129	    def __enter__(self) -> "TeeSource":
130	        self._fh = self.out_path.open("wb")
131	        if isinstance(self.upstream, AbstractContextManager):
132	            self.upstream.__enter__()
133	        return self
134	
135	    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None:
136	        try:
137	            if isinstance(self.upstream, AbstractContextManager):
138	                self.upstream.__exit__(exc_type, exc, tb)
139	        finally:
140	            if self._fh is not None:
141	                self._fh.close()
142	                self._fh = None
143	
144	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
145	        if self._fh is None:
146	            raise RuntimeError("TeeSource must be used as a context manager")
147	        for chunk in self.upstream:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
148	            self._fh.write(chunk)
149	            self._fh.flush()
150	            yield chunk
151

345	        print("\n--- stack high-water (StackType_t words free) ---")
346	        for series in sorted(hwm.values(), key=lambda s: s.task_id):
347	            samples = series.samples
348	            print(
349	                f"  {series.task_name:<16}  n={len(samples):>4}  "
350	                f"min={series.min_words}  last={samples[-1][1] if samples else '—'}"
351	            )
352	
353	    # Warnings.
354	    warns = check_frame_epoch_monotonic(records) + check_video_publish_cadence(
355	        records, timer_freq_hz
356	    )
357	    if warns:
358	        print("\n--- warnings ---")
359	        for w in warns[:50]:
360	            print(f"  [{w.kind}] {w.message}")
361	        if len(warns) > 50:
362	            print(f"  …and {len(warns) - 50} more")
363	    return 0
364	
365	
366	# ─── Argparse wiring ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
367	
368	
369	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
370	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
371	        prog="marvin-perf",
372	        description="Decode and analyze marvin firmware perf-log streams.",
373	    )
374	    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
375	
376	    p_live = sub.add_parser("live", help="Live decode from a USB-CDC serial port.")
377	    p_live.add_argument("--port", required=True, help="Serial port (e.g. /dev/cu.usbmodem...)")
378	    p_live.add_argument("--also-record", help="Optionally also write raw bytes to FILE")
379	    p_live.set_defaults(func=cmd_live)
380	
381	    p_record = sub.add_parser("record", help="Capture raw bytes (no decode).")
382	    p_record.add_argument("--port", required=True)
383	    p_record.add_argument("--out", help="Write a bare .bin (legacy)")
384	    p_record.add_argument("--out-dir", help="Write a capture directory (perf.bin + manifest.json)")
385	    p_record.set_defaults(func=cmd_record)
386	
387	    p_decode = sub.add_parser(
388	        "decode", help="Pretty-print every record in a capture (.bin or directory)."
389	    )
390	    p_decode.add_argument("path")
391	    p_decode.set_defaults(func=cmd_decode)
392	
393	    p_summary = sub.add_parser(
394	        "summarize", help="Run analysis pass over a capture (.bin or directory)."
395	    )
396	    p_summary.add_argument("path")
397	    p_summary.set_defaults(func=cmd_summarize)
398	
399	    p_serve = sub.add_parser(
400	        "serve", help="Run the visual review server (requires viewer dep group)."
401	    )
402	    p_serve.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
403	    p_serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8765)
404	    p_serve.add_argument(
405	        "--capture",
406	        help="Optional capture path (directory or .bin) to pre-load on startup.",
407	    )
408	    p_serve.set_defaults(func=cmd_serve)
409	
410	    return p
411	
412	
413	def cmd_serve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
414	    try:
415	        from .web.server import run as run_server
416	    except ImportError as e:
417	        print(
418	            "marvin-perf serve requires the 'viewer' dep group.\n"
419	            "  uv sync --group viewer\n"
420	            f"  (import error: {e})",
421	            file=sys.stderr,
422	        )
423	        return 2
424	    return run_server(host=args.host, port=args.port, capture=args.capture)
425	
426	
427	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
428	    parser = build_parser()
429	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
430	    return args.func(args)
431	
432	
433	if __name__ == "__main__":
434	    sys.exit(main())
435

32	    frame = wrap_frame(build_session_payload())

"""CLI argument parsing — record-type mask spec resolution."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

import pytest

from marvin_perf.cli import parse_types_arg
from marvin_perf.records import RecordType


def test_types_none_returns_none() -> None:
    assert parse_types_arg(None) is None


def test_types_flag_parses() -> None:
    mask = parse_types_arg("STAMP,SESSION")
    assert mask == (1 << RecordType.SESSION) | (1 << RecordType.STAMP)


def test_types_case_insensitive_and_whitespace() -> None:
    assert parse_types_arg("stamp, session") == parse_types_arg("STAMP,SESSION")


def test_types_all_token() -> None:
    assert parse_types_arg("ALL") == 0xFFFFFFFF


def test_types_min_token() -> None:
    expected = (1 << RecordType.SESSION) | (1 << RecordType.DROP)
    assert parse_types_arg("MIN") == expected


def test_types_min_combines_with_more() -> None:
    expected = (1 << RecordType.SESSION) | (1 << RecordType.DROP) | (1 << RecordType.STAMP)
    assert parse_types_arg("MIN,STAMP") == expected


def test_types_unknown_raises() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(argparse.ArgumentTypeError):
        parse_types_arg("BOGUS")

```

Easy/Medium/Hard place notes higher up the highway with longer travel time, so the same 220 ms may strike too early. Defer until the game-state controller (spec §4.8) lands and difficulty is known to marvin — until then, expert-tuned 220 ms is the working default.

139	
140	### 2026-05-22 — USB CDC bandwidth headroom + state-queue starvation diagnosis
141	
142	End-to-end strip viewer is up and rendering after the user adjusted strip dimensions in [`cv_marvin_v1.c:341-347`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L341-L347) to sensing 185×16 @ (265, 310) and strike 290×20 @ (212, 395). At those dimensions current device→host load is **1.88 MB/s** (≈8.9 KB sensing + ≈17.4 KB strike per frame × 60 Hz + ~25 KB/s state pipeline + ~80 B/frame record overhead) — the link badge is green and `dropped_strip`/`dropped_sink` are flat. But we were dropping at slightly higher dimensions just before this, so our practical CDC-ACM ceiling is < 5 MB/s on this firmware build today. Two concrete things came out of investigating that:
143	
144	**(1) Where the bandwidth is actually going.** The USB-HS bulk-IN theoretical ceiling on UDPHS is ~40-45 MB/s real-world; we're leaving ~85 % of it on the floor. The conservative 5 MB/s working number isn't a USB-HS limit — it's a software-pipeline limit specific to how the sink writes today. Five candidate levers, ranked by expected payoff:
145	
146	  1. **Pipeline writes** ([`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:251-267`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L251-L267)) — biggest single win, expect 2-3×. Today the sink owns a single staging buffer and pends a `WRITE_COMPLETE` semaphore between writes, so the USB DMA sits idle for the round-trip. The CDC write-queue depth is already 3 (`USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED = 3U` in [`configuration.h:243`](../default/src/config/default/configuration.h#L243)) so multi-buffer queueing is supported by the layers below — the sink just doesn't use it. Move to a 2- or 3-deep ring of staging buffers; submit the next write as soon as the previous returns to the queue, not when it completes.
147	  2. **Hardware CRC via CRCCU** — soft CRC at [`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:58-70`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L58-L70) burns ~14 % of CPU at the current rate (byte-at-a-time over every framed payload). CRCCU peripheral does CCITT-FALSE in DMA. Frees CPU for whatever the next bottleneck turns out to be; not a bandwidth knob in itself, but it's the cheapest path to free headroom.
148	  3. **Combine sensing+strike into one wire frame** — saves ~80 B framing overhead per ISC frame (×60 Hz = 4.8 KB/s, ~5-15 % of state-pipeline payload). Small but free if the schema accommodates it; revisit only if (1) and (2) aren't enough.
149	  4. **Move bulk-IN from EP3 → EP2** — UDPHS only exposes 3-bank FIFO depth on EP1-2 ([`drv_usb_udphs_local.h:159`](../default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_local.h#L159) `DRV_USB_UDPHS_EPT_BK = 0x00060000`); EP3-7 are 2-bank only. The current bulk-IN is on EP3 ([`usb_device_init_data.c:213-220`](../default/src/config/default/usb_device_init_data.c#L213-L220)). 3-bank lets the controller pre-load three packets ahead of the host IN tokens; smooths out scheduler micro-stalls. Marginal win unless we're already pipelining at the software layer (so do this *after* lever 1).
150	  5. **Eliminate one memcpy** (architectural) — strip producer copies pixel rows out of the ISC frame into a queue slot, drain task copies that slot bytes onto the wire. Could be reduced to one copy if the strip producer wrote into a sink-owned ring directly, at the cost of tighter coupling between perf_log and the sink. Defer; the ratio of CPU spent in memcpy vs CRC favors lever 2 first.
151	
152	  **What's *not* the bottleneck:** the `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE = 2` knob in [`configuration.h:255`](../default/src/config/default/configuration.h#L255) (multiples of 64 KB, so 128 KB cap). Our largest single record is the 23 KB strip — 5× under the cap. Bumping this to 4 or 8 changes nothing about today's behavior. Documented here because it was the first knob the user noticed and it's tempting to try; save the time.
153	
154	**(2) HWM + RUNTIME records are absent from captures because the state queue is full.** Decoded a 24 s capture — zero `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` and zero `PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME` records, but `dropped_state since_session = 17188` (~707 dropped/s). Producers are wired and the drain task is calling them every second; the records hit a full queue and get counted as drops instead. Root cause: all state-pipeline records share `s_state_q` ([`perf_log.c:50-52`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c#L50-L52), `PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH = 128`). The 60 Hz × multiple-stage STAMP traffic — especially fretboard_link's `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` and `FBL_SEND` pair, which fire on every actuator wire byte — bursts faster than the drain can pull, the queue stays near full, and the once-per-second HWM/RUNTIME emits land on a full queue. Three candidate fixes:
155	
156	  1. **Bump `PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH` from 128 to 1024.** Cheapest. 128 × 32 B/slot = 4 KB today → 32 KB after; static BSS, no malloc. Probably enough on its own — the drain isn't *behind*, it's just unable to absorb burst peaks at 128 slots. Try first.
157	  2. **Give HWM/RUNTIME a dedicated low-pressure queue** drained on the same 1 Hz tick as DROP. Decouples the slow analytics path from the fast stamp path entirely; HWM/RUNTIME can never lose to a stamp burst. More plumbing (second queue + second drain branch) but it's the right shape long-term — and natural alongside lever 1 above (pipelining the sink) since the drain task changes anyway.
158	  3. **Throttle the high-rate stamp producers** — e.g. drop `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` to 1-in-N, or roll FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE into a single record. Loses information from the timeline; do this only if (1) and (2) both fail.
159	
160	  Going to start with (1) since it's a single `#define` change and HWM is the most useful "is something about to overflow its stack" signal — we want it back before any of the bandwidth-lever work begins, since stack pressure is exactly the kind of thing that surfaces while we're refactoring the sink.
161	
162	Neither finding is being acted on in this session — captured here so the analysis survives context.
163	
164	### 2026-05-22 — Phase 2 perf-log: schema v2 (STRIP + TASK_RUNTIME) wired
165	
166	Schema bump landed end-to-end. Firmware emits the two new record types; host decoder, analyzer, and viewer read them.
167	
168	**Schema v2.** [`perf_log_records.h`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h) bumps `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 2. `PERF_REC_PATCH (0x05)` is replaced by `PERF_REC_STRIP (0x05)` — variable-length BGR888 region tagged by `perf_strip_kind_t` (SENSING=0, STRIP=1; 256 codes available). `PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME (0x08)` adds per-task state/priority/`ulRunTimeCounter` snapshots. Both mirrored on the host in [`records.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py); `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 21:27:25Z)**_

No. The web server is offline-only today — it loads a capture directory or `.bin` and serves review endpoints (manifest / summary / records / strip / health / rtos). Live streaming + recording from the web UI is explicitly Phase 2 ([api.py:3-4](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/api.py#L3-L4) says so), and the plan we just landed deferred it.

If you want live + record now, it's the CLI:
- `marvin-perf live --port … [--also-record FILE] [--types …]`
- `marvin-perf record --port … --out-dir … [--types …]`

Adding it to the web UI would mean: a serial-reader thread inside `server.py` feeding `iter_frames`, a WebSocket route in `api.py` pushing decoded records as JSON, and a "Live" tab in the static frontend. Not hard, but it's a separate piece of work — want me to plan it?

```text
"""FastAPI app composition + uvicorn entry. Imported lazily by cli.py."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from . import api


STATIC_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "static"


def build_app() -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(
        title="marvin-perf viewer",
        description="Visual review for marvin firmware perf-log captures.",
        version="0.1.0",
    )
    app.include_router(api.router)

    if STATIC_DIR.exists():
        app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=STATIC_DIR), name="static")

        @app.get("/")
        def root_index() -> FileResponse:
            return FileResponse(STATIC_DIR / "index.html")

    return app


def run(*, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 8765, capture: str | None = None) -> int:
    import uvicorn

    if capture:
        api._preload(capture)

    uvicorn.run(build_app(), host=host, port=port, log_level="info")
    return 0
```

"""FastAPI routes — thin wrapper over the pure decode/analyze/render stack.

Phase 1 covers offline review: open / manifest / summary / records / strip /
health / rtos. Live WebSocket + serial-reader thread land in Phase 2.

Capture loading is memoized by (resolved-path, mtime) so re-opening the same
capture is a hash lookup. The pump that walks `perf.bin` once and indexes
records by `frame_epoch` lives in `_LoadedCapture` so the per-request endpoints
can be O(1) lookups against pre-built dicts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query
from fastapi.responses import Response
from pydantic import BaseModel

from ..analyze import (
    SchemaVersionMismatch,
    check_frame_epoch_monotonic,
    check_schema,
    check_video_publish_cadence,
    compute_drops,
    compute_hwm,
    compute_latencies,
    find_session,
)
from ..capture import Capture, Manifest, open_capture
from ..decode import Record, decode_record
from ..framing import FrameStats, iter_frames
from ..records import (
    Drop,
    Session,
    Stage,
    Stamp,
    Strip,
    TaskHighwater,
    TaskId,
    TaskRuntime,
    TaskState,
)
from ..transport import FileSource
from .render import StripRenderError, render_strip_png


# ─── Loaded-capture model ────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@dataclass
class _LoadedCapture:
    """A capture pulled fully into memory + lookup indexes.

    Phase-1 captures are MB-scale (state-only at ~9 KB/s × minutes). Strips
    arrive in Phase 2 and bump that to ~10 MB/min, still comfortable to keep
    in RAM for the offline-review use case.
    """

    capture: Capture
    records: list[Record]
    framing_stats: FrameStats
    by_epoch: dict[int, list[int]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # epoch → record indexes

    @property
    def manifest(self) -> Manifest:
        return self.capture.manifest

    @property
    def timer_freq_hz(self) -> int:
        s = find_session(self.records)
        return s.timer_freq_hz if s else 0

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> "_LoadedCapture":
        capture = open_capture(path)
        records: list[Record] = []
        stats = FrameStats()
        with FileSource(capture.bin_path) as src:
            for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
                try:
                    records.append(decode_record(frame.payload))
                except Exception:
                    continue

        by_epoch: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
        for i, rec in enumerate(records):
            ep = rec.hdr.frame_epoch  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            by_epoch[ep].append(i)

        return cls(
            capture=capture,
            records=records,
            framing_stats=stats,
            by_epoch=dict(by_epoch),
        )


class _Registry:
    """Module-level cache: (resolved-path, mtime) → _LoadedCapture."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._by_id: dict[str, _LoadedCapture] = {}

    def open(self, path: str | Path) -> tuple[str, _LoadedCapture]:
        p = Path(path).resolve()
        # Use the bin's mtime so editing manifest.json doesn't force a reload,
        # but appending bytes (live capture, future) does.
        bin_path = p / "perf.bin" if p.is_dir() else p
        mtime = bin_path.stat().st_mtime if bin_path.exists() else 0.0
        capture_id = f"{p}@{mtime}"
        loaded = self._by_id.get(capture_id)
        if loaded is None:
            loaded = _LoadedCapture.load(p)
            self._by_id[capture_id] = loaded
        return capture_id, loaded

# ─── Pydantic request/response models ────────────────────────────────────────


class OpenRequest(BaseModel):
    path: str


class OpenResponse(BaseModel):
    capture_id: str
    manifest: dict[str, Any]


# ─── Routes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


router = APIRouter(prefix="/api")


@router.post("/capture/open", response_model=OpenResponse)
def capture_open(req: OpenRequest) -> OpenResponse:
    try:
        capture_id, loaded = _REGISTRY.open(req.path)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        raise HTTPException(404, str(e))
    return OpenResponse(capture_id=capture_id, manifest=loaded.manifest.to_dict())


@router.get("/preloaded")
def preloaded() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Capture loaded by `serve --capture PATH`. Returns null id if none."""
    if _PRELOADED_ID is None:
        return {"capture_id": None, "manifest": None}
    loaded = _REGISTRY.get(_PRELOADED_ID)
    return {"capture_id": _PRELOADED_ID, "manifest": loaded.manifest.to_dict()}


@router.get("/capture/{capture_id:path}/manifest")
def capture_manifest(capture_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return _REGISTRY.get(capture_id).manifest.to_dict()


@router.get("/capture/{capture_id:path}/summary")
def capture_summary(capture_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    loaded = _REGISTRY.get(capture_id)
    session = find_session(loaded.records)
    try:
        check_schema(session)
        schema_ok = True
        schema_msg = None
    except SchemaVersionMismatch as e:
        schema_ok = False
        schema_msg = str(e)

    timer_freq_hz = loaded.timer_freq_hz
    drops = compute_drops(loaded.records)
    hwm = compute_hwm(loaded.records)
    latencies = compute_latencies(loaded.records, timer_freq_hz)
    warns = check_frame_epoch_monotonic(loaded.records) + check_video_publish_cadence(
        loaded.records, timer_freq_hz
    )

    type_counts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)

async function loadCapture(captureId, manifest) {
  setBanner("Loading…");
  state.captureId = captureId;
  state.manifest = manifest;

  const enc = encodeURIComponent(captureId);
  const [summary, health, rtos, recs] = await Promise.all([
    api(`/api/capture/${enc}/summary`),
    api(`/api/capture/${enc}/health`),
    api(`/api/capture/${enc}/rtos`),
    api(`/api/capture/${enc}/records?limit=100000`),
  ]);
  state.summary = summary;
  state.health = health;
  state.rtos = rtos;
  state.records = recs.records;
  state.timerFreqHz = summary.timer_freq_hz || 0;
  state.ts0 = state.records.length ? state.records[0].ts_counter : 0;
  state.playheadTs = state.ts0;

  indexByKind();
  renderManifestBanner();
  renderInspector();
  renderBadges();
  renderTimeline();
  renderRtosPanel();
  renderStripSlots();

  setBanner("");

## Findings Report: Live Streaming + WebSocket Architecture for marvin-perf Viewer

### 1. FastAPI/WebSocket Dependency Posture

**pyproject.toml (lines 17–22):**
- `fastapi>=0.115` and `uvicorn[standard]>=0.32` are both pinned in the `[viewer]` optional group
- `uvicorn[standard]` explicitly includes `websockets` support (the extra installs `websockets` and `wsproto`)
- `pyserial>=3.5` is a **core dependency** (line 7), not optional — it's always available
- FastAPI's WebSocket is built in; no additional import needed beyond what's already required

**✓ Ready for WebSocket:** The stack is already wired for async WS. No additional deps required.

---

### 2. Capture-Write API Surface

**capture.py:**

- **`init_capture_dir(dir_path, *, exist_ok=False) → Path`** (lines 210–222)
  - Creates directory with `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=exist_ok)`
  - Returns absolute `Path` to the created dir
  - Does NOT write `manifest.json`

- **`finalize_capture_dir(dir_path, *, source, captured_at=None) → Manifest`** (lines 225–238)
  - Scans `perf.bin` at `dir_path / BIN_NAME` (where `BIN_NAME = "perf.bin"`)
  - Calls `synthesize_manifest(bin_path, source=source, captured_at=...)` which:
    - Walks **the entire bin** with `iter_frames` + `decode_record` (lines 127–148)
    - Returns `Manifest` dataclass with `n_records`, schema version, timers, epoch bounds
  - Writes manifest to `dir_path / "manifest.json"`
  - Returns the manifest
  - Does NOT require a records list; reads the bin directly

- **Canonical example: `cli.py:cmd_record()` (lines 258–306)**
  - Line 270: `cap_dir = init_capture_dir(args.out_dir, exist_ok=False)`
  - Line 281: Opens `ser` context, then loops `for chunk in ser:` → `fh.write(chunk)`
  - Line 297–300: Calls `finalize_capture_dir(cap_dir, source=CaptureSource(...))` after closing the bin file
  - ✓ This is the exact flow to mirror for live append

**Note:** `finalize_capture_dir` re-parses the **entire** bin every time (no incremental index), so for live streaming, you'll want a separate incremental indexing layer (not baked into finalize).

---

### 3. Frontend FSM and Rendering Pipeline

**state.fsm lifecycle (app.js lines 32–47, transitions at 587–616):**
- Transitions: `idle → loaded` (on successful capture load, line 128)
- From `loaded`: `togglePlay()` flips between `playing ↔ paused` (lines 614–616)
- No "live" or "stream" state defined
- RAF loop driven from `play()` (line 591): calls `requestAnimationFrame(tick)` with delta-wall-time integration
- Playhead advances via `state.playheadTs` update in tick; stops when `newTs >= last` (line 598)

**Records indexing (lines 141–150 `indexByKind()`):**
- Assumption: **all records loaded once at `loadCapture()` time**
- `state.byKind[kind]` = sorted array of records by `ts_counter`
- **No incremental-append seams wired** — `indexByKind()` rebuilds entire dict from `state.records` each call
- To support live append: would need to call `indexByKind()` on each new batch of records OR patch the dict incrementally
- Strip rendering uses `nearestAtOrBefore(recs, state.playheadTs)` binary search (lines 183–192) — compatible with append

**render\*() callers (line 131–137 in `loadCapture()`):**
- `renderManifestBanner()`, `renderInspector()`, `renderBadges()`, `renderTimeline()`, `renderRtosPanel()`, `renderStripSlots()`, `updatePlayheadDisplay()`
- All assume static data after load; timeline and rtos charts use Plotly and would need `.relayout()` or `.extendTraces()` calls for live updates

**No "live" or "stream" references found** in app.js (grep confirmed no matches).

---

### 4. Existing Offline Routes — URL Shapes and Response Shapes

**From api.py:**

| Route | Method | Returns | Params |
|-------|--------|---------|--------|
| `/api/capture/open` | POST | `{ capture_id, manifest }` | `{ path }` |
| `/api/preloaded` | GET | `{ capture_id, manifest }` | — |
| `/api/capture/{capture_id}/manifest` | GET | manifest dict | — |
| `/api/capture/{capture_id}/summary` | GET | `{ schema_ok, timer_freq_hz, framing, record_type_counts, drops, hwm, latencies, warnings }` | — |
| `/api/capture/{capture_id}/records` | GET | `{ records, limit, offset, returned }` | `from`, `to`, `types`, `limit`, `offset` |
| `/api/capture/{capture_id}/strip/{epoch}/{kind}.png` | GET | PNG bytes | — |
| `/api/capture/{capture_id}/health` | GET | `{ framing, drops_since_session, drops_max_delta, strip_rate_per_s, ... }` | — |
| `/api/capture/{capture_id}/rtos` | GET | `{ tasks, totals }` | — |

**Naming pattern:** `/api/capture/{id}/{resource}`. Path IDs are capture `capture_id` which is `"{resolved_path}@{mtime}"`.

**Suggested live sibling routes:**
- `/api/live/start` — POST to open serial + capture dir
- `/api/live/stop` — POST to close and finalize
- `/api/live/set-mask` — POST to send type-mask command
- `/api/live/ws` — WebSocket to stream decoded records as they arrive

---

### 5. Potential GIL / Threading / Asyncio Conflicts

**asyncio/threading scan results:**
- **No `async def` route handlers** in api.py (all sync)
- **No `asyncio` imports** anywhere in the codebase
- **No `threading` imports** anywhere in the codebase
- **All routes are CPU-bound or I/O-bound via context managers** (FileSource, SerialSource)

**Blocker assessment:**
- ✓ No pre-existing asyncio event loop to conflict with
- ✓ No pre-existing threads
- ✓ FastAPI is async-native but routes can safely call sync I/O (will be run in a thread pool by uvicorn automatically)
- ✓ SerialSource uses pyserial with blocking reads + timeout — ideal for a background thread
- ⚠ **GIL consideration:** The background thread's serial reads won't block the main asyncio loop (different threads), and decode work (CPU-bound) will be GIL-tied but uvicorn's default worker pool is sufficient

**No conflicts found.** Your plan to spawn one `threading.Thread` running `SerialSource.__iter__` + `iter_frames` → `asyncio.Queue` is clean and should work without modification to existing code.

---

## Punch List

1. **WebSocket deps:** Ready. `uvicorn[standard]` already brings `websockets`.
2. **Capture write flow:** `init_capture_dir() → write loop → finalize_capture_dir()` is canonical; finalize re-parses the whole bin (not incremental).
3. **Frontend FSM:** `idle → loaded → playing/paused`. No live state; RAF loop advances playhead. `state.records` and `state.byKind` are fully loaded and static; no incremental-append hooks exist (would need new code).
4. **Route naming:** Follow `/api/capture/{id}/...` pattern; live siblings should use `/api/live/...` prefix to keep scope clear.
5. **Threading safety:** No asyncio or threading in place; background thread + `asyncio.Queue` to FastAPI route is safe and idiomatic.

158	# ─── Type-mask CLI parsing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

160	
161	def parse_types_arg(spec: str | None) -> int | None:
162	    """Resolve a `--types` spec to a u32 mask. Returns None if `spec` is None.
163	
164	    Accepts a comma-separated list of RecordType names plus the special tokens
165	    `ALL` (0xFFFFFFFF) and `MIN` (SESSION|DROP). Case-insensitive.
166	    """
167	    if spec is None:
168	        return None
169	    mask = 0
170	    for raw in spec.split(","):
171	        token = raw.strip().upper()
172	        if not token:
173	            continue
174	        if token == "ALL":
175	            return TYPE_MASK_ALL
176	        if token == "MIN":
177	            mask |= TYPE_MASK_MIN
178	            continue
179	        if token not in RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME:
180	            valid = ", ".join(sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME))
181	            raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
182	                f"unknown record type {token!r}; valid: {valid}, ALL, MIN"
183	            )
184	        mask |= 1 << RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME[token]
185	    return mask
186	
187	
188	def _types_help() -> str:
189	    bit_lines = ", ".join(
190	        f"{name}={int(rt)}" for name, rt in sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME.items())
191	    )
192	    return (
193	        "Comma-separated record types to enable on the device. "
194	        f"Names: {bit_lines}. Special: ALL (default), MIN (SESSION+DROP). "
195	        "SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask. Old firmware ignores the command."
196	    )

208	def cmd_live(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
209	    stats = FrameStats()
210	    mask = parse_types_arg(args.types)
211	
212	    serial_src = SerialSource(args.port)
213	    if args.also_record:
214	        with serial_src as ser, TeeSource(ser, args.also_record) as tee:
215	            if mask is not None:
216	                _send_mask(ser, mask)
217	            return _live_loop(_decode_stream(tee, stats), stats)
218	    else:
219	        with serial_src as ser:
220	            if mask is not None:
221	                _send_mask(ser, mask)
222	            return _live_loop(_decode_stream(ser, stats), stats)

225	def _live_loop(records: Iterator[Record], stats: FrameStats) -> int:
226	    last_status = time.monotonic()
227	    record_count = 0
228	    drop_records = 0
229	    drop_baseline = _DropBaseline()
230	    for rec in records:
231	        record_count += 1
232	        if isinstance(rec, Drop):
233	            drop_records += 1
234	        print(_format_record(rec, drop_baseline=drop_baseline))
235	        now = time.monotonic()
236	        if (now - last_status) >= 1.0:
237	            print(
238	                f"  [status] frames={stats.frames_ok} resync_drop={stats.bytes_resync_dropped} "
239	                f"crc_err={stats.crc_mismatches} drop_recs={drop_records}",
240	                file=sys.stderr,
241	                flush=True,
242	            )
243	            last_status = now
244	    return 0

261	    Two modes: `--out FILE.bin` writes a raw legacy file; `--out-dir DIR`
262	    writes a capture directory (DIR/perf.bin + manifest.json finalized on
263	    close).
264	    """
265	    if (args.out is None) == (args.out_dir is None):
266	        print("record: exactly one of --out or --out-dir is required", file=sys.stderr)
267	        return 2
268	
269	    if args.out_dir is not None:
270	        cap_dir = init_capture_dir(args.out_dir, exist_ok=False)
271	        bin_path = cap_dir / BIN_NAME
272	        label = f"capture {cap_dir.name}/"
273	    else:
274	        cap_dir = None
275	        bin_path = Path(args.out)
276	        label = f"recording {bin_path.name}"
277	
278	    mask = parse_types_arg(args.types)

281	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser, bin_path.open("wb") as fh:

292	                    last_status = now

433	    p_live.add_argument("--port", required=True, help="Serial port (e.g. /dev/cu.usbmodem...)")
434	    p_live.add_argument("--also-record", help="Optionally also write raw bytes to FILE")

442	    p_record.add_argument("--types", help=_types_help())
443	    p_record.set_defaults(func=cmd_record)

448	    )

450	    p_set_mask.add_argument("--types", required=True, help=_types_help())
451	    p_set_mask.set_defaults(func=cmd_set_mask)
452

108	def synthesize_manifest(
109	    bin_path: Path,
110	    *,
111	    source: CaptureSource | None = None,
112	    captured_at: str | None = None,
113	) -> Manifest:
114	    """Scan a `perf.bin` end-to-end and derive a minimal manifest.
115	
116	    Used both to build the sidecar when finalizing a fresh capture and to give
117	    the viewer a usable manifest when opening a bare legacy `.bin`.
118	    """
119	    schema_version: int | None = None
120	    fw_git_short: int | None = None
121	    timer_freq_hz: int | None = None
122	    epoch_first: int | None = None
123	    epoch_last: int | None = None
124	    types: set[str] = set()
125	    n_records = 0
126	
127	    stats = FrameStats()
128	    with FileSource(bin_path) as src:
129	        for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
130	            try:
131	                rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
132	            except Exception:
133	                continue
134	            n_records += 1
135	            types.add(type(rec).__name__)
136	            if isinstance(rec, Session) and schema_version is None:
137	                schema_version = rec.schema_version
138	                fw_git_short = rec.fw_git_short
139	                timer_freq_hz = rec.timer_freq_hz
140	            # frame_epoch == 0 records (SESSION/DROP/TASK_HIGHWATER/TASK_RUNTIME)
141	            # are not frame-tied — skip them when bounding the epoch range.
142	            if isinstance(rec, (Session, Drop, TaskHighwater, TaskRuntime)):
143	                continue
144	            ep = rec.hdr.frame_epoch
145	            if epoch_first is None or ep < epoch_first:
146	                epoch_first = ep
147	            if epoch_last is None or ep > epoch_last:
148	                epoch_last = ep
149	
150	    return Manifest(
151	        schema_version=schema_version,
152	        fw_git_short=fw_git_short,
153	        timer_freq_hz=timer_freq_hz,
154	        captured_at=captured_at or _now_utc_iso(),
155	        host_user=_host_user(),
156	        source=source or CaptureSource(kind="file", file=str(bin_path)),
157	        frame_epoch_first=epoch_first,
158	        frame_epoch_last=epoch_last,
159	        producer_capabilities=sorted(types),
160	        n_records=n_records,
161	    )

164	def write_manifest(dir_path: Path, manifest: Manifest) -> Path:
165	    out = dir_path / MANIFEST_NAME
166	    out.write_text(json.dumps(manifest.to_dict(), indent=2) + "\n")
167	    return out

171	    return Manifest.from_dict(json.loads((dir_path / MANIFEST_NAME).read_text()))

184	def open_capture(path: str | Path) -> Capture:
185	    """Open a capture directory or a bare legacy `.bin` file.
186	
187	    For a directory, manifest.json is read if present; otherwise it is
188	    synthesized from the bin (and not written back). For a bare file, the
189	    manifest is always synthesized and the capture is flagged as legacy.
190	    """
191	    p = Path(path)
192	    if p.is_dir():
193	        bin_path = p / BIN_NAME
194	        if not bin_path.exists():
195	            raise FileNotFoundError(f"capture directory missing {BIN_NAME}: {p}")
196	        manifest_path = p / MANIFEST_NAME
197	        if manifest_path.exists():
198	            manifest = read_manifest(p)
199	        else:
200	            manifest = synthesize_manifest(bin_path)
201	        return Capture(path=p, bin_path=bin_path, manifest=manifest, is_legacy_bin=False)
202	    if p.is_file():
203	        manifest = synthesize_manifest(
204	            p, source=CaptureSource(kind="file", file=str(p))
205	        )
206	        return Capture(path=p.parent, bin_path=p, manifest=manifest, is_legacy_bin=True)
207	    raise FileNotFoundError(f"no such capture path: {p}")

209

211	    dir_path: str | Path,
212	    *,
213	    exist_ok: bool = False,

216	
217	    Returns the absolute directory path. `manifest.json` is not written here —
218	    it is finalized by `finalize_capture_dir` after the bin is closed.
219	    """
220	    p = Path(dir_path)

232	    p = Path(dir_path)
