394	def _record_to_dict(rec: Record) -> dict[str, Any]:
395	    """Compact, JSON-friendly view of a record. Avoid sending raw pixel bytes
396	    over JSON — strips travel out as PNG via the dedicated endpoint."""
397	    hdr = rec.hdr  # type: ignore[union-attr]
398	    base: dict[str, Any] = {
399	        "type": type(rec).__name__,
400	        "frame_epoch": hdr.frame_epoch,
401	        "ts_counter": hdr.ts_counter,
402	        "flags": hdr.flags,
403	    }
404	    if isinstance(rec, Session):
405	        base.update(
406	            timer_freq_hz=rec.timer_freq_hz,
407	            schema_version=rec.schema_version,
408	            fw_git_short=rec.fw_git_short,
409	        )
410	    elif isinstance(rec, Stamp):
411	        try:
412	            base["stage"] = Stage(rec.stage_id).name
413	        except ValueError:
414	            base["stage"] = f"stage_{rec.stage_id:#04x}"
415	        base["stage_id"] = rec.stage_id
416	        base["aux"] = rec.aux
417	    elif isinstance(rec, Drop):
418	        base.update(
419	            dropped_state=rec.dropped_state,
420	            dropped_strip=rec.dropped_strip,
421	            dropped_sink=rec.dropped_sink,
422	        )
423	    elif isinstance(rec, TaskHighwater):
424	        try:
425	            base["task_name"] = TaskId(rec.task_id).name
426	        except ValueError:
427	            base["task_name"] = f"task_{rec.task_id}"
428	        base["task_id"] = rec.task_id
429	        base["words"] = rec.words
430	    elif isinstance(rec, TaskRuntime):
431	        try:
432	            base["task_name"] = TaskId(rec.task_id).name
433	        except ValueError:
434	            base["task_name"] = f"task_{rec.task_id}"
435	        try:
436	            base["state_name"] = TaskState(rec.state).name
437	        except ValueError:
438	            base["state_name"] = f"state_{rec.state}"
439	        base["task_id"] = rec.task_id
440	        base["state"] = rec.state
441	        base["priority"] = rec.priority
442	        base["run_time_counter"] = rec.run_time_counter
443	    elif isinstance(rec, Strip):
444	        base.update(
445	            x=rec.x, y=rec.y, w=rec.w, h=rec.h,
446	            kind=rec.kind, kind_name=rec.kind_name,
447	        )
448	        # Pixels travel via the strip PNG endpoint — don't inline them.
449	    else:
450	        # Detector, Timing, UnknownRecord — keep generic field projection.
451	        for fname in getattr(rec, "__dataclass_fields__", {}):
452	            if fname == "hdr":

454	            v = getattr(rec, fname)

457	            elif isinstance(v, tuple):
458	                base[fname] = list(v)
459	            else:
460	                base[fname] = v
461	    return base

574	  if (!curRec) return;

576	  let candidate = null;
577	  for (const r of state.records) {
578	    if (r.frame_epoch === target) {
579	      if (dir > 0) { candidate = r; break; }
580	      else { candidate = r; }
581	    }
582	  }
583	  if (candidate) seekTo(candidate.ts_counter);

1	"""Byte sources feeding `framing.iter_frames`.
2	
3	Each source is an iterable of `bytes` chunks. Chunk size is not load-bearing —
4	the framer handles arbitrary boundaries.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
10	from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
11	from pathlib import Path
12	from typing import BinaryIO
13	
14	
15	# ─── File source ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
16	
17	
18	class FileSource(AbstractContextManager["FileSource"]):
19	    """Iterate over fixed-size chunks from a captured `.bin` file."""
20	
21	    def __init__(self, path: str | Path, chunk_bytes: int = 64 * 1024) -> None:
22	        self.path = Path(path)
23	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
24	        self._fh: BinaryIO | None = None
25	
26	    def __enter__(self) -> "FileSource":
27	        self._fh = self.path.open("rb")
28	        return self
29	
30	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
31	        if self._fh is not None:
32	            self._fh.close()
33	            self._fh = None
34	
35	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
36	        if self._fh is None:
37	            raise RuntimeError("FileSource must be used as a context manager")
38	        while True:
39	            chunk = self._fh.read(self.chunk_bytes)
40	            if not chunk:
41	                return
42	            yield chunk
43

45	# ─── Serial source ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
46	
47	
48	class SerialSource(AbstractContextManager["SerialSource"]):
49	    """Read bytes from the marvin USB-device CDC ACM port via pyserial.
50	
51	    The firmware sink is DTR-gated (`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:216`); pyserial raises
52	    DTR by default on open, which triggers the firmware to re-emit a SESSION
53	    record. CDC ACM ignores baud rate; we still pass one because pyserial
54	    requires it.
55	    """
56	
57	    def __init__(
58	        self,
59	        port: str,
60	        *,
61	        baudrate: int = 921600,
62	        chunk_bytes: int = 4096,
63	        read_timeout_s: float = 0.1,
64	    ) -> None:
65	        self.port = port
66	        self.baudrate = baudrate
67	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
68	        self.read_timeout_s = read_timeout_s
69	        self._ser: object | None = None
70	
71	    def __enter__(self) -> "SerialSource":
72	        # Imported lazily so file-only workflows do not require pyserial.
73	        import serial  # noqa: WPS433  (intentional lazy import)
74	
75	        self._ser = serial.Serial(
76	            port=self.port,
77	            baudrate=self.baudrate,
78	            timeout=self.read_timeout_s,
79	            dsrdtr=False,
80	        )
81	        # Make DTR explicit — some platforms default it off.
82	        try:
83	            self._ser.dtr = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
84	        except (OSError, AttributeError):
85	            pass
86	        return self
87	
88	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
89	        if self._ser is not None:
90	            try:
91	                self._ser.close()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
92	            finally:
93	                self._ser = None
94	
95	    def send_command(self, framed: bytes) -> int:
96	        """Write pre-framed command bytes to the device.
97	
98	        Caller frames via `framing.frame_encode`. Returns bytes written.
99	        """
100	        if self._ser is None:
101	            raise RuntimeError("SerialSource must be used as a context manager")
102	        return self._ser.write(framed)  # type: ignore[attr-defined,no-any-return]
103	
104	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
105	        if self._ser is None:
106	            raise RuntimeError("SerialSource must be used as a context manager")
107	        ser = self._ser
108	        while True:
109	            # `read` with timeout returns whatever has arrived (possibly empty
110	            # on timeout). `in_waiting` lets us drain the OS buffer in one go
111	            # when bytes are already queued.
112	            n = max(1, getattr(ser, "in_waiting", 0))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
113	            chunk: bytes = ser.read(min(n, self.chunk_bytes))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
114	            if chunk:
115	                yield chunk

118	# ─── Tee — passthrough source that also records to disk ──────────────────────
119	
120	
121	class TeeSource(AbstractContextManager["TeeSource"]):
122	    """Wrap any byte source so every chunk is also appended to a file.
123	
124	    Used by `marvin-perf live --also-record FILE` so a single live session
125	    yields both inline decode output and a `.bin` capture for later
126	    summarize/replay.
127	    """
128	
129	    def __init__(
130	        self,
131	        upstream: Iterable[bytes] | AbstractContextManager[Iterable[bytes]],
132	        out_path: str | Path,
133	    ) -> None:
134	        self.upstream = upstream
135	        self.out_path = Path(out_path)
136	        self._fh: BinaryIO | None = None
137	
138	    def __enter__(self) -> "TeeSource":
139	        self._fh = self.out_path.open("wb")
140	        if isinstance(self.upstream, AbstractContextManager):
141	            self.upstream.__enter__()
142	        return self
143	
144	    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None:
145	        try:
146	            if isinstance(self.upstream, AbstractContextManager):
147	                self.upstream.__exit__(exc_type, exc, tb)
148	        finally:
149	            if self._fh is not None:
150	                self._fh.close()
151	                self._fh = None
152	
153	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
154	        if self._fh is None:
155	            raise RuntimeError("TeeSource must be used as a context manager")
156	        for chunk in self.upstream:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
157	            self._fh.write(chunk)
158	            self._fh.flush()
159	            yield chunk

```text
"""Wire-frame parser for the perf-log USB CDC stream.

Wire layout (mirrors firmware perf_log_sink_cdc.c:234-245):

    SOF(4)  | LEN(u16 LE) | PAYLOAD(LEN bytes) | CRC(u16 LE)

CRC is CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE computed over `LEN || PAYLOAD` (NOT including SOF).

This module is purely byte-level. It does not understand record types — that's
decode.py's job. It exists to (a) resync after mid-stream join or byte loss,
(b) reject corrupt frames, and (c) yield validated payloads upward.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass

from .records import MAX_RECORD_BYTES, SOF_BYTES


# ─── CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_CRC_TABLE: list[int] = []


def _build_crc_table() -> list[int]:
    table: list[int] = []
    for byte in range(256):
        crc = byte << 8
        for _ in range(8):
            crc = ((crc << 1) ^ 0x1021) if (crc & 0x8000) else (crc << 1)
            crc &= 0xFFFF
        table.append(crc)
    return table


_CRC_TABLE = _build_crc_table()


def crc16_ccitt_false(data: bytes | memoryview, init: int = 0xFFFF) -> int:
    """CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE: poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflection, no xorout.

    Mirrors firmware perf_log_sink_cdc.c:58-70 byte-for-byte.
    """
    crc = init
    for b in data:
        crc = ((crc << 8) ^ _CRC_TABLE[(crc >> 8) ^ b]) & 0xFFFF
    return crc


def frame_encode(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    """SOF + LEN(u16LE) + payload + CRC16-CCITT-FALSE(u16LE).

    Mirror of the device-side framer; CRC covers LEN || PAYLOAD (not SOF).
    """
    length = len(payload)
    if length > 0xFFFF:
        raise ValueError(f"payload too large: {length} bytes")
    len_bytes = bytes((length & 0xFF, (length >> 8) & 0xFF))
    crc = crc16_ccitt_false(len_bytes + payload)
    crc_bytes = bytes((crc & 0xFF, (crc >> 8) & 0xFF))
    return SOF_BYTES + len_bytes + payload + crc_bytes


# ─── Frame iterator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FrameBytes:
    """A successfully-parsed wire frame's payload + provenance."""

    payload: bytes
    bytes_skipped_before: int  # diagnostic: bytes dropped resyncing to this frame


class FrameError(Exception):
    """Wire-level frame error (CRC mismatch, length out of range)."""


class FrameStats:
    """Mutable counters surfaced by `iter_frames` for the CLI."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.frames_ok: int = 0
        self.bytes_resync_dropped: int = 0
        self.crc_mismatches: int = 0
        self.bad_lengths: int = 0


def iter_frames(
    chunks: Iterable[bytes],
    stats: FrameStats | None = None,
) -> Iterator[FrameBytes]:
    """Consume an iterable of byte chunks, yield validated frame payloads.

    The iterator handles arbitrary chunk boundaries (a frame may straddle as
    many chunks as it likes), resyncs on the 4-byte SOF after byte loss, and
    drops frames whose CRC does not match. Counters are accumulated into
    `stats` if supplied.
```

### 2. Capture-Write API Surface

**capture.py:**

- **`init_capture_dir(dir_path, *, exist_ok=False) → Path`** (lines 210–222)
  - Creates directory with `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=exist_ok)`
  - Returns absolute `Path` to the created dir
  - Does NOT write `manifest.json`

- **`finalize_capture_dir(dir_path, *, source, captured_at=None) → Manifest`** (lines 225–238)
  - Scans `perf.bin` at `dir_path / BIN_NAME` (where `BIN_NAME = "perf.bin"`)
  - Calls `synthesize_manifest(bin_path, source=source, captured_at=...)` which:
    - Walks **the entire bin** with `iter_frames` + `decode_record` (lines 127–148)

  - Writes manifest to `dir_path / "manifest.json"`
  - Returns the manifest
  - Does NOT require a records list; reads the bin directly

- **Canonical example: `cli.py:cmd_record()` (lines 258–306)**
  - Line 270: `cap_dir = init_capture_dir(args.out_dir, exist_ok=False)`
  - Line 281: Opens `ser` context, then loops `for chunk in ser:` → `fh.write(chunk)`
  - Line 297–300: Calls `finalize_capture_dir(cap_dir, source=CaptureSource(...))` after closing the bin file
  - ✓ This is the exact flow to mirror for live append

**Note:** `finalize_capture_dir` re-parses the **entire** bin every time (no incremental index), so for live streaming, you'll want a separate incremental indexing layer (not baked into finalize).

**How should the live-mode in-browser record buffer behave?**

Options:
- **Sliding window (Recommended)** - Keep the last ~30 s of records in memory; older ones drop off the timeline. Bounded RAM, focused on recent activity. Long-term capture lives on disk via the Record button.
- **Unbounded, manual clear** - Append forever; add a Clear button to reset. Matches offline-review mental model exactly. Will eventually OOM the browser tab on a long session.

**When a Record session ends (Stop pressed or browser disconnects), should the capture dir be finalized automatically?**

Options:
- **Auto-finalize on stop (Recommended)** - Stop button writes manifest.json and the capture is immediately openable from offline mode. Browser disconnect = same as Stop.
- **Leave bin file unfinalized; finalize button** - Stop just closes the file. A separate Finalize button writes manifest.json. Useful if you want to discard a bad recording without paying the manifest synthesis cost.


**Answer:** Sliding window (Recommended), Auto-finalize on stop (Recommended)

# marvin-perf web viewer — live streaming + recording + mask toggling

## Context

The marvin-perf web viewer is offline-only today: it loads a `.bin` capture from disk and serves review endpoints (`summary` / `records` / `health` / `rtos` / `strip`). Iterating on firmware tuning currently requires three terminal moves per cycle: stop firmware, run `marvin-perf record …`, kill it after a few seconds, run `marvin-perf serve --capture …`, switch to the browser. That round-trip is expensive enough that the natural workflow is "tweak something, capture 30 s, walk away to look at it" — which is the wrong shape for the next round of tuning. The user wants the browser to be the single iteration surface: open a tab, see live records, flip record-type checkboxes to narrow what the device emits (host→device mask, just landed), hit Record when something is worth keeping.

Phase 2 of this viewer was always going to add a live mode (per the api.py:3-4 docstring). The host→device mask plumbing landed today (firmware filter + CLI `--types` + `set-mask`); the same `frame_encode` + `encode_set_mask_payload` + `SerialSource.send_command` primitives that the CLI uses can be wired behind a `POST /api/live/set-mask` route with no new wire-level concepts. Combined with a single background serial-reader thread feeding decoded records over a WebSocket, this puts the full iteration loop in one tab.

## Approach

### Architectural commitments

1. **Single-tenant live session.** One serial reader thread, one open `SerialSource`, one WebSocket peer at a time. Second WS connection gets a 4409 close code with reason `"live already in use"`. Avoids reasoning about multi-browser mask ownership. Trivial to relax later.

2. **Sliding-window in-browser buffer.** Frontend keeps the last ~30 s of records by `ts_counter` (configurable; default targets ~50k records max as a hard upper bound). Long-term captures live on disk via the Record button — exactly the same pattern as `cli.cmd_record`. This bounds RAM and keeps the timeline focused on recent activity.

3. **Auto-finalize on stop.** Stop / browser disconnect / serial error all flow through the same shutdown path that closes the bin file and calls `finalize_capture_dir`. The capture is immediately openable from offline mode. Mirrors `cli.cmd_record` precisely.

4. **Server-side decode, JSON over WS.** The WS pushes `_record_to_dict(rec)`-shaped records (the same projector the offline `/records` endpoint already uses, in api.py:394+). No new schema on the wire to the browser; no JS framer; existing `_record_to_dict` keeps the offline+live record shape identical, which means `state.byKind` indexing, timeline rendering, strip rendering all work unchanged on incoming-vs-loaded records.

5. **Background thread + asyncio.Queue.** One `threading.Thread` runs `SerialSource.__iter__` + `iter_frames` + `decode_record`. Each decoded record posts `(record_dict, raw_bytes_frame)` to a thread-safe queue (`janus.Queue` would be ideal, but pulling in a dep is overkill — use `asyncio.Queue` + `loop.call_soon_threadsafe` from the reader thread). The WS handler reads from the queue and forwards. Recording, when on, splits off in the reader thread: the framed raw bytes get appended to the bin file before the decoded form goes to the queue. Splitting raw-write off from decode-and-push means a viewer that's slow to drain doesn't slow disk writes (and disk writes that block momentarily don't slow the WS push beyond one tick).

6. **No new transport behavior in the CLI module.** Everything live-mode needs is already in `transport.SerialSource` (`__iter__`, `send_command`, DTR-on-enter), `framing.iter_frames` + `frame_encode`, `records.encode_set_mask_payload`, `capture.init_capture_dir` + `finalize_capture_dir`. The web layer composes these — no new transport-level abstractions, no duplication of CLI logic.

7. **REST for control, WS for stream.** Mask sets, record start, record stop are all idempotent control-plane operations: `POST /api/live/set-mask`, `POST /api/live/record/start`, `POST /api/live/record/stop`. Doing them over the WS would require an ad-hoc command/response framing inside the JSON channel, which adds nothing — REST is the simpler shape for one-shot RPCs, and lets the user issue them from `curl` for scripting. Pure data flow stays on the WS.

### Wire shape (server → browser)

WS endpoint: `WebSocket /api/live/ws`. After accept, server sends one `hello` message:
\```json
{ "type": "hello",
  "session": { "started_at": "<iso8601>", "port": "/dev/cu.usbmodem...", "mask": "0xffffffff", "recording": null } }
\```
Then a stream of:
\```json
{ "type": "record", "rec": <_record_to_dict(rec)> }
{ "type": "session_replay", "rec": <Session record dict> }   // re-sent on reconnect or device re-attach
{ "type": "framing_stats", "frames_ok": N, "crc_err": N, "resync_drop": N }   // 1 Hz
{ "type": "recording", "state": "started"|"stopped",
  "capture_dir": "...", "bytes_written": N, "n_records": N }
{ "type": "mask", "value": "0x...", "source": "client"|"server" }
{ "type": "error", "code": "serial-disconnect"|"frame-error"|..., "msg": "..." }
\```
Browser sends nothing over WS — all control via REST. Keeps the WS state machine trivial.

### REST control plane (new)

All under `/api/live/`. Body shapes are minimal — the live session is process-singleton, no `live_id`s.

- `GET  /api/live/status` → `{ "active": bool, "port": str|null, "mask": "0x...", "recording": {"capture_dir": str, "bytes_written": int}|null, "started_at": iso|null }`
- `POST /api/live/start` body `{ "port": "/dev/cu.usbmodem..." }` — opens `SerialSource`, spawns reader thread. 409 if already active.
- `POST /api/live/stop` — closes serial, joins thread, finalizes any active recording. Idempotent.
- `POST /api/live/set-mask` body `{ "mask": int }` *or* `{ "types": ["STAMP","SESSION",...] }` — frames + writes via `SerialSource.send_command`. Echoes back `{"mask": "0x..."}` with the resolved value. Re-uses `cli.parse_types_arg` for the names path.
- `POST /api/live/record/start` body `{ "out_dir": "captures/foo" }` — calls `init_capture_dir(out_dir, exist_ok=False)`, opens `perf.bin` for append, flips a flag in the reader thread that mirrors raw frame bytes to disk. 409 if already recording.
- `POST /api/live/record/stop` — flushes + closes bin, calls `finalize_capture_dir` with `CaptureSource(kind="serial", port=…)`. Returns the manifest. Idempotent.
- `GET  /api/serial/ports` → `[{ "device": "/dev/cu.usbmodem...", "description": "..." }]` via `serial.tools.list_ports.comports()`. Lets the UI drive port selection without copy-paste.

### Server-side internals

New `web/live.py` module owning all the live state. One module-level `_LiveSession` singleton, mutex-guarded. Public functions:

\```python
def start(port: str, *, app_loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop) -> None: ...
def stop() -> None: ...                            # idempotent
def set_mask_from_int(mask: int) -> int: ...       # returns resolved
def set_mask_from_names(names: list[str]) -> int: ...   # uses cli.parse_types_arg
def record_start(out_dir: str | Path) -> Path: ... # returns capture_dir
def record_stop() -> Manifest: ...                 # idempotent
def status() -> dict: ...
def attach_ws(ws: WebSocket) -> None: ...          # single-peer; rejects if already attached
\```

The reader thread loop:
\```
with SerialSource(port) as ser:
    for frame in iter_frames(ser, framing_stats):
        if recording: bin_fh.write(reframe(frame.payload))   # see note
        try:
            rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
        except Exception:
            continue
        loop.call_soon_threadsafe(queue.put_nowait, ("record", _record_to_dict(rec)))
\```

**Note on raw-byte recording.** `iter_frames` already strips the SOF/LEN/CRC and yields just the payload. To write a re-readable `.bin`, we need either (a) capture chunks pre-framing (hook `SerialSource.__iter__` directly and tee bytes), or (b) re-frame the validated payload via `frame_encode(payload)` before write. Option (a) writes garbage during resync (everything `iter_frames` rejects); option (b) writes a clean stream that's strictly the validated frames. **Going with (b)** — the captured `.bin` should be openable by the offline viewer without resync drops. We pay one extra CRC compute per frame on the recording path; negligible at the rates in question. Open the bin with `open(..., "wb", buffering=0)`; flush every record so a kill-switch leaves a usable file.

**Reframing actually needs a small refactor.** The reader thread has `frame.payload` but not the original framed bytes. Adding `iter_frames` to optionally yield `(payload, framed_bytes)` is the cleanest path — make `FrameBytes` carry the original bytes (already builds them up in `buf`), and recording writes `frame.framed`. **This is a one-field addition to `FrameBytes` and a one-line `bytes(...)` slice in the yield path; no behavior change for existing callers.**

The existing `transport.TeeSource` is *almost* the right shape but tees raw chunks (including resync garbage), so it doesn't match the design above. Skip it for live.

### Frontend changes

Three concrete changes to the existing single-page app:

1. **New "Mode" toggle in the toolbar header** — radio-style "Offline" / "Live". Offline keeps the existing path-input + Open button. Live shows: a port `<select>` populated from `/api/serial/ports`, a Start/Stop button, a recording-status pill, a Record/Stop button, and a record-types panel.

2. **Record-types panel** — eight checkboxes (one per `RecordType`, SESSION pinned-on and disabled because the firmware always emits it), plus ALL/MIN preset buttons. Initial state mirrors `0xFFFFFFFF`. Any change debounces 200 ms, then `POST /api/live/set-mask` with the selected names. The server reply updates the displayed mask string.

3. **State machine extension** — add `state.fsm` value `"live"`. Live mode disables the prev/next/play-pause transport buttons (no playhead-driven seeking — playhead always sits at "now"). Records arriving over the WS go through the same `state.records` array via a new `appendRecord(rec)` helper that keeps the array sliced to the last 30 s by `ts_counter`. After append, call a debounced `redraw()` that refreshes the timeline (Plotly `extendTraces` for the new points, plus a `relayout` to slide the x-window) and re-runs `renderInspector()` against the latest record. `state.byKind` rebuilds via the existing `indexByKind()` after each batch — at 50k cap it's fast enough; only revisit if profiling says otherwise.

The existing strip-rendering pipeline (`nearestAtOrBefore` + `/api/capture/.../strip/{epoch}/{kind}.png`) does **not** work in live mode because there's no `capture_id` and no on-disk PNG endpoint. **For live, render strips client-side** from the BGR bytes that already arrive in the record JSON via `_record_to_dict(rec)`. (Check: today's `_record_to_dict` strips the `bgr` payload — it would need to include it for live. Make it conditional via a `include_bgr` flag and pass `True` from the WS push.) Use a tiny canvas helper that takes a `Uint8Array` of BGR, swaps to RGBA, `putImageData`s into the existing `<canvas>` element. This keeps strips working end-to-end in live mode without round-tripping through a server PNG endpoint.

WS lifecycle: open on Live-Start, close on Live-Stop. Auto-reconnect on transient disconnect (1 s backoff up to 5 s). On reconnect the server replays the latest Session record so the timer-freq stays bound on the client.

### Phasing

- **Phase 1 — backend live + mask, no recording UI.** `web/live.py`, the `/api/live/{start,stop,set-mask,status,ws}` routes, `/api/serial/ports`, `FrameBytes.framed` field. End-to-end smoke: `curl POST /api/live/start` → connect to `/api/live/ws` with `websocat` → `curl POST /api/live/set-mask` → see record stream change. No frontend yet.
- **Phase 2 — frontend live mode + mask checkboxes.** Mode toggle, port select, Start/Stop, types panel, sliding-window record append, timeline live update, client-side strip render. Skip Record button.
- **Phase 3 — recording.** `record/start` + `record/stop` routes, frontend Record button + status pill. Auto-finalize on stop / disconnect / serial error.

Three landable PRs; each phase leaves the tool more useful than before.

### Verification

- **Backend unit tests** (`uv run pytest tools/marvin-perf/tests/`):
  - `test_live.py::test_start_then_stop_releases_thread` — start with a fake `SerialSource` (a context-manager iterator over a `list[bytes]`), stop, assert thread joined and resources released.
  - `test_live.py::test_set_mask_round_trips_to_serial_send` — patch `SerialSource.send_command` to record bytes, call `set_mask_from_names(["STAMP","SESSION"])`, assert the serial.write payload decodes back to mask `0x06` via `frame_encode`/`iter_frames`.
  - `test_live.py::test_record_start_stop_finalizes_capture` — stub serial source emitting one Session + a few Stamp frames, run start→record/start→record/stop→stop, assert resulting `manifest.json` has `n_records == expected`.
  - `test_framing.py::test_iter_frames_yields_framed_bytes` — assert `FrameBytes.framed` round-trips through `iter_frames` again.
- **End-to-end (with hardware)**:
  - `marvin-perf serve --port 8765`, open browser, click Live, pick the port, click Start. See records stream. Toggle off STRIP/DETECTOR/TIMING — visually confirm only STAMP/SESSION/DROP/HIGHWATER/RUNTIME continue. Click Record, pick `captures/web-live-test`, wait 10 s, click Stop. Confirm `marvin-perf summarize captures/web-live-test/` reports the expected types and zero `dropped_state`.
  - Disconnect device mid-stream → UI shows error pill, recording auto-finalizes, capture is openable in offline mode.
  - Two browser tabs at `/api/live/ws` → second one rejected with the close code 4409.
- **Backward compatibility**: offline `/api/capture/open` flow unchanged; existing test suite passes; `marvin-perf serve --capture FILE` still preloads as before. The Mode toggle defaults to whichever mode matches the startup state (`--capture` → Offline, no capture → Live empty).

# marvin-perf web viewer — live streaming + recording + mask toggling

## Context

The marvin-perf web viewer is offline-only today: it loads a `.bin` capture from disk and serves review endpoints (`summary` / `records` / `health` / `rtos` / `strip`). Iterating on firmware tuning currently requires three terminal moves per cycle — stop firmware, run `marvin-perf record …`, kill it after a few seconds, run `marvin-perf serve --capture …`, switch to the browser. That round-trip is expensive enough that the natural workflow becomes "tweak something, capture, walk away to look at it." That's the wrong shape for the next round of tuning. The user wants the browser to be the single iteration surface: open a tab, see live records, flip record-type checkboxes to narrow what the device emits (host→device mask, just landed), hit Record when something is worth keeping.

Phase 2 of this viewer was always going to add a live mode (per the api.py:3-4 docstring). The host→device mask plumbing landed today (firmware filter + CLI `--types` + `set-mask`); the same `frame_encode` + `encode_set_mask_payload` + `SerialSource.send_command` primitives that the CLI uses can be wired behind a `POST /api/live/set-mask` route with no new wire-level concepts. Combined with a single background serial-reader thread feeding decoded records over a WebSocket, this puts the full iteration loop in one tab.

## Approach

### Architectural commitments

1. **Single-tenant live session.** One serial reader thread, one open `SerialSource`, one WebSocket peer at a time. A second WS connection gets a 4409 close code with reason `"live already in use"`. Avoids reasoning about multi-browser mask ownership. Trivial to relax later.

2. **Sliding-window in-browser buffer.** Frontend keeps the last ~30 s of records by `ts_counter` (target ~50k records max as a hard upper bound). Long-term captures live on disk via the Record button — exactly the same pattern as `cli.cmd_record`. Bounds RAM, keeps the timeline focused on recent activity.

3. **Auto-finalize on stop.** Stop / browser disconnect / serial error all flow through the same shutdown path that closes the bin file and calls `finalize_capture_dir`. The capture is immediately openable from offline mode. Mirrors `cli.cmd_record` precisely.

4. **Server-side decode, JSON over WS.** The WS pushes `_record_to_dict(rec)`-shaped records (the same projector the offline `/records` endpoint uses, in api.py:394+). No new schema on the wire to the browser; no JS framer; existing `_record_to_dict` keeps the offline+live record shape identical, which means `state.byKind` indexing, timeline rendering, and strip rendering all work unchanged on incoming-vs-loaded records.

5. **Background thread + asyncio.Queue.** One `threading.Thread` runs `SerialSource.__iter__` + `iter_frames` + `decode_record`. Each decoded record posts to a `asyncio.Queue` via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe(queue.put_nowait, …)`. The WS handler reads from the queue and forwards. When recording is active, the reader thread also writes the validated framed bytes to disk before pushing — slow viewer ≠ slow disk writes; momentary disk stall ≠ delayed WS push beyond one tick.

6. **No new transport behavior in the CLI module.** Everything live-mode needs is already in `transport.SerialSource` (`__iter__`, `send_command`, DTR-on-enter), `framing.iter_frames` + `frame_encode`, `records.encode_set_mask_payload`, `capture.init_capture_dir` + `finalize_capture_dir`. The web layer composes these — no new transport-level abstractions, no duplication of CLI logic. `cli.parse_types_arg` is reused for the mask-by-names code path.

7. **REST for control, WS for stream.** Mask sets, record start/stop are idempotent control-plane operations: `POST /api/live/set-mask`, `POST /api/live/record/start`, `POST /api/live/record/stop`. Doing them over the WS would require an ad-hoc command/response framing inside the JSON channel, which adds nothing — REST is the simpler shape for one-shot RPCs and lets the user issue them from `curl` for scripting. Pure data flow stays on the WS; browser sends nothing over WS.

### Wire shape (server → browser)

`WebSocket /api/live/ws`. After accept, server sends one `hello`, then a stream of typed messages:

\```json
{ "type": "hello",
  "session": { "started_at": "<iso8601>", "port": "/dev/cu.usbmodem...",
               "mask": "0xffffffff", "recording": null } }

{ "type": "record",         "rec": <_record_to_dict(rec) including bgr in live mode> }
{ "type": "session_replay", "rec": <Session record dict> }   // re-sent on reconnect
{ "type": "framing_stats",  "frames_ok": N, "crc_err": N, "resync_drop": N }   // 1 Hz
{ "type": "recording",      "state": "started"|"stopped",
                            "capture_dir": "...", "bytes_written": N, "n_records": N }
{ "type": "mask",           "value": "0x...", "source": "client"|"server" }
{ "type": "error",          "code": "serial-disconnect"|"frame-error"|..., "msg": "..." }
\```

### REST control plane (new)

All under `/api/live/`. Body shapes are minimal — the live session is a process-singleton, no `live_id`s.

- `GET  /api/live/status` → `{ active, port, mask, recording: {capture_dir, bytes_written}|null, started_at }`
- `POST /api/live/start`     body `{ port }` — opens `SerialSource`, spawns reader thread. 409 if already active.
- `POST /api/live/stop`      — closes serial, joins thread, finalizes any active recording. Idempotent.
- `POST /api/live/set-mask`  body `{ mask }` *or* `{ types: ["STAMP","SESSION",...] }`. Frames + writes via `SerialSource.send_command`. Echoes the resolved value.
- `POST /api/live/record/start` body `{ out_dir }` — calls `init_capture_dir(out_dir, exist_ok=False)`, opens `perf.bin` for append, flips a flag in the reader thread that mirrors raw frame bytes to disk. 409 if already recording.
- `POST /api/live/record/stop`  — flushes + closes bin, calls `finalize_capture_dir(CaptureSource(kind="serial", port=…))`. Returns the manifest. Idempotent.
- `GET  /api/serial/ports` → `[{ device, description }]` via `serial.tools.list_ports.comports()`. Drives the UI port-select dropdown.

### Server-side internals

New `web/live.py` module owning all live state behind a single mutex-guarded `_LiveSession` singleton. Public functions:

\```
start(port, *, app_loop)        stop()                     # idempotent
set_mask_from_int(mask) -> int  set_mask_from_names(names) -> int
record_start(out_dir) -> Path   record_stop() -> Manifest  # idempotent
status() -> dict                attach_ws(ws)              # single-peer; rejects if already attached
\```

Reader-thread loop (pseudocode):
\```
with SerialSource(port) as ser:
    for frame in iter_frames(ser, framing_stats):
        if recording:
            bin_fh.write(frame.framed); bin_fh.flush()
        try:
            rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
        except Exception:
            continue
        loop.call_soon_threadsafe(
            queue.put_nowait, ("record", _record_to_dict(rec, include_bgr=True))
        )
\```

**Raw-byte recording detail.** `iter_frames` strips SOF/LEN/CRC and yields just the payload. To write a re-readable `.bin` we either (a) tee chunks pre-framing — but that captures resync garbage too — or (b) re-frame the validated payload via `frame_encode` before write. Going with (b): the captured bin is strictly validated frames, which means offline open is clean. Cost: one extra CRC compute per recorded frame; negligible at these rates. Better: have `iter_frames` carry the original framed bytes through — they're already buffered in `buf[:total]` before the slice copy. **Add a `framed: bytes` field to `FrameBytes` and a one-line `bytes(buf[:total])` capture before `del buf[:total]`** (framing.py:150). One-field addition; existing callers ignore it. The reader thread writes `frame.framed` directly when recording.

The existing `transport.TeeSource` is *almost* the right shape but tees raw chunks (resync garbage included), so it doesn't match the design. Skip it for live.

### Frontend changes

Three concrete changes to the existing single-page app:

1. **Mode toggle in the toolbar header** — radio-style "Offline" / "Live". Offline keeps existing path-input + Open button. Live shows: a port `<select>` populated from `/api/serial/ports`, a Start/Stop button, a mask string display, a record-types panel, and a Record/Stop button with a recording-status pill.

2. **Record-types panel** — eight checkboxes (one per `RecordType`, SESSION pinned-on and disabled because firmware always emits it), plus ALL/MIN preset buttons. Initial state mirrors `0xFFFFFFFF`. Any change debounces 200 ms then `POST /api/live/set-mask` with the selected names. Server reply updates the displayed mask string.

3. **State machine extension** — add `state.fsm = "live"`. Live mode disables prev/next/play-pause transport (no playhead-driven seeking — playhead is always "now"). Records arriving over WS go through a new `appendRecord(rec)` helper that pushes onto `state.records` and slices to the last 30 s by `ts_counter`. After append, a debounced `redraw()` refreshes the timeline (Plotly `extendTraces` for new points + `relayout` to slide the x-window) and re-runs `renderInspector()` against the latest record. `state.byKind` rebuilds via the existing `indexByKind()` after each batch — at the 50k cap it's fast enough; revisit only if profiling says otherwise.

The existing strip-rendering pipeline (`nearestAtOrBefore` + `/api/capture/.../strip/{epoch}/{kind}.png`) does **not** work in live mode — there's no `capture_id`, no on-disk PNG. **For live, render strips client-side** from the BGR bytes in the WS-pushed record. `_record_to_dict` today omits the `bgr` payload (a separate PNG endpoint serves the offline view); add an `include_bgr` parameter and pass `True` from the WS push. Frontend: tiny canvas helper takes a `Uint8Array` of BGR, swaps to RGBA, `putImageData`s into the existing strip `<canvas>`. Strips work end-to-end in live without a server PNG endpoint.

WS lifecycle: open on Live-Start, close on Live-Stop. Auto-reconnect on transient disconnect (1 s backoff up to 5 s). On reconnect the server replays the latest Session record so timer-freq stays bound on the client.

### Phasing

- **Phase 1 — backend live + mask, no recording UI.** `web/live.py`, `/api/live/{start,stop,set-mask,status,ws}`, `/api/serial/ports`, `FrameBytes.framed` field. Smoke: `curl POST /api/live/start` → connect to `/api/live/ws` with `websocat` → `curl POST /api/live/set-mask` → see record stream change. No frontend yet.
- **Phase 2 — frontend live mode + mask checkboxes.** Mode toggle, port select, Start/Stop, types panel, sliding-window record append, timeline live update, client-side strip render. No Record button yet.
- **Phase 3 — recording.** `record/start` + `record/stop` routes, frontend Record button + status pill. Auto-finalize on stop / disconnect / serial error.

Three landable PRs; each phase leaves the tool more useful than before.

### Verification

- **Backend unit tests** (`uv run pytest tools/marvin-perf/tests/`):
  - `test_live.py::test_start_then_stop_releases_thread` — start with a fake `SerialSource` (a context-manager iterator over a `list[bytes]`), stop, assert thread joined and resources released.
  - `test_live.py::test_set_mask_round_trips_to_serial_send` — patch `SerialSource.send_command` to record bytes; call `set_mask_from_names(["STAMP","SESSION"])`; assert the captured payload decodes back to mask `0x06` via `iter_frames`.
  - `test_live.py::test_record_start_stop_finalizes_capture` — stub serial source emits Session + a few Stamp frames; run start → record/start → record/stop → stop; assert resulting `manifest.json` has `n_records == expected`.
  - `test_framing.py::test_iter_frames_yields_framed_bytes` — assert `FrameBytes.framed` round-trips through `iter_frames` again.
- **End-to-end with hardware**:
  - `marvin-perf serve --port 8765`, open browser, click Live, pick the port, click Start. Records stream. Toggle off STRIP/DETECTOR/TIMING — visually confirm only STAMP/SESSION/DROP/HIGHWATER/RUNTIME continue. Click Record, point at `captures/web-live-test`, wait 10 s, click Stop. Confirm `marvin-perf summarize captures/web-live-test/` reports the expected types and zero `dropped_state`.
  - Disconnect device mid-stream → UI shows error pill, recording auto-finalizes, capture is openable in offline mode.
  - Two browser tabs at `/api/live/ws` → second one rejected with close code 4409.
- **Backward compatibility**: offline `/api/capture/open` flow unchanged; existing 83-test suite passes; `marvin-perf serve --capture FILE` still preloads as before. Mode toggle defaults to whichever mode matches startup state (`--capture` → Offline, no capture → Live empty).

### Critical files

To create:
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py` — `_LiveSession` singleton, reader thread, REST handler implementations
- `tools/marvin-perf/tests/test_live.py` — unit tests for live module

To update:
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/api.py` — register `/api/live/*` routes; conditional `include_bgr` flag in `_record_to_dict` (api.py:394+)

- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/static/app.js` — `state.fsm = "live"` branch, `appendRecord` with sliding window, WS open/close + reconnect, debounced `redraw`, client-side strip canvas helper

3. **State machine extension** — add `state.fsm = "live"`. Live mode disables prev/next/play-pause transport (no playhead-driven seeking — playhead is always "now"). Records arriving over WS go through a new `appendRecord(rec)` helper that pushes onto `state.records` and slices to the last 30 s by `ts_counter`. After append, a debounced `redraw()` refreshes the timeline (Plotly `extendTraces` for new points + `relayout` to slide the x-window) and re-runs `renderInspector()` against the latest record. `state.byKind` rebuilds via the existing `indexByKind()` after each batch — at the 50k cap it's fast enough; revisit only if profiling says otherwise.

The existing strip-rendering pipeline (`nearestAtOrBefore` + `/api/capture/.../strip/{epoch}/{kind}.png`) does **not** work in live mode — there's no `capture_id`, no on-disk PNG. **For live, render strips client-side** from the BGR bytes in the WS-pushed record. `_record_to_dict` today omits the `bgr` payload (a separate PNG endpoint serves the offline view); add an `include_bgr` parameter and pass `True` from the WS push. Frontend: tiny canvas helper takes a `Uint8Array` of BGR, swaps to RGBA, `putImageData`s into the existing strip `<canvas>`. Strips work end-to-end in live without a server PNG endpoint.

WS lifecycle: open on Live-Start, close on Live-Stop. Auto-reconnect on transient disconnect (1 s backoff up to 5 s). On reconnect the server replays the latest Session record so timer-freq stays bound on the client.

### Phasing

- **Phase 1 — backend live + mask, no recording UI.** `web/live.py`, `/api/live/{start,stop,set-mask,status,ws}`, `/api/serial/ports`, `FrameBytes.framed` field. Smoke: `curl POST /api/live/start` → connect to `/api/live/ws` with `websocat` → `curl POST /api/live/set-mask` → see record stream change. No frontend yet.
- **Phase 2 — frontend live mode + mask checkboxes.** Mode toggle, port select, Start/Stop, types panel, sliding-window record append, timeline live update, client-side strip render. No Record button yet.
- **Phase 3 — recording.** `record/start` + `record/stop` routes, frontend Record button + status pill. Auto-finalize on stop / disconnect / serial error.

Three landable PRs; each phase leaves the tool more useful than before.

### Verification

- **Backend unit tests** (`uv run pytest tools/marvin-perf/tests/`):
  - `test_live.py::test_start_then_stop_releases_thread` — start with a fake `SerialSource` (a context-manager iterator over a `list[bytes]`), stop, assert thread joined and resources released.
  - `test_live.py::test_set_mask_round_trips_to_serial_send` — patch `SerialSource.send_command` to record bytes; call `set_mask_from_names(["STAMP","SESSION"])`; assert the captured payload decodes back to mask `0x06` via `iter_frames`.
  - `test_live.py::test_record_start_stop_finalizes_capture` — stub serial source emits Session + a few Stamp frames; run start → record/start → record/stop → stop; assert resulting `manifest.json` has `n_records == expected`.
  - `test_framing.py::test_iter_frames_yields_framed_bytes` — assert `FrameBytes.framed` round-trips through `iter_frames` again.
- **End-to-end with hardware**:
  - `marvin-perf serve --port 8765`, open browser, click Live, pick the port, click Start. Records stream. Toggle off STRIP/DETECTOR/TIMING — visually confirm only STAMP/SESSION/DROP/HIGHWATER/RUNTIME continue. Click Record, point at `captures/web-live-test`, wait 10 s, click Stop. Confirm `marvin-perf summarize captures/web-live-test/` reports the expected types and zero `dropped_state`.
  - Disconnect device mid-stream → UI shows error pill, recording auto-finalizes, capture is openable in offline mode.
  - Two browser tabs at `/api/live/ws` → second one rejected with close code 4409.
- **Backward compatibility**: offline `/api/capture/open` flow unchanged; existing 83-test suite passes; `marvin-perf serve --capture FILE` still preloads as before. Mode toggle defaults to whichever mode matches startup state (`--capture` → Offline, no capture → Live empty).

### Critical files

To create:
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py` — `_LiveSession` singleton, reader thread, REST handler implementations
- `tools/marvin-perf/tests/test_live.py` — unit tests for live module

To update:
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/api.py` — register `/api/live/*` routes; conditional `include_bgr` flag in `_record_to_dict` (api.py:394+)
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/server.py` — make the asyncio loop accessible to `live.py` (capture inside the WS handler is sufficient — no module change needed if we grab it on first WS connect)
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/static/index.html` — Mode toggle, port `<select>`, Live controls section, types-panel checkboxes
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/static/app.js` — `state.fsm = "live"` branch, `appendRecord` with sliding window, WS open/close + reconnect, debounced `redraw`, client-side strip canvas helper
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/static/styles.css` — record-types panel layout, recording-status pill, mode toggle
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/framing.py` — `FrameBytes` adds `framed: bytes` field; `iter_frames` populates it from the same buffer slice it already constructs (framing.py:150)
- `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` — session-log entry on landing each phase

To reference (read-only):
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/cli.py:cmd_record` — canonical record-write loop to mirror
- `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/cli.py:parse_types_arg` — mask-name resolution; reuse from `live.py`

### Out of scope

- Multi-tenant live sessions (separate `live_id`, multiple browsers viewing one device). Single-peer is enough; revisit if a use case appears.
- Resumable / appendable recordings. Each Record press is a fresh capture dir.
- Persisting mask state across server restarts. Mask is RAM-only on both sides; host re-sends on attach.
- Server-side strip PNG endpoint for live mode. Client-side canvas render is the right answer when bytes already arrive in the WS message.
- Replaying a recording back through the WS as if it were live. Useful for UI testing but not on the iteration critical path.
- Discoverable host→device commands beyond SET_TYPE_MASK. Framer accommodates more; nothing else needed today.

# ─── Record → JSON ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _record_to_dict(rec: Record) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compact, JSON-friendly view of a record. Avoid sending raw pixel bytes
    over JSON — strips travel out as PNG via the dedicated endpoint."""
    hdr = rec.hdr  # type: ignore[union-attr]
    base: dict[str, Any] = {
        "type": type(rec).__name__,
        "frame_epoch": hdr.frame_epoch,
        "ts_counter": hdr.ts_counter,
        "flags": hdr.flags,
    }
    if isinstance(rec, Session):
        base.update(
            timer_freq_hz=rec.timer_freq_hz,
            schema_version=rec.schema_version,
            fw_git_short=rec.fw_git_short,
        )
    elif isinstance(rec, Stamp):
        try:
            base["stage"] = Stage(rec.stage_id).name
        except ValueError:
            base["stage"] = f"stage_{rec.stage_id:#04x}"
        base["stage_id"] = rec.stage_id
        base["aux"] = rec.aux
    elif isinstance(rec, Drop):
        base.update(
            dropped_state=rec.dropped_state,
            dropped_strip=rec.dropped_strip,
            dropped_sink=rec.dropped_sink,
        )
    elif isinstance(rec, TaskHighwater):
        try:
            base["task_name"] = TaskId(rec.task_id).name
        except ValueError:
            base["task_name"] = f"task_{rec.task_id}"
        base["task_id"] = rec.task_id
        base["words"] = rec.words
    elif isinstance(rec, TaskRuntime):
        try:
            base["task_name"] = TaskId(rec.task_id).name
        except ValueError:
            base["task_name"] = f"task_{rec.task_id}"
        try:
            base["state_name"] = TaskState(rec.state).name
        except ValueError:
            base["state_name"] = f"state_{rec.state}"
        base["task_id"] = rec.task_id
        base["state"] = rec.state
        base["priority"] = rec.priority
        base["run_time_counter"] = rec.run_time_counter
    elif isinstance(rec, Strip):
        base.update(
            x=rec.x, y=rec.y, w=rec.w, h=rec.h,
            kind=rec.kind, kind_name=rec.kind_name,
        )
        # Pixels travel via the strip PNG endpoint — don't inline them.
    else:
        # Detector, Timing, UnknownRecord — keep generic field projection.
        for fname in getattr(rec, "__dataclass_fields__", {}):
            if fname == "hdr":
                continue
            v = getattr(rec, fname)
            if isinstance(v, (bytes, bytearray)):
                base[fname] = f"<{len(v)} B>"
            elif isinstance(v, tuple):
                base[fname] = list(v)
            else:
                base[fname] = v
    return base

```python
"""Single-tenant live session: serial reader thread + WS push.

The reader thread owns the open SerialSource and runs the frame decoder.
Decoded records are pushed onto a per-WS-attach asyncio.Queue via
``loop.call_soon_threadsafe``. The CLI's `live`/`set-mask` primitives are
reused — `frame_encode`, `encode_set_mask_payload`, `SerialSource.send_command`
— so the wire-level concerns sit in transport.py / framing.py / records.py
and this module only composes them.

Recording (write framed bytes to a capture dir) is wired in Phase 3.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any

from fastapi import WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect

from ..decode import decode_record
from ..framing import FrameStats, frame_encode, iter_frames
from ..records import (
    RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME,
    Session,
    encode_set_mask_payload,
)
from ..transport import SerialSource


_QUEUE_MAX = 10_000


@dataclass
class _State:
    port: str | None = None
    mask: int = 0xFFFFFFFF
    started_at: str | None = None
    framing_stats: FrameStats = field(default_factory=FrameStats)
    last_session_dict: dict[str, Any] | None = None


class _LiveSession:
    """Process-singleton; mutex guards all field writes."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._lock = threading.RLock()
        self._state = _State()
        self._ser: SerialSource | None = None
        self._thread: threading.Thread | None = None
        self._stop_event = threading.Event()
        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] | None = None
        self._loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop | None = None
        self._ws: WebSocket | None = None
        # Late-bound to avoid a cycle: api.py passes this on import.
        self._record_to_dict = None  # type: ignore[var-annotated]

    # ─── lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def configure(self, *, record_to_dict) -> None:
        self._record_to_dict = record_to_dict

    def is_active(self) -> bool:
        with self._lock:
            return self._thread is not None and self._thread.is_alive()

    def start(self, port: str, *, ser_factory=None) -> None:
        """Open serial + start reader thread.

        ``ser_factory`` is an injection point for tests — if provided, called
        as ``ser_factory(port)`` and expected to return a context-manager
        iterable (yields bytes chunks) with ``send_command``.
        """
        with self._lock:
            if self.is_active():
                raise RuntimeError("live session already active")
            self._stop_event.clear()
            self._state = _State(
                port=port,
                started_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            )
            ser = (ser_factory or SerialSource)(port)
            ser.__enter__()
            self._ser = ser
            self._thread = threading.Thread(
                target=self._reader_loop,
                name="marvin-perf-live",
                daemon=True,
            )
            self._thread.start()

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Idempotent: safe to call when not active."""
        with self._lock:
            self._stop_event.set()
            ser = self._ser
            self._ser = None
            t = self._thread
            self._thread = None
        if ser is not None:
            try:
                ser.__exit__(None, None, None)
            except Exception:
                pass
        if t is not None and t.is_alive():
            t.join(timeout=3.0)

    # ─── control plane ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def set_mask_from_int(self, mask: int) -> int:
        m = mask & 0xFFFFFFFF
        with self._lock:
            ser = self._ser
            if ser is None:
                raise RuntimeError("live session not active")
            self._state.mask = m
        ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_set_mask_payload(m)))
        self._post("mask", {"value": f"0x{m:08x}", "source": "client"})
        return m

    def set_mask_from_names(self, names: list[str]) -> int:
        mask = 0
        for raw in names:
            token = raw.strip().upper()
            if not token:
                continue
            if token == "ALL":
                mask = 0xFFFFFFFF
                break
            if token not in RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME:
                valid = ", ".join(sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME))
                raise ValueError(f"unknown record type {token!r}; valid: {valid}, ALL")
            mask |= 1 << RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME[token]
        return self.set_mask_from_int(mask)

    def status(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        with self._lock:
            active = self.is_active()
            return {
                "active": active,
                "port": self._state.port if active else None,
                "mask": f"0x{self._state.mask:08x}" if active else None,
                "recording": None,  # Phase 3
                "started_at": self._state.started_at if active else None,
                "framing": {
                    "frames_ok": self._state.framing_stats.frames_ok,
                    "crc_err": self._state.framing_stats.crc_mismatches,
                    "resync_drop": self._state.framing_stats.bytes_resync_dropped,
                    "bad_lengths": self._state.framing_stats.bad_lengths,
                },
            }

    # ─── WS attachment ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def attach_ws(self, ws: WebSocket) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            if self._ws is not None:
                await ws.close(code=4409, reason="live already in use")
                return
            if not self.is_active():
                await ws.close(code=4404, reason="no active live session")
                return
            self._loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
            self._queue = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=_QUEUE_MAX)
            self._ws = ws

        await ws.accept()
        with self._lock:
            hello = {
                "type": "hello",
                "session": {
                    "started_at": self._state.started_at,
                    "port": self._state.port,
                    "mask": f"0x{self._state.mask:08x}",
                    "recording": None,
                },
            }
            replay = self._state.last_session_dict
        try:
            await ws.send_json(hello)
            if replay is not None:
                await ws.send_json({"type": "session_replay", "rec": replay})
            queue = self._queue
            while True:
                msg_type, payload = await queue.get()
                if msg_type == "record":
                    await ws.send_json({"type": "record", "rec": payload})
                elif msg_type == "mask":
                    await ws.send_json({"type": "mask", **payload})
                elif msg_type == "error":
                    await ws.send_json({"type": "error", **payload})
                    break
                elif msg_type == "framing_stats":
                    await ws.send_json({"type": "framing_stats", **payload})
        except WebSocketDisconnect:
            pass
        finally:
            with self._lock:
                self._ws = None
                self._queue = None

    # ─── reader thread ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _reader_loop(self) -> None:
        ser = self._ser
        stats = self._state.framing_stats
        if ser is None:
            return
        try:
            for frame in iter_frames(ser, stats):
                if self._stop_event.is_set():
                    break
                try:
                    rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
                except Exception:
                    continue
                if self._record_to_dict is None:
                    continue
                rec_dict = self._record_to_dict(rec, include_bgr=True)
                if isinstance(rec, Session):
                    with self._lock:
                        self._state.last_session_dict = rec_dict
                self._post("record", rec_dict)
        except Exception as e:
            self._post("error", {"code": "serial-error", "msg": str(e)})

    # ─── internal: cross-thread queue post ──────────────────────────────

    def _post(self, msg_type: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        loop = self._loop
        queue = self._queue
        if loop is None or queue is None:
            return
        try:
            loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._queue_put_nowait, msg_type, payload)
        except RuntimeError:
            pass

    def _queue_put_nowait(self, msg_type: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        # Runs on the asyncio loop thread.
        if self._queue is None:
            return
        try:
            self._queue.put_nowait((msg_type, payload))
        except asyncio.QueueFull:
            pass


SESSION = _LiveSession()

     def frame_encode(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
         length = len(payload)
         if length > 0xFFFF:
             raise ValueError(f"payload too large: {length} bytes")
         len_bytes = bytes((length & 0xFF, (length >> 8) & 0xFF))
         crc = crc16_ccitt_false(len_bytes + payload)
         crc_bytes = bytes((crc & 0xFF, (crc >> 8) & 0xFF))
         return SOF_BYTES + len_bytes + payload + crc_bytes
     ```

133	    return build_header(RecordType.STRIP, frame_epoch=frame_epoch) + body + bgr

136	# ─── Frame wrapper (SOF + LEN + payload + CRC) ───────────────────────────────
137	
138	
139	def wrap_frame(payload: bytes, *, corrupt_crc: bool = False) -> bytes:
140	    length = len(payload)
141	    length_bytes = struct.pack("<H", length)
142	    crc = crc16_ccitt_false(length_bytes + payload)
143	    if corrupt_crc:
144	        crc ^= 0xFFFF
145	    return SOF_BYTES + length_bytes + payload + struct.pack("<H", crc)

1	"""Byte sources feeding `framing.iter_frames`.
2	
3	Each source is an iterable of `bytes` chunks. Chunk size is not load-bearing —
4	the framer handles arbitrary boundaries.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
10	from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
11	from pathlib import Path
12	from typing import BinaryIO
13	
14	
15	# ─── File source ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
16	
17	
18	class FileSource(AbstractContextManager["FileSource"]):
19	    """Iterate over fixed-size chunks from a captured `.bin` file."""
20	
21	    def __init__(self, path: str | Path, chunk_bytes: int = 64 * 1024) -> None:
22	        self.path = Path(path)
23	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
24	        self._fh: BinaryIO | None = None
25	
26	    def __enter__(self) -> "FileSource":
27	        self._fh = self.path.open("rb")
28	        return self
29	
30	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
31	        if self._fh is not None:
32	            self._fh.close()
33	            self._fh = None
34	
35	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
36	        if self._fh is None:
37	            raise RuntimeError("FileSource must be used as a context manager")
38	        while True:
39	            chunk = self._fh.read(self.chunk_bytes)
40	            if not chunk:
41	                return
42	            yield chunk
43	
44	
45	# ─── Serial source ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
46	
47	
48	class SerialSource(AbstractContextManager["SerialSource"]):
49	    """Read bytes from the marvin USB-device CDC ACM port via pyserial.
50	
51	    The firmware sink is DTR-gated (`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:216`); pyserial raises
52	    DTR by default on open, which triggers the firmware to re-emit a SESSION
53	    record. CDC ACM ignores baud rate; we still pass one because pyserial
54	    requires it.
55	    """
56	
57	    def __init__(
58	        self,
59	        port: str,
60	        *,
61	        baudrate: int = 921600,
62	        chunk_bytes: int = 4096,
63	        read_timeout_s: float = 0.1,
64	    ) -> None:
65	        self.port = port
66	        self.baudrate = baudrate
67	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
68	        self.read_timeout_s = read_timeout_s
69	        self._ser: object | None = None
70	
71	    def __enter__(self) -> "SerialSource":
72	        # Imported lazily so file-only workflows do not require pyserial.
73	        import serial  # noqa: WPS433  (intentional lazy import)
74	
75	        self._ser = serial.Serial(
76	            port=self.port,
77	            baudrate=self.baudrate,
78	            timeout=self.read_timeout_s,
79	            dsrdtr=False,
80	        )
81	        # Make DTR explicit — some platforms default it off.
82	        try:
83	            self._ser.dtr = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
84	        except (OSError, AttributeError):
85	            pass
86	        return self
87	
88	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
89	        if self._ser is not None:
90	            try:
91	                self._ser.close()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
92	            finally:
93	                self._ser = None
94	
95	    def send_command(self, framed: bytes) -> int:
96	        """Write pre-framed command bytes to the device.
97	
98	        Caller frames via `framing.frame_encode`. Returns bytes written.
99	        """
100	        if self._ser is None:
101	            raise RuntimeError("SerialSource must be used as a context manager")
102	        return self._ser.write(framed)  # type: ignore[attr-defined,no-any-return]
103	
104	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
105	        if self._ser is None:
106	            raise RuntimeError("SerialSource must be used as a context manager")
107	        ser = self._ser
108	        while True:
109	            # `read` with timeout returns whatever has arrived (possibly empty
110	            # on timeout). `in_waiting` lets us drain the OS buffer in one go
111	            # when bytes are already queued.
112	            n = max(1, getattr(ser, "in_waiting", 0))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
113	            chunk: bytes = ser.read(min(n, self.chunk_bytes))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
114	            if chunk:
115	                yield chunk
116	
117	
118	# ─── Tee — passthrough source that also records to disk ──────────────────────
119	
120	
121	class TeeSource(AbstractContextManager["TeeSource"]):
122	    """Wrap any byte source so every chunk is also appended to a file.
123	
124	    Used by `marvin-perf live --also-record FILE` so a single live session
125	    yields both inline decode output and a `.bin` capture for later
126	    summarize/replay.
127	    """
128	
129	    def __init__(
130	        self,
131	        upstream: Iterable[bytes] | AbstractContextManager[Iterable[bytes]],
132	        out_path: str | Path,
133	    ) -> None:
134	        self.upstream = upstream
135	        self.out_path = Path(out_path)
136	        self._fh: BinaryIO | None = None
137	
138	    def __enter__(self) -> "TeeSource":
139	        self._fh = self.out_path.open("wb")
140	        if isinstance(self.upstream, AbstractContextManager):
141	            self.upstream.__enter__()
142	        return self
143	
144	    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None:
145	        try:
146	            if isinstance(self.upstream, AbstractContextManager):
147	                self.upstream.__exit__(exc_type, exc, tb)
148	        finally:
149	            if self._fh is not None:
150	                self._fh.close()
151	                self._fh = None
152	
153	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
154	        if self._fh is None:
155	            raise RuntimeError("TeeSource must be used as a context manager")
156	        for chunk in self.upstream:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
157	            self._fh.write(chunk)
158	            self._fh.flush()
159	            yield chunk
160

"""Single-tenant live session — reader thread lifecycle + control plane."""

from __future__ import annotations

import threading
import time
from typing import Any

import pytest

from marvin_perf.framing import FrameStats, frame_encode, iter_frames
from marvin_perf.records import (
    PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC,
    PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK,
    RecordType,
    encode_set_mask_payload,
)
from marvin_perf.web.live import _LiveSession


class _FakeSerial:
    """Stand-in for SerialSource — context-managed iterable + send_command capture."""

    def __init__(self, port: str) -> None:
        self.port = port
        self.sent: list[bytes] = []
        self._closed = threading.Event()
        self._entered = False

    def __enter__(self) -> "_FakeSerial":
        self._entered = True
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
        self._closed.set()

    def send_command(self, framed: bytes) -> int:
        self.sent.append(framed)
        return len(framed)

    def __iter__(self):
        # Block until the session closes us. Yields nothing — reader thread
        # idles in iter_frames waiting for chunks that never come.
        while not self._closed.is_set():
            time.sleep(0.005)
        return
        yield  # pragma: no cover  (make this a generator)


def _make_session() -> _LiveSession:
    sess = _LiveSession()
    sess.configure(record_to_dict=lambda rec, *, include_bgr=False: {})
    return sess


def test_start_then_stop_releases_thread() -> None:
    sess = _make_session()
    fake_holder: dict[str, _FakeSerial] = {}

    def factory(port: str) -> _FakeSerial:
        ser = _FakeSerial(port)
        fake_holder["ser"] = ser
        return ser

    sess.start("/dev/null", ser_factory=factory)
    assert sess.is_active()
    assert fake_holder["ser"]._entered

    sess.stop()
    assert not sess.is_active()
    assert fake_holder["ser"]._closed.is_set()
    # Idempotent.
    sess.stop()


def test_set_mask_round_trips_to_serial_send() -> None:
    sess = _make_session()
    captured: dict[str, _FakeSerial] = {}

    def factory(port: str) -> _FakeSerial:
        ser = _FakeSerial(port)
        captured["ser"] = ser
        return ser

    sess.start("/dev/null", ser_factory=factory)
    try:
        resolved = sess.set_mask_from_names(["STAMP", "SESSION"])
        expected = (1 << RecordType.SESSION) | (1 << RecordType.STAMP)
        assert resolved == expected

        ser = captured["ser"]
        assert len(ser.sent) == 1
        # Decode the framed command back via iter_frames and confirm payload.
        out = list(iter_frames([ser.sent[0]], FrameStats()))
        assert len(out) == 1
        assert out[0].payload == encode_set_mask_payload(expected)
        # And that payload starts with the command magic + opcode.
        assert out[0].payload[:2] == bytes(
            (PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC & 0xFF, (PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC >> 8) & 0xFF)
        )
        assert out[0].payload[2] == PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK
    finally:
        sess.stop()


def test_set_mask_when_inactive_raises() -> None:
    sess = _make_session()
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        sess.set_mask_from_int(0xFF)


def test_set_mask_unknown_name_raises() -> None:
    sess = _make_session()

    def factory(port: str) -> _FakeSerial:
        return _FakeSerial(port)

    sess.start("/dev/null", ser_factory=factory)
    try:
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            sess.set_mask_from_names(["BOGUS"])
    finally:
        sess.stop()


def test_set_mask_all_token() -> None:
    sess = _make_session()

    def factory(port: str) -> _FakeSerial:
        return _FakeSerial(port)

    sess.start("/dev/null", ser_factory=factory)
    try:
        resolved = sess.set_mask_from_names(["ALL"])
        assert resolved == 0xFFFFFFFF
    finally:
        sess.stop()


def test_double_start_raises() -> None:
    sess = _make_session()

    def factory(port: str) -> _FakeSerial:
        return _FakeSerial(port)

    sess.start("/dev/null", ser_factory=factory)
    try:
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
            sess.start("/dev/null", ser_factory=factory)
    finally:
        sess.stop()


def test_status_inactive() -> None:
    sess = _make_session()
    s = sess.status()
    assert s["active"] is False
    assert s["port"] is None
    assert s["mask"] is None


def test_status_active_reports_port_and_mask() -> None:
    sess = _make_session()

    def factory(port: str) -> _FakeSerial:
        return _FakeSerial(port)

    sess.start("/dev/cu.usbmodem-test", ser_factory=factory)
    try:
        s = sess.status()
        assert s["active"] is True
        assert s["port"] == "/dev/cu.usbmodem-test"
        assert s["mask"] == "0xffffffff"
        assert s["recording"] is None
    finally:
        sess.stop()
