```text
+### 2026-05-22 — perf-log host→device record-type masking
+
+Bidirectional control on the perf-log channel. Host can now narrow which record types the device emits per-capture without rebuilding firmware. Default is all-on (parity with prior behavior); host sends a `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK` over the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer that's used for records, with a distinct command magic (`0x4D43` 'MC' vs records' `0x4D56` 'MV') so misrouted bytes can't be parsed in the wrong direction.
+
+**Device side.** New [`perf_log_rx.{h,c}`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_rx.c) holds a small SOF-resync state machine fed from the CDC sink's `USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE` handler; valid `SET_TYPE_MASK` frames call `PerfLog_SetEnabledMask`. The CDC sink primes a 64-byte read on `EVENT_DEVICE_CONFIGURED` and re-primes after each completion. Filter is one `s_enabled_mask` (volatile u32, lock-free single-load on Cortex-A) checked at three early-return points: `send_state` (covers all state records), `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame`, and `PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR`. SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask — the host needs `timer_freq_hz` on attach.
+
+**Host side.** New `frame_encode` in [`framing.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/framing.py) (mirror of the device framer); `encode_set_mask_payload` + `RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME` in [`records.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py); `SerialSource.send_command` in [`transport.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/transport.py). CLI `live` and `record` get `--types STAMP,SESSION,DROP,…` (special tokens `ALL`, `MIN`); new `set-mask` subcommand pokes a running capture from another terminal. 9 new tests; 83/83 passing.
+
+**Why now.** The 1.88 MB/s STRIP-dominated load was masking HWM/RUNTIME records (state-queue starvation, ~707 dropped/s — see prior entry). Cutting record types at the source is a cleaner fix than enlarging queues we don't actually want full. With STRIP off, expected sink load drops to ~25 KB/s, and the state queue should drain freely.
+
+**Out of scope.** No schema bump (purely additive at the host→device edge — v2 stays v2). No flash persistence of the mask. No mask-state echo back (host knows what it sent). No viewer UI checkbox panel — deferred to when live-WS lands.
+
+**Verification pending hardware.** Bench check: `marvin-perf record --types STAMP,SESSION,DROP,HIGHWATER,RUNTIME --port … --out-dir …` should produce a capture with zero STRIP/DETECTOR/TIMING records and `dropped_state == 0`. Sanity: firmware UART log shows `PerfLog: mask=0x...` when the host attaches.
+
+### 2026-05-22 — USB CDC bandwidth headroom + state-queue starvation diagnosis
+
+End-to-end strip viewer is up and rendering after the user adjusted strip dimensions in [`cv_marvin_v1.c:341-347`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L341-L347) to sensing 185×16 @ (265, 310) and strike 290×20 @ (212, 395). At those dimensions current device→host load is **1.88 MB/s** (≈8.9 KB sensing + ≈17.4 KB strike per frame × 60 Hz + ~25 KB/s state pipeline + ~80 B/frame record overhead) — the link badge is green and `dropped_strip`/`dropped_sink` are flat. But we were dropping at slightly higher dimensions just before this, so our practical CDC-ACM ceiling is < 5 MB/s on this firmware build today. Two concrete things came out of investigating that:
+
+**(1) Where the bandwidth is actually going.** The USB-HS bulk-IN theoretical ceiling on UDPHS is ~40-45 MB/s real-world; we're leaving ~85 % of it on the floor. The conservative 5 MB/s working number isn't a USB-HS limit — it's a software-pipeline limit specific to how the sink writes today. Five candidate levers, ranked by expected payoff:
+
+  1. **Pipeline writes** ([`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:251-267`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L251-L267)) — biggest single win, expect 2-3×. Today the sink owns a single staging buffer and pends a `WRITE_COMPLETE` semaphore between writes, so the USB DMA sits idle for the round-trip. The CDC write-queue depth is already 3 (`USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED = 3U` in [`configuration.h:243`](../default/src/config/default/configuration.h#L243)) so multi-buffer queueing is supported by the layers below — the sink just doesn't use it. Move to a 2- or 3-deep ring of staging buffers; submit the next write as soon as the previous returns to the queue, not when it completes.
+  2. **Hardware CRC via CRCCU** — soft CRC at [`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:58-70`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L58-L70) burns ~14 % of CPU at the current rate (byte-at-a-time over every framed payload). CRCCU peripheral does CCITT-FALSE in DMA. Frees CPU for whatever the next bottleneck turns out to be; not a bandwidth knob in itself, but it's the cheapest path to free headroom.
+  3. **Combine sensing+strike into one wire frame** — saves ~80 B framing overhead per ISC frame (×60 Hz = 4.8 KB/s, ~5-15 % of state-pipeline payload). Small but free if the schema accommodates it; revisit only if (1) and (2) aren't enough.
+  4. **Move bulk-IN from EP3 → EP2** — UDPHS only exposes 3-bank FIFO depth on EP1-2 ([`drv_usb_udphs_local.h:159`](../default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_local.h#L159) `DRV_USB_UDPHS_EPT_BK = 0x00060000`); EP3-7 are 2-bank only. The current bulk-IN is on EP3 ([`usb_device_init_data.c:213-220`](../default/src/config/default/usb_device_init_data.c#L213-L220)). 3-bank lets the controller pre-load three packets ahead of the host IN tokens; smooths out scheduler micro-stalls. Marginal win unless we're already pipelining at the software layer (so do this *after* lever 1).
+  5. **Eliminate one memcpy** (architectural) — strip producer copies pixel rows out of the ISC frame into a queue slot, drain task copies that slot bytes onto the wire. Could be reduced to one copy if the strip producer wrote into a sink-owned ring directly, at the cost of tighter coupling between perf_log and the sink. Defer; the ratio of CPU spent in memcpy vs CRC favors lever 2 first.
+
+  **What's *not* the bottleneck:** the `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE = 2` knob in [`configuration.h:255`](../default/src/config/default/configuration.h#L255) (multiples of 64 KB, so 128 KB cap). Our largest single record is the 23 KB strip — 5× under the cap. Bumping this to 4 or 8 changes nothing about today's behavior. Documented here because it was the first knob the user noticed and it's tempting to try; save the time.
+
+**(2) HWM + RUNTIME records are absent from captures because the state queue is full.** Decoded a 24 s capture — zero `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` and zero `PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME` records, but `dropped_state since_session = 17188` (~707 dropped/s). Producers are wired and the drain task is calling them every second; the records hit a full queue and get counted as drops instead. Root cause: all state-pipeline records share `s_state_q` ([`perf_log.c:50-52`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c#L50-L52), `PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH = 128`). The 60 Hz × multiple-stage STAMP traffic — especially fretboard_link's `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` and `FBL_SEND` pair, which fire on every actuator wire byte — bursts faster than the drain can pull, the queue stays near full, and the once-per-second HWM/RUNTIME emits land on a full queue. Three candidate fixes:
+
+  1. **Bump `PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH` from 128 to 1024.** Cheapest. 128 × 32 B/slot = 4 KB today → 32 KB after; static BSS, no malloc. Probably enough on its own — the drain isn't *behind*, it's just unable to absorb burst peaks at 128 slots. Try first.
+  2. **Give HWM/RUNTIME a dedicated low-pressure queue** drained on the same 1 Hz tick as DROP. Decouples the slow analytics path from the fast stamp path entirely; HWM/RUNTIME can never lose to a stamp burst. More plumbing (second queue + second drain branch) but it's the right shape long-term — and natural alongside lever 1 above (pipelining the sink) since the drain task changes anyway.
+  3. **Throttle the high-rate stamp producers** — e.g. drop `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` to 1-in-N, or roll FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE into a single record. Loses information from the timeline; do this only if (1) and (2) both fail.
+
+  Going to start with (1) since it's a single `#define` change and HWM is the most useful "is something about to overflow its stack" signal — we want it back before any of the bandwidth-lever work begins, since stack pressure is exactly the kind of thing that surfaces while we're refactoring the sink.
+
+Neither finding is being acted on in this session — captured here so the analysis survives context.
+
+### 2026-05-22 — Phase 2 perf-log: schema v2 (STRIP + TASK_RUNTIME) wired
+
+Schema bump landed end-to-end. Firmware emits the two new record types; host decoder, analyzer, and viewer read them.
+
+**Schema v2.** [`perf_log_records.h`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h) bumps `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 2. `PERF_REC_PATCH (0x05)` is replaced by `PERF_REC_STRIP (0x05)` — variable-length BGR888 region tagged by `perf_strip_kind_t` (SENSING=0, STRIP=1; 256 codes available). `PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME (0x08)` adds per-task state/priority/`ulRunTimeCounter` snapshots. Both mirrored on the host in [`records.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py); `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`.
+
+**STRIP producer in [`cv_marvin_v1.c`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c).** Two strips per ISC frame, emitted between `detect_frame` and `draw_overlay` so the captured pixels are clean detector input. Sensing line at (240, 295) 240×32, strike line at (240, 400) 240×32 — same coordinates `cv_marvin_v1` already samples for fret detection. Cost: 240×32×3 × 2 × 60 Hz ≈ 2.76 MB/s, well under the 5 MB/s CDC ceiling. The strip queue holds max-sized slots (`PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES = 23040`); drain task computes the on-wire length per record from `(w, h)` so future kinds at smaller dimensions cost only what they emit.
+
+**TASK_RUNTIME producer in `perf_log.c`.** 1 Hz alongside the existing HWM emitter — `sample_and_emit_runtimes` fills a static `TaskStatus_t buf[16]` via `uxTaskGetSystemState`, maps each handle to its `perf_task_id_t` via `s_task_handles[]`, and emits `state` (mapped from `eTaskState`), `uxCurrentPriority`, and `ulRunTimeCounter`. Static buffer + bounded loop (no malloc, no recursion). Cost: 24 B × 6 tasks × 1 Hz = 144 B/s.
+
+**FreeRTOSConfig.** `INCLUDE_eTaskGetState` flipped 0 → 1 — required for the `eCurrentState` field that `uxTaskGetSystemState` populates. `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` from patch #8 already in place.
+
+**Host.** `decode.py` validates `len(bgr) == w*h*3` against on-wire dims (not a compile-time constant) so future kinds at other rectangles decode cleanly. `analyze.py` field rename `dropped_patch → dropped_strip`. Viewer's `STRIP_KIND_REGISTRY` already kind-driven from Phase 1 — strips render in their pre-allocated slots without additional work. 60 → 74 passing pytests.
+
+End-to-end verification still pending: user builds in MPLAB X, captures a session, confirms strips render in the viewer and the RTOS-tab CPU% chart populates.
+
 ### 2026-05-22 — STAMP producers wired across pipeline; 64-bit ts_counter; diag UART dump retired
 
 Follow-on session to Phase 1 — wired the seven `perf_stage_t` producers that had been declared since the schema landed but had no emitters, fixed a 32-bit timer truncation that was poisoning the timeline, and retired the 10 s diag UART dump now that the perf-log channel covers RTOS analytics.
```

```text
+def frame_encode(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
+    """SOF + LEN(u16LE) + payload + CRC16-CCITT-FALSE(u16LE).
+
+    Mirror of the device-side framer; CRC covers LEN || PAYLOAD (not SOF).
+    """
+    length = len(payload)
+    if length > 0xFFFF:
+        raise ValueError(f"payload too large: {length} bytes")
+    len_bytes = bytes((length & 0xFF, (length >> 8) & 0xFF))
+    crc = crc16_ccitt_false(len_bytes + payload)
+    crc_bytes = bytes((crc & 0xFF, (crc >> 8) & 0xFF))
+    return SOF_BYTES + len_bytes + payload + crc_bytes
+
```

```text
144	                PerfLogRx_Feed(s_rx_buf, (uint32_t)rd->length);
145	            }
146	            prime_rx_read();
147	            break;
148	        }
149	
150	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_SENT:
151	        default:
152	            break;
153	    }
154	    return USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE_NONE;
155	}
156	
157	/* ─── Device-layer event handler ─────────────────────────────────────────── */
158	
159	static void device_event_handler(USB_DEVICE_EVENT event, void *eventData,
160	                                 uintptr_t context)
161	{
162	    (void)context;
163	
164	    switch (event)
165	    {
166	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESET:
167	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DECONFIGURED:
168	            s_is_configured = false;
169	            break;
170	
171	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_CONFIGURED:
172	        {
173	            const USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DATA_CONFIGURED *cd = eventData;
174	            if (cd->configurationValue == 1u)
175	            {
176	                (void)USB_DEVICE_CDC_EventHandlerSet(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
177	                                                    cdc_event_handler, 0u);
178	                s_is_configured = true;
179	                LOG_INFO("PERF: USB device CDC configured\r\n");
180	                prime_rx_read();
181	            }
182	            break;
183	        }
184	
185	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_DETECTED:
186	            (void)USB_DEVICE_Attach(s_dev_handle);
187	            break;
188	
189	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_REMOVED:
190	            (void)USB_DEVICE_Detach(s_dev_handle);
191	            s_is_configured = false;
192	            break;
193	
194	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SUSPENDED:
195	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESUMED:
196	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SOF:
197	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_ERROR:
198	        default:
199	            break;
200	    }
201	}
202	
203	/* ─── Public sink interface ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
204	
205	void PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize(void)
206	{
207	    s_write_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_write_done_buf);
208	    configASSERT(s_write_done != NULL);
209	
210	    PerfLogRx_Initialize();
211	
212	    /* Open may fail until USB_DEVICE_Initialize finishes its own first
213	     * task tick — retry until success. Drain task is alive at this
214	     * point so vTaskDelay is fine. */
215	    while (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
216	    {
217	        s_dev_handle = USB_DEVICE_Open(USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0,
218	                                       DRV_IO_INTENT_READWRITE);
219	        if (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
220	        {
221	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SINK_OPEN_RETRY_MS));
222	        }
223	    }
224	
225	    USB_DEVICE_EventHandlerSet(s_dev_handle, device_event_handler, 0u);
226	
227	    /* Cold-boot-with-cable case: by the time we register the handler the
228	     * UDPHS driver may have already raced past the VBUS edge it needed
229	     * to fire POWER_DETECTED, or the host may have seen a brief pull-up
230	     * assertion during early boot and given up retrying. Force a clean
```

```text
137	
138	## Session log
139	
140	### 2026-05-22 — perf-log host→device record-type masking
141	
142	Bidirectional control on the perf-log channel. Host can now narrow which record types the device emits per-capture without rebuilding firmware. Default is all-on (parity with prior behavior); host sends a `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK` over the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer that's used for records, with a distinct command magic (`0x4D43` 'MC' vs records' `0x4D56` 'MV') so misrouted bytes can't be parsed in the wrong direction.
143	
144	**Device side.** New [`perf_log_rx.{h,c}`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_rx.c) holds a small SOF-resync state machine fed from the CDC sink's `USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE` handler; valid `SET_TYPE_MASK` frames call `PerfLog_SetEnabledMask`. The CDC sink primes a 64-byte read on `EVENT_DEVICE_CONFIGURED` and re-primes after each completion. Filter is one `s_enabled_mask` (volatile u32, lock-free single-load on Cortex-A) checked at three early-return points: `send_state` (covers all state records), `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame`, and `PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR`. SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask — the host needs `timer_freq_hz` on attach.
145	
146	**Host side.** New `frame_encode` in [`framing.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/framing.py) (mirror of the device framer); `encode_set_mask_payload` + `RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME` in [`records.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py); `SerialSource.send_command` in [`transport.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/transport.py). CLI `live` and `record` get `--types STAMP,SESSION,DROP,…` (special tokens `ALL`, `MIN`); new `set-mask` subcommand pokes a running capture from another terminal. 9 new tests; 83/83 passing.
147	
148	**Why now.** The 1.88 MB/s STRIP-dominated load was masking HWM/RUNTIME records (state-queue starvation, ~707 dropped/s — see prior entry). Cutting record types at the source is a cleaner fix than enlarging queues we don't actually want full. With STRIP off, expected sink load drops to ~25 KB/s, and the state queue should drain freely.
149	
150	**Out of scope.** No schema bump (purely additive at the host→device edge — v2 stays v2). No flash persistence of the mask. No mask-state echo back (host knows what it sent). No viewer UI checkbox panel — deferred to when live-WS lands.
151	
152	**Verification pending hardware.** Bench check: `marvin-perf record --types STAMP,SESSION,DROP,HIGHWATER,RUNTIME --port … --out-dir …` should produce a capture with zero STRIP/DETECTOR/TIMING records and `dropped_state == 0`. Sanity: firmware UART log shows `PerfLog: mask=0x...` when the host attaches.
153	
154	### 2026-05-22 — USB CDC bandwidth headroom + state-queue starvation diagnosis
155	
156	End-to-end strip viewer is up and rendering after the user adjusted strip dimensions in [`cv_marvin_v1.c:341-347`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L341-L347) to sensing 185×16 @ (265, 310) and strike 290×20 @ (212, 395). At those dimensions current device→host load is **1.88 MB/s** (≈8.9 KB sensing + ≈17.4 KB strike per frame × 60 Hz + ~25 KB/s state pipeline + ~80 B/frame record overhead) — the link badge is green and `dropped_strip`/`dropped_sink` are flat. But we were dropping at slightly higher dimensions just before this, so our practical CDC-ACM ceiling is < 5 MB/s on this firmware build today. Two concrete things came out of investigating that:
157	
158	**(1) Where the bandwidth is actually going.** The USB-HS bulk-IN theoretical ceiling on UDPHS is ~40-45 MB/s real-world; we're leaving ~85 % of it on the floor. The conservative 5 MB/s working number isn't a USB-HS limit — it's a software-pipeline limit specific to how the sink writes today. Five candidate levers, ranked by expected payoff:
159	
160	  1. **Pipeline writes** ([`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:251-267`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L251-L267)) — biggest single win, expect 2-3×. Today the sink owns a single staging buffer and pends a `WRITE_COMPLETE` semaphore between writes, so the USB DMA sits idle for the round-trip. The CDC write-queue depth is already 3 (`USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED = 3U` in [`configuration.h:243`](../default/src/config/default/configuration.h#L243)) so multi-buffer queueing is supported by the layers below — the sink just doesn't use it. Move to a 2- or 3-deep ring of staging buffers; submit the next write as soon as the previous returns to the queue, not when it completes.
161	  2. **Hardware CRC via CRCCU** — soft CRC at [`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:58-70`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L58-L70) burns ~14 % of CPU at the current rate (byte-at-a-time over every framed payload). CRCCU peripheral does CCITT-FALSE in DMA. Frees CPU for whatever the next bottleneck turns out to be; not a bandwidth knob in itself, but it's the cheapest path to free headroom.
162	  3. **Combine sensing+strike into one wire frame** — saves ~80 B framing overhead per ISC frame (×60 Hz = 4.8 KB/s, ~5-15 % of state-pipeline payload). Small but free if the schema accommodates it; revisit only if (1) and (2) aren't enough.
163	  4. **Move bulk-IN from EP3 → EP2** — UDPHS only exposes 3-bank FIFO depth on EP1-2 ([`drv_usb_udphs_local.h:159`](../default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_local.h#L159) `DRV_USB_UDPHS_EPT_BK = 0x00060000`); EP3-7 are 2-bank only. The current bulk-IN is on EP3 ([`usb_device_init_data.c:213-220`](../default/src/config/default/usb_device_init_data.c#L213-L220)). 3-bank lets the controller pre-load three packets ahead of the host IN tokens; smooths out scheduler micro-stalls. Marginal win unless we're already pipelining at the software layer (so do this *after* lever 1).
164	  5. **Eliminate one memcpy** (architectural) — strip producer copies pixel rows out of the ISC frame into a queue slot, drain task copies that slot bytes onto the wire. Could be reduced to one copy if the strip producer wrote into a sink-owned ring directly, at the cost of tighter coupling between perf_log and the sink. Defer; the ratio of CPU spent in memcpy vs CRC favors lever 2 first.
165	
166	  **What's *not* the bottleneck:** the `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE = 2` knob in [`configuration.h:255`](../default/src/config/default/configuration.h#L255) (multiples of 64 KB, so 128 KB cap). Our largest single record is the 23 KB strip — 5× under the cap. Bumping this to 4 or 8 changes nothing about today's behavior. Documented here because it was the first knob the user noticed and it's tempting to try; save the time.
167	
168	**(2) HWM + RUNTIME records are absent from captures because the state queue is full.** Decoded a 24 s capture — zero `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` and zero `PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME` records, but `dropped_state since_session = 17188` (~707 dropped/s). Producers are wired and the drain task is calling them every second; the records hit a full queue and get counted as drops instead. Root cause: all state-pipeline records share `s_state_q` ([`perf_log.c:50-52`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c#L50-L52), `PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH = 128`). The 60 Hz × multiple-stage STAMP traffic — especially fretboard_link's `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` and `FBL_SEND` pair, which fire on every actuator wire byte — bursts faster than the drain can pull, the queue stays near full, and the once-per-second HWM/RUNTIME emits land on a full queue. Three candidate fixes:
169	
170	  1. **Bump `PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH` from 128 to 1024.** Cheapest. 128 × 32 B/slot = 4 KB today → 32 KB after; static BSS, no malloc. Probably enough on its own — the drain isn't *behind*, it's just unable to absorb burst peaks at 128 slots. Try first.
171	  2. **Give HWM/RUNTIME a dedicated low-pressure queue** drained on the same 1 Hz tick as DROP. Decouples the slow analytics path from the fast stamp path entirely; HWM/RUNTIME can never lose to a stamp burst. More plumbing (second queue + second drain branch) but it's the right shape long-term — and natural alongside lever 1 above (pipelining the sink) since the drain task changes anyway.
172	  3. **Throttle the high-rate stamp producers** — e.g. drop `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` to 1-in-N, or roll FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE into a single record. Loses information from the timeline; do this only if (1) and (2) both fail.
173	
174	  Going to start with (1) since it's a single `#define` change and HWM is the most useful "is something about to overflow its stack" signal — we want it back before any of the bandwidth-lever work begins, since stack pressure is exactly the kind of thing that surfaces while we're refactoring the sink.
175	
176	Neither finding is being acted on in this session — captured here so the analysis survives context.
177	
178	### 2026-05-22 — Phase 2 perf-log: schema v2 (STRIP + TASK_RUNTIME) wired
179	
180	Schema bump landed end-to-end. Firmware emits the two new record types; host decoder, analyzer, and viewer read them.
181	
182	**Schema v2.** [`perf_log_records.h`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h) bumps `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 2. `PERF_REC_PATCH (0x05)` is replaced by `PERF_REC_STRIP (0x05)` — variable-length BGR888 region tagged by `perf_strip_kind_t` (SENSING=0, STRIP=1; 256 codes available). `PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME (0x08)` adds per-task state/priority/`ulRunTimeCounter` snapshots. Both mirrored on the host in [`records.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py); `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`.
183	
184	**STRIP producer in [`cv_marvin_v1.c`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c).** Two strips per ISC frame, emitted between `detect_frame` and `draw_overlay` so the captured pixels are clean detector input. Sensing line at (240, 295) 240×32, strike line at (240, 400) 240×32 — same coordinates `cv_marvin_v1` already samples for fret detection. Cost: 240×32×3 × 2 × 60 Hz ≈ 2.76 MB/s, well under the 5 MB/s CDC ceiling. The strip queue holds max-sized slots (`PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES = 23040`); drain task computes the on-wire length per record from `(w, h)` so future kinds at smaller dimensions cost only what they emit.
185	
186	**TASK_RUNTIME producer in `perf_log.c`.** 1 Hz alongside the existing HWM emitter — `sample_and_emit_runtimes` fills a static `TaskStatus_t buf[16]` via `uxTaskGetSystemState`, maps each handle to its `perf_task_id_t` via `s_task_handles[]`, and emits `state` (mapped from `eTaskState`), `uxCurrentPriority`, and `ulRunTimeCounter`. Static buffer + bounded loop (no malloc, no recursion). Cost: 24 B × 6 tasks × 1 Hz = 144 B/s.
187
```

Commit 2: host→device mask

```bash
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
perf-log: host→device record-type mask over CDC

Adds bidirectional control on the perf-log channel — host sends a per-
record-type enable mask via the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer the device uses
for records, with a distinct command magic ('MC' = 0x4D43 vs records'
'MV' = 0x4D56) so misrouted bytes can't be parsed in the wrong direction.
Default is all-on (parity with prior behavior); SESSION is always emitted
regardless so the host gets timer_freq_hz on attach.

Motivation: 1.88 MB/s STRIP-dominated traffic was starving the shared
state queue, dropping ~707 HWM/RUNTIME records per second. Cutting record
types at the source is cleaner than enlarging queues that shouldn't be
full to begin with.

Firmware:
- perf_log_rx.{c,h}: small SOF-resync state machine fed from the CDC
  sink's READ_COMPLETE handler; valid SET_TYPE_MASK frames update
  s_enabled_mask (volatile u32, lock-free single-load on Cortex-A)
- perf_log.c: mask checked at three early-return points (send_state,
  EmitStripFromFrame, EmitStampFromISR)
- sink_cdc: 64-byte bulk-OUT staging buffer; primes a read on
  EVENT_DEVICE_CONFIGURED and re-primes after each completion

Host:
- frame_encode in framing.py: mirror of the device framer (SOF + LEN +
  payload + CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE)
- SerialSource.send_command: thin write() wrapper for framed bytes
- cli.py: --types STAMP,SESSION,DROP,… on `live` and `record` (special
  tokens ALL, MIN); new `set-mask` subcommand pokes a running capture
  from another terminal
- 9 new tests covering the encode round-trip, command magic vector, and
  CLI mask-spec parsing

No schema bump (purely additive at the host→device edge — v2 stays v2).
No flash persistence; no mask echo back. Viewer UI checkbox panel is the
follow-on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
```

   **Phase A (completed earlier in session)**: Add host→device record-type masking to the marvin perf-log channel — bidirectional CDC control where the host sends a per-record-type enable mask, defaulting to all-on. Goal: per-capture filtering replaces per-rebuild filtering.
   
   **Phase B (current focus)**: User said "I would like to be able to iterate faster which I think includes running everything from web page. including turning on and off record types" — make the marvin-perf web viewer the single iteration surface with live streaming, recording control, and mask-toggle UI. User approved a 3-phase plan: (1) backend live + mask routes + WS, (2) frontend live mode + mask checkboxes, (3) recording start/stop.
   
   User UX choices: Live buffer = **Sliding window** (~30 s, ~50k record cap); Recording stop = **Auto-finalize**.
   
   **Most recent request**: "we should probably commit something - it's been a while" → user chose **Three commits** when given commit-split options.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - perf-log v2 wire format: SOF + LEN(u16 LE) + PAYLOAD + CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE(u16 LE)
   - PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC=0x4D56 ('MV') for records; PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC=0x4D43 ('MC') for commands
   - USB CDC ACM bidirectional endpoint pair on UDPHS
   - FastAPI + uvicorn[standard] (websockets); pyserial as core dep
   - WebSocket for stream + REST for control plane
   - Single-tenant live session (one reader thread, one WS, second WS gets close code 4409)
   - asyncio.Queue + `loop.call_soon_threadsafe` cross-thread bridge
   - `FrameBytes.framed` field carries original framed bytes (no extra CRC compute on record path)
   - Static FreeRTOS memory only; no malloc
   - Late-binding via _LIVE.configure(record_to_dict=...) to avoid api.py↔live.py import cycle
   - Edit-then-stage technique for splitting mixed-feature working copies into clean commits

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/api.py** — Added live routes + Pydantic models. Key additions:
   ```python
   from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query, WebSocket
   from .live import SESSION as _LIVE
   
   class LiveStartRequest(BaseModel):
       port: str
   
   class SetMaskRequest(BaseModel):
       mask: int | None = None
       types: list[str] | None = None
   
   # Late-bind the JSON projector so live.py doesn't need to import api.py.
   _LIVE.configure(record_to_dict=_record_to_dict)
   
   @router.get("/serial/ports")
   def serial_ports() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
       from serial.tools import list_ports
       return [{"device": p.device, "description": p.description or ""}
               for p in list_ports.comports()]
   
   @router.get("/live/status")
   def live_status() -> dict[str, Any]:
       return _LIVE.status()
   
   @router.post("/live/start")
   def live_start(req: LiveStartRequest) -> dict[str, Any]:
       try:
           _LIVE.start(req.port)
       except RuntimeError as e:
           raise HTTPException(409, str(e))
       except Exception as e:
           raise HTTPException(500, f"failed to open serial port: {e}")
       return _LIVE.status()
   
   @router.post("/live/stop")
   def live_stop() -> dict[str, Any]:
       _LIVE.stop()
       return _LIVE.status()
   
   @router.post("/live/set-mask")
   def live_set_mask(req: SetMaskRequest) -> dict[str, Any]:
       if req.mask is None and req.types is None:
           raise HTTPException(400, "must supply 'mask' or 'types'")
       try:
           if req.types is not None:
               resolved = _LIVE.set_mask_from_names(req.types)
           else:
               resolved = _LIVE.set_mask_from_int(int(req.mask))
       except RuntimeError as e:
           raise HTTPException(409, str(e))
       except ValueError as e:
           raise HTTPException(400, str(e))
       return {"mask": f"0x{resolved:08x}"}
   
   @router.websocket("/live/ws")
   async def live_ws(ws: WebSocket) -> None:
       await _LIVE.attach_ws(ws)
   ```

   **tools/marvin-perf/tests/test_live.py** — 8 tests using `_FakeSerial` context-managed iterable. Key pattern:
   ```python
   class _FakeSerial:
       def __init__(self, port: str) -> None:
           self.port = port
           self.sent: list[bytes] = []
           self._closed = threading.Event()
           self._entered = False
       def __enter__(self): self._entered = True; return self
       def __exit__(self, *_): self._closed.set()
       def send_command(self, framed): self.sent.append(framed); return len(framed)
       def __iter__(self):
           while not self._closed.is_set():
   ```

```text
 ## Session log
 
+### 2026-05-22 — marvin-perf web viewer: live-mode backend (Phase 1 of 3)
+
+Backend half of "make the browser the iteration surface." Single-tenant live session: one serial reader thread, one open `SerialSource`, one WebSocket peer at a time (a second WS gets close code 4409 with reason `"live already in use"`). REST for control (`/api/live/{start,stop,set-mask,status}`, `/api/serial/ports`), WS for the data stream (`/api/live/ws`); browser sends nothing over WS. No frontend changes yet — frontend live mode + record-types panel is Phase 2; recording start/stop is Phase 3.
+
+**Module shape.** New [`web/live.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py) owns a mutex-guarded `_LiveSession` singleton. Reader thread runs `iter_frames(SerialSource, stats) → decode_record(frame.payload) → _record_to_dict(rec, include_bgr=True)` and posts onto a per-WS-attach `asyncio.Queue` via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`. Disconnects in either direction flow through the same shutdown path that joins the thread and closes the port. `_record_to_dict` is late-bound from `api.py` to avoid the import cycle.
+
+**Recording groundwork.** Added `framed: bytes` field to `FrameBytes`, populated from the same `buf[:total]` slice `iter_frames` already constructs — Phase 3's record path becomes a one-line write of validated frame bytes with no extra CRC compute. The existing `transport.TeeSource` would tee resync garbage too, so it's not the right shape for live recording.
+
+**Strip pixels in WS messages.** Offline mode keeps strip pixels on the dedicated PNG endpoint, but live mode has no `capture_id` to hang a URL off. `_record_to_dict` grew an `include_bgr` flag — when set, Strip records carry `bgr_b64` (base64) so the browser can render client-side onto the existing strip canvas without a server round-trip.
+
+**Tests.** 92/92 pass. New `test_iter_frames_yields_framed_bytes`, plus 8 in `test_live.py` (lifecycle, mask round-trip via fake `SerialSource`, error paths, status). Test injection point on `_LiveSession.start(port, *, ser_factory=...)` lets unit tests substitute a context-managed fake that yields nothing until `__exit__` fires — exercises the thread-join and stop-event paths without real serial.
+
+**Out of scope this commit:** all frontend changes (mode toggle, port `<select>`, record-types checkboxes, sliding-window timeline append, client-side strip render, WS reconnect) and the recording REST routes. Verification beyond unit tests waits on the frontend landing — `curl POST /api/live/start` + `websocat ws://…/api/live/ws` is the Phase-1 hardware smoke check.
+
 ### 2026-05-22 — perf-log host→device record-type masking
 
 Bidirectional control on the perf-log channel. Host can now narrow which record types the device emits per-capture without rebuilding firmware. Default is all-on (parity with prior behavior); host sends a `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK` over the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer that's used for records, with a distinct command magic (`0x4D43` 'MC' vs records' `0x4D56` 'MV') so misrouted bytes can't be parsed in the wrong direction.
```

```text
116	    api(`/api/capture/${enc}/summary`),
117	    api(`/api/capture/${enc}/health`),
118	    api(`/api/capture/${enc}/rtos`),
119	    api(`/api/capture/${enc}/records?limit=100000`),
120	  ]);
121	  state.summary = summary;
122	  state.health = health;
123	  state.rtos = rtos;
124	  state.records = recs.records;
125	  state.timerFreqHz = summary.timer_freq_hz || 0;
126	  state.ts0 = state.records.length ? state.records[0].ts_counter : 0;
127	  state.playheadTs = state.ts0;
128	  state.fsm = "loaded";
129	
130	  indexByKind();
131	  renderManifestBanner();
132	  renderInspector();
133	  renderBadges();
134	  renderTimeline();
135	  renderRtosPanel();
136	  renderStripSlots();
137	  updatePlayheadDisplay();
138	  setBanner("");
139	}
140	
141	function indexByKind() {
142	  state.byKind = {};
143	  for (const r of state.records) {
144	    if (typeof r.kind !== "number") continue;
145	    (state.byKind[r.kind] ||= []).push(r);
146	  }
147	  for (const k of Object.keys(state.byKind)) {
148	    state.byKind[k].sort((a, b) => a.ts_counter - b.ts_counter);
149	  }
150	}

154	function renderManifestBanner() {
155	  const m = state.manifest;
156	  const s = state.summary;
157	  const msgs = [];
158	  if (s && s.schema_ok === false) {
159	    msgs.push(`schema mismatch: ${s.schema_message}`);
160	  }
161	  if (m && m.producer_capabilities && !m.producer_capabilities.includes("Strip")) {
162	    msgs.push("v1 capture — no strip records yet");
163	  }
164	  if (msgs.length) setBanner(msgs.join("  ·  "));

181	// ── Inspector content ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
182	
183	function nearestAtOrBefore(records, ts) {
184	  // Binary search on ts_counter ascending.
185	  let lo = 0, hi = records.length - 1, best = -1;
186	  while (lo <= hi) {
187	    const mid = (lo + hi) >> 1;
188	    if (records[mid].ts_counter <= ts) { best = mid; lo = mid + 1; }
189	    else hi = mid - 1;
190	  }
191	  return best >= 0 ? records[best] : null;
192	}
193	
194	function renderInspector() {
195	  const m = state.manifest || {};
196	  fillMeta($("#session-meta"), [
197	    ["schema", m.schema_version ?? "—"],
198	    ["timer_hz", m.timer_freq_hz ?? "—"],
199	    ["fw_git", m.fw_git_short ?? "—"],
200	    ["captured", m.captured_at ?? "—"],
201	    ["epoch first", m.frame_epoch_first ?? "—"],
202	    ["epoch last", m.frame_epoch_last ?? "—"],
203	    ["records", m.n_records ?? state.records.length],
204	    ["producers", (m.producer_capabilities || []).join(", ") || "—"],
205	  ]);
206	
207	  const s = state.summary || {};
208	  const drops = s.drops || {};
209	  fillMeta($("#drops-meta"), [
210	    ["state", drops.since_session_state ?? 0],
211	    ["patch", drops.since_session_patch ?? 0],
212	    ["sink B", drops.since_session_sink_bytes ?? 0],
213	    ["max Δstate", drops.max_state_delta ?? 0],
214	    ["max Δpatch", drops.max_patch_delta ?? 0],
215	    ["max Δsink", drops.max_sink_bytes_delta ?? 0],
216	  ]);
217	
218	  const warns = (s.warnings || []);
219	  const ul = $("#warnings-list");
220	  ul.innerHTML = "";
221	  if (warns.length === 0) {
222	    ul.classList.add("empty");
223	  } else {
224	    ul.classList.remove("empty");
225	    for (const w of warns) {
226	      const li = document.createElement("li");
227	      li.textContent = `${w.kind}: ${w.message}`;
228	      ul.appendChild(li);
229	    }
230	  }
231	
232	  updatePlayheadInspector();
233	}

235	function updatePlayheadInspector() {
236	  const rec = nearestAtOrBefore(state.records, state.playheadTs);
237	  if (!rec) { fillMeta($("#event-meta"), []); return; }
238	  const rows = [["type", rec.type]];
239	  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(rec)) {
240	    if (k === "type") continue;
241	    rows.push([k, typeof v === "object" ? JSON.stringify(v) : v]);
242	  }
243	  fillMeta($("#event-meta"), rows);
244	}

248	function renderRtosPanel() {
249	  const r = state.rtos;
250	  const tbl = $("#rtos-table");
251	  tbl.innerHTML = "";
252	  if (!r || !r.tasks || r.tasks.length === 0) {
253	    tbl.innerHTML = "<tr><td>(no RTOS records)</td></tr>";
254	    Plotly.purge("rtos-hwm-chart");
255	    return;
256	  }
257	  const head = document.createElement("tr");

259	    const th = document.createElement("th"); th.textContent = h; head.appendChild(th);

261	  tbl.appendChild(head);
262	  for (const t of r.tasks) {
263	    const tr = document.createElement("tr");

265	      t.task_name, t.task_id,
266	      t.hwm_words.min ?? "—",
267	      t.hwm_words.first ?? "—",
268	      t.hwm_words.last ?? "—",
269	      (t.hwm_words.samples || []).length,
270	    ];
271	    cells.forEach((c, i) => {
272	      const td = document.createElement("td"); td.textContent = String(c);
273	      if (i === 2 && typeof c === "number") {
274	        if (c < 32) td.classList.add("danger");
275	        else if (c < 64) td.classList.add("warn");
276	      }
277	      tr.appendChild(td);
278	    });
279	    tbl.appendChild(tr);
280	  }
281	
282	  // HWM trend per task: Plotly line chart.
283	  const traces = r.tasks.map((t) => {
284	    const xs = (t.hwm_words.samples || []).map(([ts]) => tickToMs(ts));
285	    const ys = (t.hwm_words.samples || []).map(([, w]) => w);
286	    return { x: xs, y: ys, name: t.task_name, mode: "lines+markers", type: "scatter" };
287	  });
288	  Plotly.newPlot("rtos-hwm-chart", traces, {
289	    margin: { l: 36, r: 8, t: 4, b: 28 },
290	    paper_bgcolor: "#1d2229", plot_bgcolor: "#1d2229",
291	    font: { color: "#d4d8de", size: 10 },
292	    xaxis: { title: "ms", gridcolor: "#303843", zerolinecolor: "#303843" },
293	    yaxis: { title: "free words", gridcolor: "#303843", zerolinecolor: "#303843" },
294	    legend: { orientation: "h", y: -0.25 },
295	    showlegend: true,
296	  }, { displayModeBar: false, responsive: true });
297	}

299	function tickToMs(ts) {
300	  if (!state.timerFreqHz) return ts;
301	  return ((ts - state.ts0) / state.timerFreqHz) * 1000.0;
302	}

306	function renderBadges() {
307	  const h = state.health || {};
308	  const f = h.framing || {};
309	  const d = h.drops_since_session || {};
310	  let level = "green", label = "link ●";
311	  if ((f.crc_mismatches || 0) > 0 || (f.bytes_resync_dropped || 0) > 0) {
312	    level = "red"; label = `link ✗ ${f.crc_mismatches || 0} crc`;
313	  } else if ((d.state_records || 0) + (d.patch_records || 0) + (d.sink_bytes || 0) > 0) {
314	    level = "yellow"; label = "link drops";

316	  setBadge("badge-link", level, label);

319	  const t = r.totals || {};

321	  if (t.any_task_below_32_words) { rl = "red"; rt = "rtos <32w"; }
322	  else if (t.any_task_below_64_words) { rl = "yellow"; rt = "rtos <64w"; }
323	  setBadge("badge-rtos", rl, rt);

326	// ── Strip slots ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
327	
328	function renderStripSlots() {
329	  const wrap = $("#strip-slots");
330	  wrap.innerHTML = "";
331	  const observedKinds = Object.keys(state.byKind).map(Number);
332	  const m = state.manifest || {};
333	  const hasStripProducer = (m.producer_capabilities || []).includes("Strip");
334	
335	  if (observedKinds.length === 0 && !hasStripProducer) {
336	    $("#strip-hint").classList.remove("hidden");
337	    $("#strip-hint").textContent = "No STRIP records — Phase 2 wires producers.";
338	    return;
339	  }
340	  $("#strip-hint").classList.add("hidden");
341	
342	  // Take the first record per kind as the canonical (x, y, w, h). All records
343	  // for a kind share the same crop window today (producer-side constants), so
344	  // bbox computed once is correct for every frame.
345	  const knownKinds = Object.keys(STRIP_KIND_REGISTRY).map(Number);
346	  const allKinds = Array.from(new Set([...knownKinds, ...observedKinds]));
347	  const positioned = [];
348	  const unpositioned = [];
349	  for (const kind of allKinds) {
350	    const cfg = STRIP_KIND_REGISTRY[kind];
351	    const id = cfg ? cfg.id : `kind-${kind}`;
352	    const label = cfg ? cfg.label : `Kind ${kind} (unknown)`;
353	    const color = cfg ? cfg.color : "#8a93a0";
354	    const recs = state.byKind[kind] || [];
355	    const sample = recs[0];
356	    if (sample) {
357	      positioned.push({ kind, id, label, color, recs,
358	                        x: sample.x, y: sample.y, w: sample.w, h: sample.h });
359	    } else {
360	      unpositioned.push({ kind, id, label, color });
361	    }
362	  }
363	
364	  if (positioned.length > 0) {
365	    const minX = Math.min(...positioned.map((p) => p.x));
366	    const minY = Math.min(...positioned.map((p) => p.y));
367	    const maxX = Math.max(...positioned.map((p) => p.x + p.w));
368	    const maxY = Math.max(...positioned.map((p) => p.y + p.h));
369	    const z = STRIP_PANE_ZOOM;
370	
371	    const legend = document.createElement("div");
372	    legend.className = "strip-legend";
373	    for (const p of positioned) {
374	      const li = document.createElement("span");
375	      li.className = "strip-legend-item";
376	      li.innerHTML = `<span class="dot" style="background:${p.color}"></span>` +
377	                     `${p.label} · ${p.w}×${p.h} @ (${p.x},${p.y}) · ${p.recs.length} samples`;
378	      legend.appendChild(li);
379	    }
380	    wrap.appendChild(legend);
381	
382	    const pane = document.createElement("div");
383	    pane.className = "strip-pane";
384	    pane.style.width  = `${(maxX - minX) * z}px`;
385	    pane.style.height = `${(maxY - minY) * z}px`;
386	    pane.dataset.bboxOriginX = String(minX);
387	    pane.dataset.bboxOriginY = String(minY);
388	
389	    for (const p of positioned) {
390	      const card = document.createElement("div");
391	      card.className = "strip-card positioned";
392	      card.dataset.kind = String(p.kind);
393	      card.style.left   = `${(p.x - minX) * z}px`;
394	      card.style.top    = `${(p.y - minY) * z}px`;
395	      card.style.width  = `${p.w * z}px`;
396	      card.style.height = `${p.h * z}px`;
397	      card.style.outlineColor = p.color;
398	
399	      const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
400	      canvas.id = `strip-canvas-${p.id}`;
401	      canvas.width  = p.w;
402	      canvas.height = p.h;
403	      canvas.style.width  = `${p.w * z}px`;
404	      canvas.style.height = `${p.h * z}px`;
405	      card.appendChild(canvas);
406	      pane.appendChild(card);
407	    }
408	    wrap.appendChild(pane);
409	  }
410	
411	  if (unpositioned.length > 0) {
412	    const empty = document.createElement("div");
413	    empty.className = "strip-empty-list";
414	    for (const p of unpositioned) {
415	      const item = document.createElement("div");
416	      item.className = "strip-empty-item";
417	      item.innerHTML = `<span class="dot" style="background:${p.color}"></span>` +
418	                       `${p.label} · (no samples)`;
419	      empty.appendChild(item);
420	    }
421	    wrap.appendChild(empty);
422	  }
423	}
424	
425	function updateStripsAtPlayhead() {
426	  const tolTicks = state.timerFreqHz ? state.timerFreqHz / 60 * 1.5 : Infinity;
427	  for (const kindStr of Object.keys(state.byKind)) {
428	    const kind = Number(kindStr);
429	    const recs = state.byKind[kind];
430	    const rec = nearestAtOrBefore(recs, state.playheadTs);
431	    if (!rec) continue;
432	    if (state.playheadTs - rec.ts_counter > tolTicks) continue;
433	    const cfg = STRIP_KIND_REGISTRY[kind];
434	    const id = cfg ? cfg.id : `kind-${kind}`;
435	    const canvas = document.getElementById(`strip-canvas-${id}`);
436	    if (!canvas) continue;
437	    const img = new Image();
438	    img.onload = () => {
439	      if (canvas.width !== img.width || canvas.height !== img.height) {
440	        canvas.width = img.width; canvas.height = img.height;
441	        canvas.style.width = `${img.width * STRIP_PANE_ZOOM}px`;
442	        canvas.style.height = `${img.height * STRIP_PANE_ZOOM}px`;
443	      }
444	      const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
445	      ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
446	      ctx.drawImage(img, 0, 0);
447	    };
448	    const enc = encodeURIComponent(state.captureId);
449	    img.src = `/api/capture/${enc}/strip/${rec.frame_epoch}/${cfg ? cfg.id : kind}.png`;
450	  }
451	}

453	// ── Timeline ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
454	
455	function renderTimeline() {
456	  const stamps = state.records.filter((r) => r.type === "Stamp");
457	  const drops = state.records.filter((r) => r.type === "Drop");
458	
459	  const stampsByStage = {};
460	  for (const s of stamps) {
461	    (stampsByStage[s.stage] ||= []).push(s);
462	  }
463	  const stampTraces = Object.entries(stampsByStage).map(([stage, recs]) => ({
464	    x: recs.map((r) => tickToMs(r.ts_counter)),
465	    y: recs.map(() => stage),
466	    text: recs.map((r) => `epoch ${r.frame_epoch}`),
467	    name: stage,
468	    mode: "markers",
469	    type: "scatter",
470	    marker: { color: STAGE_COLORS[stage] || STAGE_FALLBACK, size: 8, symbol: "line-ns-open" },
471	  }));
472	
473	  const dropTrace = {
474	    x: drops.map((r) => tickToMs(r.ts_counter)),
475	    y: drops.map(() => "DROP"),
476	    text: drops.map((r) => `state=${r.dropped_state} strip=${r.dropped_strip} sink=${r.dropped_sink}`),
477	    name: "Drop",
478	    mode: "markers",
479	    type: "scatter",
480	    marker: { color: "#f87171", size: 10, symbol: "triangle-down" },
481	  };
482	
483	  const traces = [...stampTraces, dropTrace];
484	
485	  const lastTs = state.records.length
486	    ? state.records[state.records.length - 1].ts_counter
487	    : state.ts0 + 1;
488	  const xMax = Math.max(1, tickToMs(lastTs));
489	
490	  const layout = {
491	    margin: { l: 140, r: 12, t: 8, b: 32 },
492	    paper_bgcolor: "#1d2229",
493	    plot_bgcolor: "#1d2229",
494	    font: { color: "#d4d8de", size: 11 },
495	    xaxis: {
496	      title: "ms since session",
497	      range: [0, xMax],
498	      gridcolor: "#303843", zerolinecolor: "#303843",
499	    },
500	    yaxis: {
501	      type: "category",
502	      automargin: true,
503	      gridcolor: "#262d36",
504	    },
505	    showlegend: false,
506	    shapes: [playheadShape()],
507	  };
508	
509	  Plotly.newPlot("timeline-chart", traces, layout, {
510	    displayModeBar: false, responsive: true,
511	  });
512	
513	  $("#timeline-chart").on("plotly_click", (ev) => {
514	    if (!ev.points || !ev.points.length) return;
515	    const ms = ev.points[0].x;
516	    const ticks = state.ts0 + (ms / 1000.0) * state.timerFreqHz;
517	    seekTo(ticks);
518	  });
519	}
520	
521	function playheadShape() {
522	  const xMs = tickToMs(state.playheadTs);
523	  return {
524	    type: "line",
525	    x0: xMs, x1: xMs, y0: 0, y1: 1,
526	    yref: "paper",
527	    line: { color: "#facc15", width: 1.5, dash: "dot" },
528	  };
529	}
530	
531	function refreshPlayheadShape() {
532	  const node = document.getElementById("timeline-chart");
533	  if (!node || !node.layout) return;
534	  Plotly.relayout(node, { shapes: [playheadShape()] });
535	}
536	
537	// ── Playhead / playback FSM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
538	
539	function updatePlayheadDisplay() {
540	  const rec = nearestAtOrBefore(state.records, state.playheadTs);
541	  $("#ph-epoch").textContent = rec ? rec.frame_epoch : "—";
542	  $("#ph-ts").textContent = state.records.length ? fmtMs(state.playheadTs) : "—";
543	  updatePlayheadInspector();
544	  updateStripsAtPlayhead();
545	  refreshPlayheadShape();
546	}
547	
548	function seekTo(ticks) {
549	  if (!state.records.length) return;
550	  const first = state.records[0].ts_counter;
551	  const last = state.records[state.records.length - 1].ts_counter;
552	  state.playheadTs = Math.max(first, Math.min(last, ticks));
553	  updatePlayheadDisplay();
554	}
555	
556	function stepEvent(dir) {
557	  if (!state.records.length) return;
558	  const cur = state.playheadTs;
559	  if (dir > 0) {
560	    const next = state.records.find((r) => r.ts_counter > cur);
561	    if (next) seekTo(next.ts_counter);
562	  } else {
563	    let prev = null;
564	    for (const r of state.records) {
565	      if (r.ts_counter < cur) prev = r; else break;
566	    }
567	    if (prev) seekTo(prev.ts_counter);
568	  }
569	}
570	
571	function stepEpoch(dir) {
572	  if (!state.records.length) return;
573	  const curRec = nearestAtOrBefore(state.records, state.playheadTs);
574	  if (!curRec) return;
575	  const target = curRec.frame_epoch + (dir > 0 ? 1 : -1);
576	  let candidate = null;
577	  for (const r of state.records) {
578	    if (r.frame_epoch === target) {
579	      if (dir > 0) { candidate = r; break; }
580	      else { candidate = r; }
581	    }
582	  }
583	  if (candidate) seekTo(candidate.ts_counter);
584	}
585	
586	function play() {
587	  if (state.fsm === "playing" || !state.records.length) return;
588	  state.fsm = "playing";
589	  $("#play-pause").textContent = "⏸";
590	  state.rafLastWall = performance.now();
591	  const tick = (now) => {
592	    if (state.fsm !== "playing") return;
593	    const dWall = (now - state.rafLastWall) / 1000.0;
594	    state.rafLastWall = now;
595	    const dTicks = dWall * state.speed * (state.timerFreqHz || 1);
596	    const last = state.records[state.records.length - 1].ts_counter;
597	    const newTs = state.playheadTs + dTicks;
598	    if (newTs >= last) { seekTo(last); pause(); return; }
599	    state.playheadTs = newTs;
600	    updatePlayheadDisplay();
601	    state.rafHandle = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
602	  };
603	  state.rafHandle = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
604	}
605	
606	function pause() {
607	  if (state.fsm !== "playing") return;
608	  state.fsm = "paused";
609	  $("#play-pause").textContent = "▶";
610	  if (state.rafHandle) cancelAnimationFrame(state.rafHandle);
611	  state.rafHandle = null;
612	}
613	
614	function togglePlay() {
615	  if (state.fsm === "playing") pause(); else play();
616	}
617	
618	function changeSpeed(delta) {
619	  const choices = [0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4];
620	  const sel = $("#speed");
621	  let idx = choices.indexOf(parseFloat(sel.value));
622	  if (idx < 0) idx = 2;
623	  idx = Math.max(0, Math.min(choices.length - 1, idx + delta));
624	  sel.value = String(choices[idx]);
625	  state.speed = choices[idx];
626	}
627	
628	// ── Wire-up ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
629	
630	function setupControls() {
631	  $("#open-btn").addEventListener("click", async () => {
632	    const path = $("#capture-path").value.trim();
633	    if (!path) return;
634	    try { await openCapture(path); }
635	    catch (e) { setBanner(e.message, "error"); }
636	  });
637	  $("#capture-path").addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
638	    if (e.key === "Enter") $("#open-btn").click();
639	  });
640	  $("#play-pause").addEventListener("click", togglePlay);
641	  $("#step-prev").addEventListener("click", () => stepEvent(-1));
642	  $("#step-next").addEventListener("click", () => stepEvent(1));
643	  $("#speed").addEventListener("change", (e) => {
644	    state.speed = parseFloat(e.target.value);
645	  });
646	
647	  document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
648	    const tag = (e.target && e.target.tagName) || "";
649	    if (tag === "INPUT" || tag === "SELECT" || tag === "TEXTAREA") return;
650	    switch (e.key) {
651	      case " ":          e.preventDefault(); togglePlay(); break;
652	      case "ArrowLeft":   e.shiftKey ? stepEpoch(-1) : stepEvent(-1); break;
653	      case "ArrowRight":  e.shiftKey ? stepEpoch(1)  : stepEvent(1);  break;
654	      case "[":           changeSpeed(-1); break;
655	      case "]":           changeSpeed(1);  break;
656	    }
657	  });
658	}
659	
660	async function probePreloaded() {
661	  try {

666	    }
667	  } catch (e) {
668	    // Endpoint may not be available; fall through to manual open.
669	  }
670	}
```

```text
1	"""Single-tenant live session: serial reader thread + WS push.
2	
3	The reader thread owns the open SerialSource and runs the frame decoder.
4	Decoded records are pushed onto a per-WS-attach asyncio.Queue via
5	``loop.call_soon_threadsafe``. The CLI's `live`/`set-mask` primitives are
6	reused — `frame_encode`, `encode_set_mask_payload`, `SerialSource.send_command`
7	— so the wire-level concerns sit in transport.py / framing.py / records.py
8	and this module only composes them.
9	
10	Recording (write framed bytes to a capture dir) is wired in Phase 3.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import asyncio
16	import threading
17	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
18	from datetime import datetime, timezone
19	from typing import Any
20	
21	from fastapi import WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect
22	
23	from ..decode import decode_record
24	from ..framing import FrameStats, frame_encode, iter_frames
25	from ..records import (
26	    RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME,
27	    Session,
28	    encode_set_mask_payload,
29	)
30	from ..transport import SerialSource
31	
32	
33	_QUEUE_MAX = 10_000
34	
35	
36	@dataclass
37	class _State:
38	    port: str | None = None
39	    mask: int = 0xFFFFFFFF
40	    started_at: str | None = None
41	    framing_stats: FrameStats = field(default_factory=FrameStats)
42	    last_session_dict: dict[str, Any] | None = None
43	
44	
45	class _LiveSession:
46	    """Process-singleton; mutex guards all field writes."""
47	
48	    def __init__(self) -> None:
49	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
50	        self._state = _State()
51	        self._ser: SerialSource | None = None
52	        self._thread: threading.Thread | None = None
53	        self._stop_event = threading.Event()
54	        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] | None = None
55	        self._loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop | None = None
56	        self._ws: WebSocket | None = None
57	        # Late-bound to avoid a cycle: api.py passes this on import.
58	        self._record_to_dict = None  # type: ignore[var-annotated]
59	
60	    # ─── lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
61	
62	    def configure(self, *, record_to_dict) -> None:
63	        self._record_to_dict = record_to_dict
64	
65	    def is_active(self) -> bool:
66	        with self._lock:
67	            return self._thread is not None and self._thread.is_alive()
68	
69	    def start(self, port: str, *, ser_factory=None) -> None:
70	        """Open serial + start reader thread.
71	
72	        ``ser_factory`` is an injection point for tests — if provided, called
73	        as ``ser_factory(port)`` and expected to return a context-manager
74	        iterable (yields bytes chunks) with ``send_command``.
75	        """
76	        with self._lock:
77	            if self.is_active():
78	                raise RuntimeError("live session already active")
79	            self._stop_event.clear()
80	            self._state = _State(
81	                port=port,
82	                started_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
83	            )
84	            ser = (ser_factory or SerialSource)(port)
85	            ser.__enter__()
86	            self._ser = ser
87	            self._thread = threading.Thread(
88	                target=self._reader_loop,
89	                name="marvin-perf-live",
90	                daemon=True,
91	            )
92	            self._thread.start()
93	
94	    def stop(self) -> None:
95	        """Idempotent: safe to call when not active."""
96	        with self._lock:
97	            self._stop_event.set()
98	            ser = self._ser
99	            self._ser = None
100	            t = self._thread
101	            self._thread = None
102	        if ser is not None:
103	            try:
104	                ser.__exit__(None, None, None)
105	            except Exception:
106	                pass
107	        if t is not None and t.is_alive():
108	            t.join(timeout=3.0)
109	
110	    # ─── control plane ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
111	
112	    def set_mask_from_int(self, mask: int) -> int:
113	        m = mask & 0xFFFFFFFF
114	        with self._lock:
115	            ser = self._ser
116	            if ser is None:
117	                raise RuntimeError("live session not active")
118	            self._state.mask = m
119	        ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_set_mask_payload(m)))
120	        self._post("mask", {"value": f"0x{m:08x}", "source": "client"})
121	        return m
122	
123	    def set_mask_from_names(self, names: list[str]) -> int:
124	        mask = 0
125	        for raw in names:
126	            token = raw.strip().upper()
127	            if not token:
128	                continue
129	            if token == "ALL":
130	                mask = 0xFFFFFFFF
131	                break
132	            if token not in RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME:
133	                valid = ", ".join(sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME))
134	                raise ValueError(f"unknown record type {token!r}; valid: {valid}, ALL")
135	            mask |= 1 << RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME[token]
136	        return self.set_mask_from_int(mask)
137	
138	    def status(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
139	        with self._lock:
140	            active = self.is_active()
141	            return {
142	                "active": active,
143	                "port": self._state.port if active else None,
144	                "mask": f"0x{self._state.mask:08x}" if active else None,
145	                "recording": None,  # Phase 3
146	                "started_at": self._state.started_at if active else None,
147	                "framing": {
148	                    "frames_ok": self._state.framing_stats.frames_ok,
149	                    "crc_err": self._state.framing_stats.crc_mismatches,
150	                    "resync_drop": self._state.framing_stats.bytes_resync_dropped,
151	                    "bad_lengths": self._state.framing_stats.bad_lengths,
152	                },
153	            }
154	
155	    # ─── WS attachment ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
156	
157	    async def attach_ws(self, ws: WebSocket) -> None:
158	        with self._lock:
159	            if self._ws is not None:
160	                await ws.close(code=4409, reason="live already in use")
161	                return
162	            if not self.is_active():
163	                await ws.close(code=4404, reason="no active live session")
164	                return
165	            self._loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
166	            self._queue = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=_QUEUE_MAX)
167	            self._ws = ws
168	
169	        await ws.accept()
170	        with self._lock:
171	            hello = {
172	                "type": "hello",
173	                "session": {
174	                    "started_at": self._state.started_at,
175	                    "port": self._state.port,
176	                    "mask": f"0x{self._state.mask:08x}",
177	                    "recording": None,
178	                },
179	            }
180	            replay = self._state.last_session_dict
181	        try:
182	            await ws.send_json(hello)
183	            if replay is not None:
184	                await ws.send_json({"type": "session_replay", "rec": replay})
185	            queue = self._queue
186	            while True:
187	                msg_type, payload = await queue.get()
188	                if msg_type == "record":
189	                    await ws.send_json({"type": "record", "rec": payload})
190	                elif msg_type == "mask":
191	                    await ws.send_json({"type": "mask", **payload})
192	                elif msg_type == "error":
193	                    await ws.send_json({"type": "error", **payload})
194	                    break
195	                elif msg_type == "framing_stats":
196	                    await ws.send_json({"type": "framing_stats", **payload})
197	        except WebSocketDisconnect:
198	            pass
199	        finally:
200	            with self._lock:
201	                self._ws = None
202	                self._queue = None
203	
204	    # ─── reader thread ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
205	
206	    def _reader_loop(self) -> None:
207	        ser = self._ser
208	        stats = self._state.framing_stats
209	        if ser is None:
210	            return
211	        try:
212	            for frame in iter_frames(ser, stats):
213	                if self._stop_event.is_set():
214	                    break
215	                try:
216	                    rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
217	                except Exception:
218	                    continue
219	                if self._record_to_dict is None:
220	                    continue
221	                rec_dict = self._record_to_dict(rec, include_bgr=True)
222	                if isinstance(rec, Session):
223	                    with self._lock:
224	                        self._state.last_session_dict = rec_dict
225	                self._post("record", rec_dict)
226	        except Exception as e:
227	            self._post("error", {"code": "serial-error", "msg": str(e)})
228	
229	    # ─── internal: cross-thread queue post ──────────────────────────────
230	
231	    def _post(self, msg_type: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
232	        loop = self._loop
233	        queue = self._queue
234	        if loop is None or queue is None:
235	            return
236	        try:
237	            loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._queue_put_nowait, msg_type, payload)
238	        except RuntimeError:
239	            pass
240	
241	    def _queue_put_nowait(self, msg_type: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
242	        # Runs on the asyncio loop thread.
243	        if self._queue is None:
244	            return
245	        try:
246	            self._queue.put_nowait((msg_type, payload))
247	        except asyncio.QueueFull:
248	            pass
249	
250	
251	SESSION = _LiveSession()
```

 `./firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`

```text
137	
138	## Session log
139	
140	### 2026-05-22 — marvin-perf web viewer: live-mode backend (Phase 1 of 3)
141	
142	Backend half of "make the browser the iteration surface." Single-tenant live session: one serial reader thread, one open `SerialSource`, one WebSocket peer at a time (a second WS gets close code 4409 with reason `"live already in use"`). REST for control (`/api/live/{start,stop,set-mask,status}`, `/api/serial/ports`), WS for the data stream (`/api/live/ws`); browser sends nothing over WS. No frontend changes yet — frontend live mode + record-types panel is Phase 2; recording start/stop is Phase 3.
143	
144	**Module shape.** New [`web/live.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py) owns a mutex-guarded `_LiveSession` singleton. Reader thread runs `iter_frames(SerialSource, stats) → decode_record(frame.payload) → _record_to_dict(rec, include_bgr=True)` and posts onto a per-WS-attach `asyncio.Queue` via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`. Disconnects in either direction flow through the same shutdown path that joins the thread and closes the port. `_record_to_dict` is late-bound from `api.py` to avoid the import cycle.
145	
146	**Recording groundwork.** Added `framed: bytes` field to `FrameBytes`, populated from the same `buf[:total]` slice `iter_frames` already constructs — Phase 3's record path becomes a one-line write of validated frame bytes with no extra CRC compute. The existing `transport.TeeSource` would tee resync garbage too, so it's not the right shape for live recording.
147	
148	**Strip pixels in WS messages.** Offline mode keeps strip pixels on the dedicated PNG endpoint, but live mode has no `capture_id` to hang a URL off. `_record_to_dict` grew an `include_bgr` flag — when set, Strip records carry `bgr_b64` (base64) so the browser can render client-side onto the existing strip canvas without a server round-trip.
149	
150	**Tests.** 92/92 pass. New `test_iter_frames_yields_framed_bytes`, plus 8 in `test_live.py` (lifecycle, mask round-trip via fake `SerialSource`, error paths, status). Test injection point on `_LiveSession.start(port, *, ser_factory=...)` lets unit tests substitute a context-managed fake that yields nothing until `__exit__` fires — exercises the thread-join and stop-event paths without real serial.
151	
152	**Out of scope this commit:** all frontend changes (mode toggle, port `<select>`, record-types checkboxes, sliding-window timeline append, client-side strip render, WS reconnect) and the recording REST routes. Verification beyond unit tests waits on the frontend landing — `curl POST /api/live/start` + `websocat ws://…/api/live/ws` is the Phase-1 hardware smoke check.
153	
154	### 2026-05-22 — perf-log host→device record-type masking
155	
156	Bidirectional control on the perf-log channel. Host can now narrow which record types the device emits per-capture without rebuilding firmware. Default is all-on (parity with prior behavior); host sends a `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK` over the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer that's used for records, with a distinct command magic (`0x4D43` 'MC' vs records' `0x4D56` 'MV') so misrouted bytes can't be parsed in the wrong direction.
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 22:36:41Z)**_

I've worked it out. The server's WS push queue (10k items deep) backs up under STRIP traffic at 60 Hz × ~10 KB — a mask toggle takes ~10 s to visibly take effect because the queue keeps draining stale data. That also explains the jumpy UI: JS falls farther behind real time as the queue saturates.

Three fixes:

1. **Default STRIP off** in the types panel — on by default is too much for the WS+JSON pipe at 60 Hz.
2. **Drop-oldest queue + smaller depth + flush on mask change** in `live.py` — bounds the staleness toggle window.
3. **Clear local buffer on mask toggle** in the client so the user sees fresh records immediately.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - perf-log v2 wire format: SOF + LEN(u16 LE) + PAYLOAD + CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE
   - PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC=0x4D56 ('MV') for records; PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC=0x4D43 ('MC') for commands
   - PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK = 0x01: bit i corresponds to RecordType enum value i
   - RecordType: SESSION=1, STAMP=2, DETECTOR=3, TIMING=4, STRIP=5, DROP=6, TASK_HIGHWATER=7, TASK_RUNTIME=8
   - TYPE_MASK_ALL=0xFFFFFFFF; TYPE_MASK_MIN=(1<<1)|(1<<6)=0x42 (SESSION+DROP)
   - Single-tenant live session: one serial reader thread + asyncio.Queue + WS push
   - WS close codes: 4409 "live already in use", 4404 "no active live session"
   - Late-binding: api.py calls `_LIVE.configure(record_to_dict=...)` to avoid import cycle
   - Strip records carry BGR pixels; live mode adds `bgr_b64` (base64) field via `include_bgr=True` to `_record_to_dict`; client decodes BGR→RGBA per-pixel byte-swap → ImageData → putImageData
   - Sliding-window buffer (30s by ts_counter, 50k record cap) for live mode
   - Plotly used via newPlot (full re-init); debounce-throttled to combat redraw cost
   - JS bitwise unsigned via `>>> 0`
   - Static FreeRTOS memory only; no malloc
   - User builds firmware in MPLAB X — Claude must NOT try to build firmware

   ```js
   const RECORD_TYPES = [
     { name: "SESSION",        bit: 1, alwaysOn: true,  defaultOn: true  },
     { name: "STAMP",          bit: 2, alwaysOn: false, defaultOn: true  },
     { name: "DETECTOR",       bit: 3, alwaysOn: false, defaultOn: true  },
     { name: "TIMING",         bit: 4, alwaysOn: false, defaultOn: true  },
     // STRIP carries ~10 KB/frame at 60 Hz × 2 kinds — opt-in
     { name: "STRIP",          bit: 5, alwaysOn: false, defaultOn: false },
     { name: "DROP",           bit: 6, alwaysOn: false, defaultOn: true  },
     { name: "TASK_HIGHWATER", bit: 7, alwaysOn: false, defaultOn: true  },
     { name: "TASK_RUNTIME",   bit: 8, alwaysOn: false, defaultOn: true  },
   ];
   const MASK_ALL = 0xFFFFFFFF >>> 0;
   const MASK_MIN = ((1 << 1) | (1 << 6)) >>> 0;
   const LIVE_BUFFER_SECONDS = 30;
   const LIVE_MAX_RECORDS = 50_000;

   // state extended with: mode, ws, liveStopRequested, reconnectAttempts,
   // lastSession, pendingRedrawHandle, pendingMaskHandle, liveMask
   
   function paintBgrIntoCanvas(canvas, b64, w, h) {
     if (canvas.width !== w || canvas.height !== h) {
       canvas.width = w; canvas.height = h; ...
     }
     const bin = atob(b64);
     const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
     const img = ctx.createImageData(w, h);
     const data = img.data;
     for (let i = 0, j = 0; i < bin.length; i += 3, j += 4) {
       data[j]     = bin.charCodeAt(i + 2);  // R
       data[j + 1] = bin.charCodeAt(i + 1);  // G
       data[j + 2] = bin.charCodeAt(i);      // B
       data[j + 3] = 255;
     }
     ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
     ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
   }

   function scheduleLiveRedraw() {
     if (state.pendingRedrawHandle != null) return;
     const debounceMs = state.records.length > 5000
       ? LIVE_REDRAW_DEBOUNCE_MS * 4
       : LIVE_REDRAW_DEBOUNCE_MS;
     state.pendingRedrawHandle = setTimeout(() => {
       state.pendingRedrawHandle = null;
       indexByKind();
       renderTimeline();
       updatePlayheadInspector();
   ```

   ```python
               raise RuntimeError("live session not active")
           self._state.mask = m
       ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_set_mask_payload(m)))
       # Drain the WS queue so the browser sees fresh records under the new
       # mask immediately, rather than draining 5–10 s of stale backlog.
       self._drain_queue()
       self._post("mask", {"value": f"0x{m:08x}", "source": "client"})
       return m
   
   def _queue_put_nowait(self, msg_type, payload):
       if self._queue is None:
           return
       try:
           self._queue.put_nowait((msg_type, payload))
       except asyncio.QueueFull:
           try:
               self._queue.get_nowait()  # drop oldest
           except asyncio.QueueEmpty:
               return
           try:
               self._queue.put_nowait((msg_type, payload))
           except asyncio.QueueFull:
               pass
   
   def _drain_queue(self) -> None:
       loop = self._loop
       if loop is None: return
       try:
           loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._queue_drain)
       except RuntimeError:
           pass
   
   def _queue_drain(self) -> None:
       if self._queue is None: return
       while True:
           try:
               self._queue.get_nowait()
           except asyncio.QueueEmpty:
               return
   ```

```text
311	      tr.appendChild(td);
312	    });
313	    tbl.appendChild(tr);
314	  }
315	
316	  // HWM trend per task: Plotly line chart.
317	  const traces = r.tasks.map((t) => {
318	    const xs = (t.hwm_words.samples || []).map(([ts]) => tickToMs(ts));
319	    const ys = (t.hwm_words.samples || []).map(([, w]) => w);
320	    return { x: xs, y: ys, name: t.task_name, mode: "lines+markers", type: "scatter" };
321	  });
322	  Plotly.newPlot("rtos-hwm-chart", traces, {
323	    margin: { l: 36, r: 8, t: 4, b: 28 },
324	    paper_bgcolor: "#1d2229", plot_bgcolor: "#1d2229",
325	    font: { color: "#d4d8de", size: 10 },
326	    xaxis: { title: "ms", gridcolor: "#303843", zerolinecolor: "#303843" },
327	    yaxis: { title: "free words", gridcolor: "#303843", zerolinecolor: "#303843" },
328	    legend: { orientation: "h", y: -0.25 },
329	    showlegend: true,
330	  }, { displayModeBar: false, responsive: true });
331	}
332	
333	function tickToMs(ts) {
334	  if (!state.timerFreqHz) return ts;
335	  return ((ts - state.ts0) / state.timerFreqHz) * 1000.0;
336	}

338	// ── Badges ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

340	function renderBadges() {
341	  const h = state.health || {};
342	  const f = h.framing || {};
343	  const d = h.drops_since_session || {};
344	  let level = "green", label = "link ●";
345	  if ((f.crc_mismatches || 0) > 0 || (f.bytes_resync_dropped || 0) > 0) {
346	    level = "red"; label = `link ✗ ${f.crc_mismatches || 0} crc`;
347	  } else if ((d.state_records || 0) + (d.patch_records || 0) + (d.sink_bytes || 0) > 0) {
348	    level = "yellow"; label = "link drops";
349	  }
350	  setBadge("badge-link", level, label);
351	
352	  const r = state.rtos || {};
353	  const t = r.totals || {};
354	  let rl = "green", rt = "rtos ●";
355	  if (t.any_task_below_32_words) { rl = "red"; rt = "rtos <32w"; }
356	  else if (t.any_task_below_64_words) { rl = "yellow"; rt = "rtos <64w"; }
357	  setBadge("badge-rtos", rl, rt);
358	}
```
