360	// ── Strip slots ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
361	
362	function renderStripSlots() {
363	  const wrap = $("#strip-slots");
364	  wrap.innerHTML = "";
365	  const observedKinds = Object.keys(state.byKind).map(Number);
366	  const m = state.manifest || {};
367	  const hasStripProducer = (m.producer_capabilities || []).includes("Strip");
368	
369	  if (observedKinds.length === 0 && !hasStripProducer) {
370	    $("#strip-hint").classList.remove("hidden");
371	    $("#strip-hint").textContent = "No STRIP records — Phase 2 wires producers.";
372	    return;
373	  }
374	  $("#strip-hint").classList.add("hidden");
375	
376	  // Take the first record per kind as the canonical (x, y, w, h). All records
377	  // for a kind share the same crop window today (producer-side constants), so
378	  // bbox computed once is correct for every frame.
379	  const knownKinds = Object.keys(STRIP_KIND_REGISTRY).map(Number);
380	  const allKinds = Array.from(new Set([...knownKinds, ...observedKinds]));
381	  const positioned = [];
382	  const unpositioned = [];
383	  for (const kind of allKinds) {
384	    const cfg = STRIP_KIND_REGISTRY[kind];
385	    const id = cfg ? cfg.id : `kind-${kind}`;
386	    const label = cfg ? cfg.label : `Kind ${kind} (unknown)`;
387	    const color = cfg ? cfg.color : "#8a93a0";
388	    const recs = state.byKind[kind] || [];
389	    const sample = recs[0];
390	    if (sample) {
391	      positioned.push({ kind, id, label, color, recs,
392	                        x: sample.x, y: sample.y, w: sample.w, h: sample.h });
393	    } else {
394	      unpositioned.push({ kind, id, label, color });
395	    }
396	  }
397	
398	  if (positioned.length > 0) {
399	    const minX = Math.min(...positioned.map((p) => p.x));
400	    const minY = Math.min(...positioned.map((p) => p.y));
401	    const maxX = Math.max(...positioned.map((p) => p.x + p.w));
402	    const maxY = Math.max(...positioned.map((p) => p.y + p.h));
403	    const z = STRIP_PANE_ZOOM;
404	
405	    const legend = document.createElement("div");
406	    legend.className = "strip-legend";
407	    for (const p of positioned) {
408	      const li = document.createElement("span");
409	      li.className = "strip-legend-item";
410	      li.innerHTML = `<span class="dot" style="background:${p.color}"></span>` +
411	                     `${p.label} · ${p.w}×${p.h} @ (${p.x},${p.y}) · ${p.recs.length} samples`;
412	      legend.appendChild(li);
413	    }
414	    wrap.appendChild(legend);
415	
416	    const pane = document.createElement("div");
417	    pane.className = "strip-pane";
418	    pane.style.width  = `${(maxX - minX) * z}px`;
419	    pane.style.height = `${(maxY - minY) * z}px`;
420	    pane.dataset.bboxOriginX = String(minX);
421	    pane.dataset.bboxOriginY = String(minY);
422	
423	    for (const p of positioned) {
424	      const card = document.createElement("div");
425	      card.className = "strip-card positioned";
426	      card.dataset.kind = String(p.kind);
427	      card.style.left   = `${(p.x - minX) * z}px`;
428	      card.style.top    = `${(p.y - minY) * z}px`;
429	      card.style.width  = `${p.w * z}px`;
430	      card.style.height = `${p.h * z}px`;
431	      card.style.outlineColor = p.color;
432	
433	      const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
434	      canvas.id = `strip-canvas-${p.id}`;
435	      canvas.width  = p.w;
436	      canvas.height = p.h;
437	      canvas.style.width  = `${p.w * z}px`;
438	      canvas.style.height = `${p.h * z}px`;
439	      card.appendChild(canvas);
440	      pane.appendChild(card);
441	    }
442	    wrap.appendChild(pane);
443	  }
444	
445	  if (unpositioned.length > 0) {
446	    const empty = document.createElement("div");
447	    empty.className = "strip-empty-list";
448	    for (const p of unpositioned) {
449	      const item = document.createElement("div");
450	      item.className = "strip-empty-item";
451	      item.innerHTML = `<span class="dot" style="background:${p.color}"></span>` +
452	                       `${p.label} · (no samples)`;
453	      empty.appendChild(item);
454	    }
455	    wrap.appendChild(empty);
456	  }
457	}
458	
459	function updateStripsAtPlayhead() {
460	  const tolTicks = state.timerFreqHz ? state.timerFreqHz / 60 * 1.5 : Infinity;
461	  for (const kindStr of Object.keys(state.byKind)) {
462	    const kind = Number(kindStr);
463	    const recs = state.byKind[kind];
464	    const rec = nearestAtOrBefore(recs, state.playheadTs);
465	    if (!rec) continue;
466	    if (state.playheadTs - rec.ts_counter > tolTicks) continue;
467	    const cfg = STRIP_KIND_REGISTRY[kind];
468	    const id = cfg ? cfg.id : `kind-${kind}`;
469	    const canvas = document.getElementById(`strip-canvas-${id}`);
470	    if (!canvas) continue;
471	    if (rec.bgr_b64) {
472	      paintBgrIntoCanvas(canvas, rec.bgr_b64, rec.w, rec.h);
473	      continue;
474	    }
475	    if (!state.captureId) continue;
476	    const img = new Image();
477	    img.onload = () => {
478	      if (canvas.width !== img.width || canvas.height !== img.height) {
479	        canvas.width = img.width; canvas.height = img.height;
480	        canvas.style.width = `${img.width * STRIP_PANE_ZOOM}px`;
481	        canvas.style.height = `${img.height * STRIP_PANE_ZOOM}px`;
482	      }
483	      const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
484	      ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
485	      ctx.drawImage(img, 0, 0);
486	    };
487	    const enc = encodeURIComponent(state.captureId);
488	    img.src = `/api/capture/${enc}/strip/${rec.frame_epoch}/${cfg ? cfg.id : kind}.png`;
489	  }
490	}
491	
492	function paintBgrIntoCanvas(canvas, b64, w, h) {
493	  if (canvas.width !== w || canvas.height !== h) {
494	    canvas.width = w; canvas.height = h;
495	    canvas.style.width = `${w * STRIP_PANE_ZOOM}px`;
496	    canvas.style.height = `${h * STRIP_PANE_ZOOM}px`;
497	  }
498	  const bin = atob(b64);
499	  const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
500	  const img = ctx.createImageData(w, h);
501	  const data = img.data;
502	  // BGR (3 B/pixel) → RGBA (4 B/pixel).
503	  for (let i = 0, j = 0; i < bin.length; i += 3, j += 4) {
504	    data[j]     = bin.charCodeAt(i + 2);
505	    data[j + 1] = bin.charCodeAt(i + 1);
506	    data[j + 2] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
507	    data[j + 3] = 255;
508	  }
509	  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
510	  ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
511	}

513	// ── Timeline ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
514	
515	function renderTimeline() {
516	  const stamps = state.records.filter((r) => r.type === "Stamp");
517	  const drops = state.records.filter((r) => r.type === "Drop");
518	
519	  const stampsByStage = {};
520	  for (const s of stamps) {
521	    (stampsByStage[s.stage] ||= []).push(s);
522	  }
523	  const stampTraces = Object.entries(stampsByStage).map(([stage, recs]) => ({
524	    x: recs.map((r) => tickToMs(r.ts_counter)),
525	    y: recs.map(() => stage),
526	    text: recs.map((r) => `epoch ${r.frame_epoch}`),
527	    name: stage,
528	    mode: "markers",
529	    type: "scatter",
530	    marker: { color: STAGE_COLORS[stage] || STAGE_FALLBACK, size: 8, symbol: "line-ns-open" },
531	  }));
532	
533	  const dropTrace = {
534	    x: drops.map((r) => tickToMs(r.ts_counter)),
535	    y: drops.map(() => "DROP"),
536	    text: drops.map((r) => `state=${r.dropped_state} strip=${r.dropped_strip} sink=${r.dropped_sink}`),
537	    name: "Drop",
538	    mode: "markers",
539	    type: "scatter",
540	    marker: { color: "#f87171", size: 10, symbol: "triangle-down" },
541	  };
542	
543	  const traces = [...stampTraces, dropTrace];
544	
545	  const lastTs = state.records.length
546	    ? state.records[state.records.length - 1].ts_counter
547	    : state.ts0 + 1;
548	  const xMax = Math.max(1, tickToMs(lastTs));
549	
550	  const layout = {
551	    margin: { l: 140, r: 12, t: 8, b: 32 },
552	    paper_bgcolor: "#1d2229",
553	    plot_bgcolor: "#1d2229",
554	    font: { color: "#d4d8de", size: 11 },
555	    xaxis: {
556	      title: "ms since session",
557	      range: [0, xMax],
558	      gridcolor: "#303843", zerolinecolor: "#303843",
559	    },
560	    yaxis: {
561	      type: "category",
562	      automargin: true,
563	      gridcolor: "#262d36",
564	    },
565	    showlegend: false,
566	    shapes: [playheadShape()],
567	  };
568	
569	  Plotly.newPlot("timeline-chart", traces, layout, {
570	    displayModeBar: false, responsive: true,
571	  });
572	
573	  $("#timeline-chart").on("plotly_click", (ev) => {
574	    if (!ev.points || !ev.points.length) return;
575	    const ms = ev.points[0].x;
576	    const ticks = state.ts0 + (ms / 1000.0) * state.timerFreqHz;
577	    seekTo(ticks);
578	  });
579	}
580	
581	function playheadShape() {
582	  const xMs = tickToMs(state.playheadTs);
583	  return {
584	    type: "line",
585	    x0: xMs, x1: xMs, y0: 0, y1: 1,
586	    yref: "paper",
587	    line: { color: "#facc15", width: 1.5, dash: "dot" },
588	  };
589	}
590	
591	function refreshPlayheadShape() {
592	  const node = document.getElementById("timeline-chart");
593	  if (!node || !node.layout) return;
594	  Plotly.relayout(node, { shapes: [playheadShape()] });
595	}

597	// ── Playhead / playback FSM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
598	
599	function updatePlayheadDisplay() {
600	  const rec = nearestAtOrBefore(state.records, state.playheadTs);
601	  $("#ph-epoch").textContent = rec ? rec.frame_epoch : "—";
602	  $("#ph-ts").textContent = state.records.length ? fmtMs(state.playheadTs) : "—";
603	  updatePlayheadInspector();
604	  updateStripsAtPlayhead();
605	  refreshPlayheadShape();
606	}
607	
608	function seekTo(ticks) {
609	  if (!state.records.length) return;
610	  const first = state.records[0].ts_counter;
611	  const last = state.records[state.records.length - 1].ts_counter;
612	  state.playheadTs = Math.max(first, Math.min(last, ticks));
613	  updatePlayheadDisplay();
614	}
615	
616	function stepEvent(dir) {
617	  if (!state.records.length) return;
618	  const cur = state.playheadTs;
619	  if (dir > 0) {
620	    const next = state.records.find((r) => r.ts_counter > cur);
621	    if (next) seekTo(next.ts_counter);
622	  } else {
623	    let prev = null;
624	    for (const r of state.records) {
625	      if (r.ts_counter < cur) prev = r; else break;
626	    }
627	    if (prev) seekTo(prev.ts_counter);
628	  }
629	}
630	
631	function stepEpoch(dir) {
632	  if (!state.records.length) return;
633	  const curRec = nearestAtOrBefore(state.records, state.playheadTs);
634	  if (!curRec) return;
635	  const target = curRec.frame_epoch + (dir > 0 ? 1 : -1);
636	  let candidate = null;
637	  for (const r of state.records) {
638	    if (r.frame_epoch === target) {
639	      if (dir > 0) { candidate = r; break; }
640	      else { candidate = r; }
641	    }
642	  }
643	  if (candidate) seekTo(candidate.ts_counter);
644	}
645	
646	function play() {
647	  if (state.fsm === "playing" || !state.records.length) return;
648	  state.fsm = "playing";
649	  $("#play-pause").textContent = "⏸";
650	  state.rafLastWall = performance.now();
651	  const tick = (now) => {
652	    if (state.fsm !== "playing") return;
653	    const dWall = (now - state.rafLastWall) / 1000.0;
654	    state.rafLastWall = now;
655	    const dTicks = dWall * state.speed * (state.timerFreqHz || 1);
656	    const last = state.records[state.records.length - 1].ts_counter;
657	    const newTs = state.playheadTs + dTicks;
658	    if (newTs >= last) { seekTo(last); pause(); return; }
659	    state.playheadTs = newTs;
660	    updatePlayheadDisplay();
661	    state.rafHandle = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
662	  };
663	  state.rafHandle = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
664	}
665	
666	function pause() {
667	  if (state.fsm !== "playing") return;
668	  state.fsm = "paused";
669	  $("#play-pause").textContent = "▶";
670	  if (state.rafHandle) cancelAnimationFrame(state.rafHandle);
671	  state.rafHandle = null;
672	}
673	
674	function togglePlay() {
675	  if (state.fsm === "playing") pause(); else play();
676	}
677	
678	function changeSpeed(delta) {
679	  const choices = [0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4];
680	  const sel = $("#speed");
681	  let idx = choices.indexOf(parseFloat(sel.value));
682	  if (idx < 0) idx = 2;
683	  idx = Math.max(0, Math.min(choices.length - 1, idx + delta));
684	  sel.value = String(choices[idx]);
685	  state.speed = choices[idx];
686	}

688	// ── Mode toggle ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
689	
690	function setMode(mode) {
691	  if (state.mode === mode) return;
692	  state.mode = mode;
693	  $("#mode-offline").classList.toggle("active", mode === "offline");
694	  $("#mode-live").classList.toggle("active", mode === "live");
695	  $("#offline-controls").classList.toggle("hidden", mode !== "offline");
696	  $("#live-controls").classList.toggle("hidden", mode !== "live");
697	  $("#types-panel").classList.toggle("hidden", mode !== "live");
698	  $("#badge-live").classList.toggle("hidden", mode !== "live");
699	  setLiveTransportEnabled(mode !== "live");
700	
701	  // Reset capture-state when crossing the mode boundary so leftover offline
702	  // records don't bleed into a live session and vice versa.
703	  resetCaptureState();
704	  if (mode === "live") {
705	    buildTypesPanel();
706	    refreshSerialPorts();
707	    setBanner("Pick a port and click Start to stream from the device.");
708	  } else {
709	    closeWS({ userInitiated: true });
710	    setBanner("");
711	  }
712	}
713	
714	function setLiveTransportEnabled(enabled) {
715	  for (const id of ["#step-prev", "#play-pause", "#step-next", "#speed"]) {
716	    const el = $(id);
717	    if (el) el.disabled = !enabled;
718	  }
719	}

721	function resetCaptureState() {
722	  pause();
723	  state.captureId = null;
724	  state.manifest = null;
725	  state.summary = null;
726	  state.health = null;
727	  state.rtos = null;
728	  state.records = [];
729	  state.byKind = {};
730	  state.timerFreqHz = 0;
731	  state.ts0 = 0;
732	  state.playheadTs = 0;
733	  state.fsm = "idle";
734	  state.lastSession = null;
735	  // Clear panels so the previous mode's contents don't linger.
736	  fillMeta($("#event-meta"), []);
737	  fillMeta($("#session-meta"), []);
738	  fillMeta($("#drops-meta"), []);
739	  $("#warnings-list").innerHTML = "";
740	  $("#warnings-list").classList.add("empty");
741	  $("#strip-slots").innerHTML = "";
742	  $("#strip-hint").classList.remove("hidden");
743	  $("#strip-hint").textContent = "(no records yet)";
744	  Plotly.purge("timeline-chart");
745	  Plotly.purge("rtos-hwm-chart");
746	  setBadge("badge-link", null, "link ●");
747	  setBadge("badge-rtos", null, "rtos ●");
748	  $("#ph-epoch").textContent = "—";
749	  $("#ph-ts").textContent = "—";
750	}

752	// ── Live: serial ports ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
753	
754	async function refreshSerialPorts() {
755	  try {
756	    const ports = await api("/api/serial/ports");
757	    const sel = $("#live-port");
758	    const prev = sel.value;
759	    sel.innerHTML = "";
760	    const placeholder = document.createElement("option");
761	    placeholder.value = ""; placeholder.textContent = "(select port)";
762	    sel.appendChild(placeholder);
763	    for (const p of ports) {
764	      const opt = document.createElement("option");
765	      opt.value = p.device;
766	      opt.textContent = p.description ? `${p.device} — ${p.description}` : p.device;
767	      sel.appendChild(opt);
768	    }
769	    if (prev && ports.find((p) => p.device === prev)) sel.value = prev;
770	  } catch (e) {
771	    setBanner(`Could not list serial ports: ${e.message}`, "error");
772	  }
773	}

775	// ── Live: start / stop / WS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
776	
777	async function liveStart() {
778	  const port = $("#live-port").value;
779	  if (!port) { setBanner("Pick a serial port first.", "error"); return; }
780	  resetCaptureState();
781	  state.fsm = "live";
782	  state.liveStopRequested = false;
783	  state.reconnectAttempts = 0;
784	  setBanner("Starting…");
785	  try {
786	    await api("/api/live/start", {
787	      method: "POST",
788	      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
789	      body: JSON.stringify({ port }),
790	    });
791	  } catch (e) {
792	    setBanner(e.message, "error");
793	    state.fsm = "idle";
794	    return;
795	  }
796	  $("#live-start").disabled = true;
797	  $("#live-stop").disabled = false;
798	  $("#live-port").disabled = true;
799	  setBadge("badge-live", "yellow", "live …");
800	  openWS();
801	  // Push the initial mask the UI is showing (server defaults to ALL — keep
802	  // them in sync without making the user click anything).
803	  applyMaskFromCheckboxes({ immediate: true });
804	}
805	
806	async function liveStop() {
807	  state.liveStopRequested = true;
808	  closeWS({ userInitiated: true });
809	  try {
810	    await api("/api/live/stop", { method: "POST" });
811	  } catch (e) {
812	    setBanner(e.message, "error");
813	  }
814	  $("#live-start").disabled = false;
815	  $("#live-stop").disabled = true;
816	  $("#live-port").disabled = false;
817	  setBadge("badge-live", null, "live ●");
818	  state.fsm = "idle";
819	}
820	
821	function openWS() {
822	  const proto = location.protocol === "https:" ? "wss:" : "ws:";
823	  const ws = new WebSocket(`${proto}//${location.host}/api/live/ws`);
824	  state.ws = ws;
825	  ws.addEventListener("open", () => {
826	    state.reconnectAttempts = 0;
827	    setBadge("badge-live", "green", "live ●");
828	    setBanner("");
829	  });
830	  ws.addEventListener("message", (ev) => {
831	    let msg;
832	    try { msg = JSON.parse(ev.data); } catch { return; }
833	    handleWSMessage(msg);
834	  });
835	  ws.addEventListener("close", (ev) => {
836	    state.ws = null;
837	    if (state.liveStopRequested) {
838	      setBadge("badge-live", null, "live ●");
839	      return;
840	    }
841	    setBadge("badge-live", "yellow", `live ✗ ${ev.code}`);
842	    if (ev.code === 4409) {
843	      setBanner("Another client is using the live session.", "error");
844	      return;
845	    }
846	    scheduleReconnect();
847	  });
848	  ws.addEventListener("error", () => {
849	    // 'close' will follow; reconnect handled there.
850	  });
851	}
852	
853	function closeWS({ userInitiated }) {
854	  if (!state.ws) return;
855	  if (userInitiated) state.liveStopRequested = true;
856	  try { state.ws.close(); } catch {}
857	  state.ws = null;

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 22:45:25Z)**_

I see two real problems:

1. **Checkboxes feel "broken"** — the client trusts the device-side mask, but there's a serial round-trip (plus already-buffered records in flight) before the device actually stops sending the disabled type. Records keep arriving for ~hundreds of ms after a toggle. Plus there's a race in `liveStart()`: WS attaches before the initial set-mask reaches the server, so `hello` reports `0xffffffff` and clobbers the checkboxes back on.

2. **Stuttering after a while** — `renderTimeline` calls `Plotly.newPlot` which destroys+recreates the whole chart. At 50k records it takes hundreds of ms per tick. Should use `Plotly.react`. Also `LIVE_MAX_RECORDS=50_000` is way more than the 30s window needs.

Fix plan: add client-side mask filtering in `appendLiveRecord`, switch the live redraw to `Plotly.react`, drop the buffer cap, and order set-mask before WS open.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 22:47:11Z)**_

Four changes to [app.js](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/static/app.js):

1. **Client-side mask filter in [appendLiveRecord](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/static/app.js#L905)** — drops records of disabled types before they hit the buffer, so checkbox toggles take effect immediately instead of waiting for the device to ack the new filter (and for already-buffered serial frames to drain).

2. **State applied locally first in [applyMaskFromCheckboxes](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/static/app.js#L1018)** — `state.liveMask` and the displayed value update synchronously; the POST runs in the background. The server's "mask" echo then re-confirms the same value (no flicker).

3. **Order fix in [liveStart](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/static/app.js#L795)** — `await applyMaskFromCheckboxes({immediate: true})` *before* `openWS()`, so the WS hello reflects the user's mask instead of the server-default `0xffffffff` (which was clobbering the STRIP-off default back on).

4. **`Plotly.react` instead of `newPlot` for the live redraw** in [renderTimeline](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/static/app.js#L572) — reuses chart DOM instead of tearing it down each tick. Plus `LIVE_MAX_RECORDS` lowered from 50k → 10k as a safety net (the 30s window cap usually keeps it under that anyway).

Server-side queue drain on mask change is still in place. Try a hard refresh and run it again.

34	static uint16_t crc16_ccitt(uint16_t crc, uint8_t b)
35	{
36	    crc ^= (uint16_t)b << 8;
37	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < 8u; i++)
38	    {
39	        crc = (crc & 0x8000u) ? (uint16_t)((crc << 1) ^ 0x1021u)
40	                              : (uint16_t)(crc << 1);
41	    }
42	    return crc;
43	}
44	
45	static void reset(void)
46	{
47	    s_state       = RX_WAIT_SOF_0;
48	    s_len         = 0u;
49	    s_payload_idx = 0u;
50	    s_crc_calc    = 0xFFFFu;
51	    s_crc_rx      = 0u;
52	}
53	
54	static void drop_and_reset(void)
55	{
56	    s_drops++;
57	    reset();
58	}

60	/* Resync helper: if we're past WAIT_SOF_0 and the byte we just rejected
61	 * happens to be the first SOF byte of a fresh frame, give it credit
62	 * rather than waiting another full frame for the sync window. */
63	static void resync(uint8_t b)
64	{
65	    drop_and_reset();
66	    if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_0)
67	    {
68	        s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_1;
69	    }
70	}

72	static void dispatch_payload(void)
73	{
74	    if (s_len < sizeof(perf_cmd_hdr_t)) { return; }
75	
76	    perf_cmd_hdr_t hdr;
77	    memcpy(&hdr, s_payload, sizeof(hdr));
78	    if (hdr.magic != PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC) { return; }
79	
80	    switch (hdr.cmd_id)
81	    {
82	        case PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK:
83	            if (s_len == sizeof(perf_cmd_set_mask_t))
84	            {
85	                perf_cmd_set_mask_t cmd;
86	                memcpy(&cmd, s_payload, sizeof(cmd));
87	                PerfLog_SetEnabledMask(cmd.enabled_mask);
88	            }
89	            break;
90	
91	        default:
92	            break;
93	    }
94	}

102	void PerfLogRx_Feed(const uint8_t *bytes, uint32_t len)
103	{
104	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < len; i++)
105	    {
106	        uint8_t b = bytes[i];
107	        switch (s_state)
108	        {
109	            case RX_WAIT_SOF_0:
110	                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_0) { s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_1; }
111	                break;
112	
113	            case RX_WAIT_SOF_1:
114	                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_1) { s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_2; }
115	                else                     { resync(b); }
116	                break;
117	
118	            case RX_WAIT_SOF_2:
119	                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_2) { s_state = RX_WAIT_SOF_3; }
120	                else                     { resync(b); }
121	                break;
122	
123	            case RX_WAIT_SOF_3:
124	                if (b == PERF_LOG_SOF_3) { s_state = RX_READ_LEN_0; }
125	                else                     { resync(b); }
126	                break;
127	
128	            case RX_READ_LEN_0:
129	                s_len      = b;
130	                s_crc_calc = crc16_ccitt(s_crc_calc, b);
131	                s_state    = RX_READ_LEN_1;
132	                break;
133	
134	            case RX_READ_LEN_1:
135	                s_len     |= (uint16_t)b << 8;
136	                s_crc_calc = crc16_ccitt(s_crc_calc, b);
137	                if (s_len == 0u || s_len > PL_RX_PAYLOAD_MAX) { drop_and_reset(); }
138	                else                                          { s_state = RX_READ_PAYLOAD; }
139	                break;
140	
141	            case RX_READ_PAYLOAD:
142	                s_payload[s_payload_idx++] = b;
143	                s_crc_calc = crc16_ccitt(s_crc_calc, b);
144	                if (s_payload_idx >= s_len) { s_state = RX_READ_CRC_0; }
145	                break;
146	
147	            case RX_READ_CRC_0:
148	                s_crc_rx = b;
149	                s_state  = RX_READ_CRC_1;
150	                break;
151	
152	            case RX_READ_CRC_1:
153	                s_crc_rx |= (uint16_t)b << 8;
154	                if (s_crc_rx == s_crc_calc) { dispatch_payload(); reset(); }
155	                else                        { drop_and_reset(); }
156	                break;
157	
158	            default:
159	                drop_and_reset();
160	                break;
161	        }
162	    }
163	}

372	 * frame into the queue slot. Total pixel bytes (w*h*3) must fit the queue
373	 * slot's bgr[] capacity (PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES); per-axis shape is
374	 * unconstrained beyond that. Drop-on-full; counter incremented under
375	 * critical section. */
376	void PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(uint32_t frame_epoch,
377	                                perf_strip_kind_t kind,
378	                                const uint8_t *frame, uint32_t frame_stride,
379	                                uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
380	                                uint16_t w, uint16_t h)
381	{
382	    if (s_strip_q == NULL || frame == NULL) { return; }
383	    if (!type_enabled(PERF_REC_STRIP)) { return; }
384	    if (w == 0u || h == 0u) { return; }
385	    if ((uint32_t)w * (uint32_t)h * PERF_STRIP_BPP > PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES) { return; }
386	
387	    static perf_rec_strip_t r;     /* one staging slot; producer is single-task */
388	    memset(&r, 0, PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES);
389	    hdr_fill(&r.hdr, PERF_REC_STRIP, 0u, frame_epoch);
390	    r.x    = x;
391	    r.y    = y;
392	    r.w    = w;
393	    r.h    = h;
394	    r.kind = (uint8_t)kind;
395	
396	    const uint32_t row_bytes = (uint32_t)w * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
397	    const uint8_t *src = frame + (uint32_t)y * frame_stride + (uint32_t)x * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
398	    uint8_t *dst = r.bgr;
399	    for (uint16_t row = 0u; row < h; row++)
400	    {
401	        memcpy(dst, src, row_bytes);
402	        src += frame_stride;
403	        dst += row_bytes;
404	    }
405	
406	    if (xQueueSend(s_strip_q, &r, 0) != pdTRUE)
407	    {
408	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
409	    }
410	}

1	"""Byte sources feeding `framing.iter_frames`.
2	
3	Each source is an iterable of `bytes` chunks. Chunk size is not load-bearing —
4	the framer handles arbitrary boundaries.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
10	from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
11	from pathlib import Path
12	from typing import BinaryIO
13	
14	
15	# ─── File source ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
16	
17	
18	class FileSource(AbstractContextManager["FileSource"]):
19	    """Iterate over fixed-size chunks from a captured `.bin` file."""
20	
21	    def __init__(self, path: str | Path, chunk_bytes: int = 64 * 1024) -> None:
22	        self.path = Path(path)
23	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
24	        self._fh: BinaryIO | None = None
25	
26	    def __enter__(self) -> "FileSource":
27	        self._fh = self.path.open("rb")
28	        return self
29	
30	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
31	        if self._fh is not None:
32	            self._fh.close()
33	            self._fh = None
34	
35	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
36	        if self._fh is None:
37	            raise RuntimeError("FileSource must be used as a context manager")
38	        while True:
39	            chunk = self._fh.read(self.chunk_bytes)
40	            if not chunk:
41	                return
42	            yield chunk
43	
44	
45	# ─── Serial source ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
46	
47	
48	class SerialSource(AbstractContextManager["SerialSource"]):
49	    """Read bytes from the marvin USB-device CDC ACM port via pyserial.
50	
51	    The firmware sink is DTR-gated (`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:216`); pyserial raises
52	    DTR by default on open, which triggers the firmware to re-emit a SESSION
53	    record. CDC ACM ignores baud rate; we still pass one because pyserial
54	    requires it.
55	    """
56	
57	    def __init__(
58	        self,
59	        port: str,
60	        *,
61	        baudrate: int = 921600,
62	        chunk_bytes: int = 4096,
63	        read_timeout_s: float = 0.1,
64	    ) -> None:
65	        self.port = port
66	        self.baudrate = baudrate
67	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
68	        self.read_timeout_s = read_timeout_s
69	        self._ser: object | None = None
70	
71	    def __enter__(self) -> "SerialSource":
72	        # Imported lazily so file-only workflows do not require pyserial.
73	        import serial  # noqa: WPS433  (intentional lazy import)
74	
75	        self._ser = serial.Serial(
76	            port=self.port,
77	            baudrate=self.baudrate,
78	            timeout=self.read_timeout_s,
79	            dsrdtr=False,
80	        )
81	        # Make DTR explicit — some platforms default it off.
82	        try:
83	            self._ser.dtr = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
84	        except (OSError, AttributeError):
85	            pass

```text
commit 424a48e9329331099141ad314b4e3ebe074e8154
Author: Greg Mrozek <greg.mrozek@microchip.com>
Date:   Fri May 22 17:12:18 2026 -0500

    perf-log: host→device record-type mask over CDC
    
    Adds bidirectional control on the perf-log channel — host sends a per-
    record-type enable mask via the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer the device uses
    for records, with a distinct command magic ('MC' = 0x4D43 vs records'
    'MV' = 0x4D56) so misrouted bytes can't be parsed in the wrong direction.
    Default is all-on (parity with prior behavior); SESSION is always emitted
    regardless so the host gets timer_freq_hz on attach.
    
    Motivation: 1.88 MB/s STRIP-dominated traffic was starving the shared
    state queue, dropping ~707 HWM/RUNTIME records per second. Cutting record
    types at the source is cleaner than enlarging queues that shouldn't be
    full to begin with.
    
    Firmware:
    - perf_log_rx.{c,h}: small SOF-resync state machine fed from the CDC
      sink's READ_COMPLETE handler; valid SET_TYPE_MASK frames update
      s_enabled_mask (volatile u32, lock-free single-load on Cortex-A)
    - perf_log.c: mask checked at three early-return points (send_state,
      EmitStripFromFrame, EmitStampFromISR)
    - sink_cdc: 64-byte bulk-OUT staging buffer; primes a read on
      EVENT_DEVICE_CONFIGURED and re-primes after each completion
    
    Host:
    - frame_encode in framing.py: mirror of the device framer (SOF + LEN +
      payload + CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE)
```

Replace with the `csi_phy_hs_rx_init(lane_code, bit_rate)` helper and call it for lanes 0/1/2/3 from a flat `if (nlanes >= …)` chain.

99-  2. **`plib_xlcdc.c` `XLCDC_EnableClocks` — `PMC_PLL_ACR`.** Set to datasheet-optimal `0x12023010` for the LVDSPLL with our 24 MHz reference (in the `fIN ∈ [20 MHz, 32 MHz]` band). Specifically: `LOOP_FILTER=0x12, LOCK_THR=0x2, UTMIBG=1, UTMIVR=1, CONTROL=0x10`. MCC's default emits a different (less-optimal) analog config (`LOOP_FILTER=0x1B, LOCK_THR=0x4, no UTMI bits`). Doesn't affect functional behavior in our use (50 Hz refresh works either way), but is the manufacturer-recommended jitter/lock optimum.
100-
--
147-
148:**Mask checkboxes.** SESSION is pinned-on (firmware always emits it; checkbox disabled). Any change debounces 200 ms then `POST /api/live/set-mask` with the integer mask; server reply updates the displayed `0x…` value. ALL / MIN preset buttons map to `0xFFFFFFFF` and `(SESSION|DROP)` respectively. The very first start fires an immediate set-mask so server and UI start synchronized.
149-
150-**Strip render.** `paintBgrIntoCanvas(canvas, b64, w, h)` decodes base64 → BGR-byte string → `ImageData` (RGBA via per-pixel byte swap) → `putImageData`. First STRIP record of a new kind triggers `indexByKind() + renderStripSlots()` so the canvas exists before paint; subsequent strips paint directly. Offline strip path still uses the PNG endpoint — `updateStripsAtPlayhead` prefers `rec.bgr_b64` when present, falls through to PNG otherwise.
151-
--
157-
158:Backend half of "make the browser the iteration surface." Single-tenant live session: one serial reader thread, one open `SerialSource`, one WebSocket peer at a time (a second WS gets close code 4409 with reason `"live already in use"`). REST for control (`/api/live/{start,stop,set-mask,status}`, `/api/serial/ports`), WS for the data stream (`/api/live/ws`); browser sends nothing over WS. No frontend changes yet — frontend live mode + record-types panel is Phase 2; recording start/stop is Phase 3.
159-
160-**Module shape.** New [`web/live.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py) owns a mutex-guarded `_LiveSession` singleton. Reader thread runs `iter_frames(SerialSource, stats) → decode_record(frame.payload) → _record_to_dict(rec, include_bgr=True)` and posts onto a per-WS-attach `asyncio.Queue` via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`. Disconnects in either direction flow through the same shutdown path that joins the thread and closes the port. `_record_to_dict` is late-bound from `api.py` to avoid the import cycle.
161-
--

170:### 2026-05-22 — perf-log host→device record-type masking
171-
172-Bidirectional control on the perf-log channel. Host can now narrow which record types the device emits per-capture without rebuilding firmware. Default is all-on (parity with prior behavior); host sends a `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK` over the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer that's used for records, with a distinct command magic (`0x4D43` 'MC' vs records' `0x4D56` 'MV') so misrouted bytes can't be parsed in the wrong direction.

CLI `live` and `record` get `--types STAMP,SESSION,DROP,…` (special tokens `ALL`, `MIN`); new `set-mask` subcommand pokes a running capture from another terminal. 9 new tests; 83/83 passing.

178-**Why now.** The 1.88 MB/s STRIP-dominated load was masking HWM/RUNTIME records (state-queue starvation, ~707 dropped/s — see prior entry). Cutting record types at the source is a cleaner fix than enlarging queues we don't actually want full. With STRIP off, expected sink load drops to ~25 KB/s, and the state queue should drain freely.

Three-way check next time you run it:

1. Toggle a checkbox.
2. **Server console** should show `[live] set-mask 0xXX → wrote 16 B: aa55…`. If yes, the host wrote the bytes.
3. **Firmware UART** should show `PerfLog: mask=0xXX` matching what the server printed. If yes, the device parsed the frame and updated the filter.

The journal flagged this code as "Verification pending hardware" — it may never have round-tripped end-to-end. A few suspects in priority order:

- **Firmware not rebuilt since [424a48e](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_rx.c)** — if the running image predates that commit, the device has no RX framer and silently ignores incoming bytes.
- **CDC RX endpoint never primed** — `prime_rx_read()` runs on `USB_DEVICE_EVENT_CONFIGURED`. If macOS pyserial's open doesn't trigger a re-config event, and the device was already configured before you started the server, the read is primed once at boot and that's it. Should still work, but worth double-checking the firmware UART for the initial `PERF: USB device CDC configured` line.
- **CRC mismatch on device side** — `PerfLogRx_GetDropCount()` would show this; unfortunately we don't expose it on the wire.

Run a session with the firmware UART tail open and tell me what you see in each log when toggling.

PC side is **perfect**. Frame decodes byte-for-byte:

```
55 4d 52 56                  SOF "UMRV"
08 00                        LEN = 8
43 4d                        magic 0x4D43 "MC"
01                           cmd_id = PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK
00                           reserved
9e 01 00 00                  mask = 0x0000019e  ✓ matches header
64 b4                        CRC-16
```

16 bytes, well-formed, matches the firmware framer's expectations exactly.

So the issue is on the device side, downstream of the USB-CDC bulk-OUT endpoint. Three things to check on the firmware UART:

1. Do you see `PERF: USB device CDC configured` once at startup? If not, the RX endpoint was never primed.
2. Do you see `PerfLog: mask=0x0000019e` when you toggle the checkbox? If yes — the device received and applied it, and we have a *different* bug (records-in-flight, or a producer that ignores the mask). If no — the bytes never reached the framer (or the framer rejected them).
3. Is the running firmware image built from a commit at or after `424a48e`? `git log --oneline 424a48e..HEAD -- firmware/marvin/` shows what's been added since, but the test is whether the .elf you flashed actually contains `perf_log_rx.c`.

Tell me what the UART shows.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 22:59:20Z)**_

Bytes leave the host fine, the device sees enumeration, but the framer never sees the bytes. Most common cause on Cortex-A7 with caches on: the RX DMA buffer isn't being cache-invalidated before the CPU reads it. TX works because the driver flushes the cache before DMA-out; RX is the symmetric case that often gets missed.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - perf-log v2 wire format: SOF "UMRV" (0x55, 0x4D, 0x52, 0x56) + LEN(u16 LE) + PAYLOAD + CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE(u16 LE)
   - PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC=0x4D43 ('MC') for host→device commands; PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC=0x4D56 ('MV') for records
   - PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK = 0x01: `<HBBI` = magic, cmd_id, reserved, mask
   - RecordType enum: SESSION=1, STAMP=2, DETECTOR=3, TIMING=4, STRIP=5, DROP=6, TASK_HIGHWATER=7, TASK_RUNTIME=8
   - Single-tenant live session: serial reader thread + asyncio.Queue + WS push
   - Sliding-window in-browser buffer (30s by ts_counter, 10k records cap after this session)
   - Plotly.react vs Plotly.newPlot — react reuses chart DOM; cheaper for live redraws
   - SAM9X75 = Cortex-A7 with UDPHS (USB Device High Speed) peripheral
   - HS bulk-OUT max packet size = 512 bytes; FS = 64 bytes
   - Cache coherency on Cortex-A7: DMA buffers need explicit invalidate/clean operations
   - Harmony USB driver does `SYS_CACHE_InvalidateDCache_by_Addr` and `SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr`

206	{
207	    s_write_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_write_done_buf);
208	    configASSERT(s_write_done != NULL);

210	    PerfLogRx_Initialize();
211	
212	    /* Open may fail until USB_DEVICE_Initialize finishes its own first
213	     * task tick — retry until success. Drain task is alive at this
214	     * point so vTaskDelay is fine. */
215	    while (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
216	    {
217	        s_dev_handle = USB_DEVICE_Open(USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0,
218	                                       DRV_IO_INTENT_READWRITE);
219	        if (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
220	        {

222	        }
223	    }

227	    /* Cold-boot-with-cable case: by the time we register the handler the
228	     * UDPHS driver may have already raced past the VBUS edge it needed
229	     * to fire POWER_DETECTED, or the host may have seen a brief pull-up
230	     * assertion during early boot and given up retrying. Force a clean
231	     * detach→short delay→attach edge so the host sees an unambiguous
232	     * device-arrival on the bus. Hot-plug after this point is unaffected
233	     * because POWER_REMOVED/POWER_DETECTED still drive Detach/Attach. */
234	    (void)USB_DEVICE_Detach(s_dev_handle);
235	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100));

Looking at [perf_log_sink_cdc.c:58-68](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L58-L68):

```c
/* RX staging — one bulk-OUT max-packet (64 B at high speed). Cache-
 * aligned for the same reason as s_tx_frame. */
#define SINK_RX_BUF_BYTES  64u
static uint8_t CACHE_ALIGN s_rx_buf[SINK_RX_BUF_BYTES];

static void prime_rx_read(void)
{
    USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
    (void)USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0, &th,
                              s_rx_buf, SINK_RX_BUF_BYTES);
}
```

The comment is wrong: HS bulk-OUT MPS is **512** (per the device descriptor at [usb_device_init_data.c:209-210](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/usb_device_init_data.c#L209-L210), which sets EP2-OUT wMaxPacketSize to `0x0200`). 64 is the FS value.

The UDPHS driver enforces this — see [drv_usb_udphs_device.c:1958](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_device.c#L1958), which checks `(nPendingBytes + byteCount) > irp->size` and warns about corrupting RAM. With an undersized IRP buffer, the driver either rejects the read submission or refuses to copy the packet — the `(void)` cast on `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` hides any error return code.

Our 16-byte SET_MASK frame is well under 512, but the IRP buffer has to be sized to the endpoint's max packet, not to the data we expect to receive. The driver allocates DMA descriptors based on IRP size, so anything < MPS likely means the read never completes (or one max-packet boundary in, depending on how the controller signals short).

Proposed one-line fix:

 ## Session log
 
+### 2026-05-22 — marvin-perf web viewer: live-mode frontend (Phase 2 of 3)
+
+Frontend half of "browser is the iteration surface." Single-page app gains a Mode toggle (Offline/Live), port `<select>`, Start/Stop buttons, mask display, and an 8-checkbox types panel with ALL/MIN presets. Records stream over the WS into a sliding-window buffer (last 30 s, hard-capped at 50 k). STRIP records render client-side from the `bgr_b64` payload — no server PNG round-trip. The existing offline path is unchanged: every offline route + UI element still works as before; the mode toggle is the boundary.
+
+**State machine.** Added `state.fsm = "live"` and `state.mode = "live" | "offline"`. Live disables transport (prev/next/play-pause/speed) — playhead is always "now". Crossing the mode boundary calls `resetCaptureState()` to clear the previous mode's records, panels, and Plotly charts so leftover state can't bleed across.
+
+**Sliding window.** Each WS record append calls `pruneLiveBuffer()` which drops anything older than the newest record's `ts_counter` minus `LIVE_BUFFER_SECONDS * timer_freq_hz`, then enforces `LIVE_MAX_RECORDS`. `state.ts0` re-pins to the oldest survivor so timeline x-axis stays sensible as the window slides. Plotly redraw is debounced 250 ms; the playhead text + strip canvas update inline so per-frame visuals stay smooth.
+
+**Mask checkboxes.** SESSION is pinned-on (firmware always emits it; checkbox disabled). Any change debounces 200 ms then `POST /api/live/set-mask` with the integer mask; server reply updates the displayed `0x…` value. ALL / MIN preset buttons map to `0xFFFFFFFF` and `(SESSION|DROP)` respectively. The very first start fires an immediate set-mask so server and UI start synchronized.
+
+**Strip render.** `paintBgrIntoCanvas(canvas, b64, w, h)` decodes base64 → BGR-byte string → `ImageData` (RGBA via per-pixel byte swap) → `putImageData`. First STRIP record of a new kind triggers `indexByKind() + renderStripSlots()` so the canvas exists before paint; subsequent strips paint directly. Offline strip path still uses the PNG endpoint — `updateStripsAtPlayhead` prefers `rec.bgr_b64` when present, falls through to PNG otherwise.
+
+**WS lifecycle.** Open on Live-Start (after `/api/live/start` returns OK), close on Live-Stop. Auto-reconnect on unexpected close: 1 s × attempt-count, capped at 5 s. Server's `session_replay` on reconnect re-binds `timer_freq_hz`. Close code 4409 ("already in use") surfaces as a banner without retry. On page reload mid-session, `probeLiveSession()` sees the active session via `/api/live/status` and re-attaches the WS — no manual restart.
+
+**Out of scope this commit:** recording start/stop UI + backend (Phase 3), debounced timeline patching via `Plotly.extendTraces` (current full-replot is fine at the 250 ms cadence), and a "drops since session" live counter.
+
 ### 2026-05-22 — marvin-perf web viewer: live-mode backend (Phase 1 of 3)
 
 Backend half of "make the browser the iteration surface." Single-tenant live session: one serial reader thread, one open `SerialSource`, one WebSocket peer at a time (a second WS gets close code 4409 with reason `"live already in use"`). REST for control (`/api/live/{start,stop,set-mask,status}`, `/api/serial/ports`), WS for the data stream (`/api/live/ws`); browser sends nothing over WS. No frontend changes yet — frontend live mode + record-types panel is Phase 2; recording start/stop is Phase 3.

134	- **`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS` likely needs to vary by difficulty.** 220 ms tuned well on Expert (notes are dense, the delay lines up against fast-moving notes near the strike line). Easy/Medium/Hard place notes higher up the highway with longer travel time, so the same 220 ms may strike too early. Open: per-difficulty preset, runtime-tunable from the manual-control surface, or auto-tuned from observed note-velocity.
